of this chapter). Such an employee has 
permanent tenure as a classified civil 
service appointee in the agency in which 
employed unless he was reappointed 
with a time limitation of one year or 
less.
Any transfer or reappointment of an 
employee who was originally appointed 
“subject to investigation” will be subject 
to the results of the investigation.
Any transfer or reappointment of an 
employee who has been recommended 
for classification in his former position, 
and whose suitability for classification 
was under investigation, shall be subject 
to the results of such investigation.

person, except one who was holding a 
temporary position, who was transferred 
by the Commission with reemployment

9067 (3 CFR, Cum. Supp., p. 1093) or

No. 10, and who is subsequently involun­
tarily furloughed or separated without 
cause as would reflect upon his suita­

shall be entitled to the rights specified 
below, provided he is still qualified to 
perform the duties of his position and 
that he makes application for reem-

tion then exists, that is not held by a

§  4.1 Prohibition against political ac­
tivity. Persons in the executive branch 
shall retain the right to vote as they 
choose and to express their opinions on 
all political subjects and candidates, but 
such persons shall not use their official 
authority or influence for the purpose 
of interfering with an election or affect­

management or in political campaigns 
except as may be provided by or pur­
suant to statute.

research_rationale:
EO 9301 (February 9, 1943, Franklin D. Roosevelt; 8 FR 1825, issue of Thursday, February 11, 1943), read in full in the held Federal Register text, declares that "For the duration of the war" no plant or place of employment is deemed to make the most effective use of manpower if its minimum workweek is under 48 hours (section 1, inside the lead row of the machine inventory), directs agencies to require contractors to comply (2), authorizes the Chairman of the War Manpower Commission to interpret the order and issue policies, directives and regulations and to set a different workweek in particular cases (3), requires agencies to comply (4) and states that the order is not to supersede other hours or wage laws (5). EO 9607 (August 30, 1945), held Federal Register text, revokes it by number in one sentence. The phrase "For the duration of the war" is an own-terms condition; no held instrument or source fixes a legal end of the war before August 30, 1945, and EO 9607 revokes the order outright without reciting that it had lapsed, so the first end is the express revocation.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end is held. Own terms: section 1 begins \"For the duration of the war\", which ends on a legal event that no held source places before August 30, 1945 (the formal proclamation of the war's end is not held), so it is a disclosed candidate that cannot be dated and not an end. A later general rule is not shown to have ended any command. Searches of the held corpus for \"Executive Order 9301\" and for the minimum-workweek wording found EO 9607 (the revocation) and EO 9332 (Solid Fuels Administration), which cites EO 9301 in a list of orders and does not revoke or amend it. The contents table of the held Federal Register issue of August 21, 1945 (10 FR page 10166) lists a rescission of the War Manpower Commission's regulations on the minimum wartime workweek; that page is not held, so the rescission's date and text cannot be read. It would concern regulations issued under section 3, not the order, and it does not name EO 9301's revocation, so it is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end.","independent_command_check":"Section 3 gives the Chairman of the War Manpower Commission authority to issue regulations and set a different workweek; it is a delegation inside the order and ends with it. Section 5 is a rule of construction protecting other laws and agreements and has no force once the order is revoked. No other independent command is found.","savings_check":"EO 9607 consists of the revocation sentence and no saving, exception or transition wording. Obligations that contractors incurred under contracts made while EO 9301 and the War Manpower Commission's regulations were in force arise from those contracts and the regulations, not from a continuing command of the order, and no held source shows any continuing effect; that is a disclosed qualification, not a finding.","scope_check":"The inventory is five rows: the lead (authority recital and section 1) and sections 2 to 5. All rows end together on the revocation of the whole order; no row was amended or ended separately before then."}

Obligations that contractors incurred under contracts made while EO 9301 and the War Manpower Commission's regulations were in force arise from those contracts and the regulations, not from a continuing command of the order, and no held source shows any continuing effect; that is a disclosed qualification, not a finding.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 12553, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, official Federal Register text held), orders that the listed Executive Orders, "and any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its number column lists 9702 (the held American Presidency Project transcription pairs 9702 with the subject 'Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute'). The wording has no effective-date clause, so the recorded date is the signing date 1986-02-25 (printed March 3, 1986, the alternative reading). Disclosed note: the order was functionally spent earlier, when the board reported and the standstill ran out; the report date is not held.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 9702
Creating an Emergency Board to Investi ­
gate a D ispute  B etween  T he A lton 
Railroad Company and Other Carriers, 
and C ertain of T heir E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
The Alton Railroad Company and other  
carriers, as set forth in the list attached  
hereto and made a part hereof, and cer­
tain of their employees represented by  
the Brotherhood o’ f Locomotive Engi­
neers and the Brotherhood of Railroad  
Trainmen, labor organizations; and  
WHEREAS the dispute has not hereto­
fore been adjusted under the provisions  
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  
and
"V ^H E R E A S the dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to  
deprive the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate said dispute. No member of  
the said board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization  
of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said dis­
pute within thirty days from the date of  
this order.
As provide^ by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by The Alton Railroad Company  
and the other carriers, or their employees 
in the condition out of which the said  
dispute arose.

Identity and text: read in full in the registered Federal Register original (11 FR, issue of 1946-03-12; grade original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original true). Order 9702 of March 8, 1946 creates an emergency board of three members under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute between the Alton Railroad Company and other carriers and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, directs a report within thirty days of the order, and recites the statutory no-change period of thirty days after the report. Inventory: one sole paragraph. End: EO 12553, signed February 25, 1986, orders, in the official Federal Register text (51 FR 7237, held), that the listed Executive Orders, "and any amendments thereto, are revoked:", and its number column lists 9702; the held American Presidency Project transcription (corroboration only, not cited as evidence) pairs 9702 with the subject 'Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute'. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadlines) the report date and the end of the standstill are spent facts, not ends; the order ends on the express revocation. No held source records when the board reported; if it reported by its deadline of April 7, 1946, the standstill ended by May 7, 1946. Functionally spent no later than 1946-05-07 on that assumption, which is not established by a held source.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The thirty-day report direction and the thirty-day no-change period are a deadline and a standstill that depend on the actual report date; neither is an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 report-deadline). The dossier chain is empty; the only later instrument naming the order is EO 12553. Search coverage: the later-events catalogue (OFR disposition notes from 1937) and the held order texts; Public Land Orders and Civil Service Commission notices printed in issues without an executive order are not searched.","independent_command_check":"The statutory no-change period is a Railway Labor Act section 10 consequence that the order recites; it ran by statute and is not an independent executive command.","savings_check":"See savings reason.","scope_check":"One clause. EO 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. In the held text of Executive Order 12553 the number 9918 appears in the number column of the first table page, and the aligned entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) describes an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes in the plural, matching this order's title. This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Alabama, Tennessee and Northern Railroad Company and other carriers named in List A and certain of their employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of December 31, 1947 (due by January 30, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

WHEREAS disputes exist between the 
Alabama, Tennessee and Northern Rail­
road Company and certain other car­
riers designated in list A attached hereto 
and made a part hereof, and certain of 
their employees represented by the 
seventeen cooperating nonoperating la­
bor organizations’ designated in list B 
attached hereto and made a part hereof; 
and
WHEREAS these disputes have not 
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the 
judgment of the National Mediation 
Board, threaten substantially to inter­
rupt interstate commerce to a -degree 
such as to deprive the country of essen­
tial transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I  hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said disputes.
Each of the carriers involved shall be 
given independent consideration in such 
investigation, and the said labor organi­
zations shall be permitted to function
FEDERAL REGISTER
as a unit in proceedings before the 
board.
No member of the said board shall be 
pecuniarily or otherwise interested in 
any organization of railway employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
disputes within thirty days from the 
date of this order. The report of the 
board shall contain separate and inde­
pendent findings with respect to each of 
the carriers involved.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by any of the carriers involved or 
their employees in the conditions out of 
which the said disputes arose.

Identity: the held Federal Register text is the order itself (heading and body read in full; signed December 31, 1947). Inventory read and confirmed (correction only where stated). End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25 under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadline option C): a report deadline and an expired standstill are not ends. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete with no coverage warning.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (January 30, 1948, thirty days after signing on December 31, 1947) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); that statute is an independent source of duty and is untouched by the revocation, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows them still running.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full and contains no saving clause. The residual consequences of the order (the board's investigation and report, any settlement of the dispute) are not shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (recitals, creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). Signature, date line and the attached List A and List B identify the parties and contain no separate command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the full held text of Executive Order 12553, because no acting-provision record for this order is in the packet."}

WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Chicago, North ^Shore &  Milwaukee 
Railway Company, a carrier, and certain  
of its employees represented by the Inter­
national Union of Amalgamated Asso­
ciation of Street Electric Railway and  
Motor Coach Employees of America, a  
labor organization; and  
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce within The States of  
Illinois and Wisconsin to a degree such  
as to deprive those States of essential  
transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate the said dispute. No  
member of the said board shall be pe­
cuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railway employees or any  
carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said  
dispute within thirty days from the date  
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Chicago, North Shore &  Mil­
waukee Railway Company or its em­
ployees in the conditions out of which the  
said dispute arose.

In the held text of Executive Order 12553 the number 9923 appears in the number column of the first table page, and the aligned entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, matching this order's title. This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of January 13, 1948 (due by February 12, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text is the order itself (heading and body read in full; signed January 13, 1948). Inventory read and confirmed (correction only where stated). End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25 under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadline option C): a report deadline and an expired standstill are not ends. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete with no coverage warning.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (February 12, 1948, thirty days after signing on January 13, 1948) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); that statute is an independent source of duty and is untouched by the revocation, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows them still running.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full and contains no saving clause. The residual consequences of the order (the board's investigation and report, any settlement of the dispute) are not shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (recitals, creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). Signature, date line and any attached list identify the parties and contain no separate command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence of Executive Order 12553."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. In the held text of Executive Order 12553 the number 9929 appears in the number column of the first table page, and the aligned entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, matching this order's title. This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Akron, Canton & Youngstown Railroad Company and other carriers named in the attached list and certain of their employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of January 27, 1948 (due by February 26, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

UNITED STATES STANDARDS FOR FRESH 
SPINACH LEAVES
On December 27, 1947, notice of pro­
posed rule making was published in the 
F ederal  R egister  (12 F . R . 8843) regard­
ing the proposed issuance of United 
States Consumer Standards for Fresh 
Spinach Leaves. After consideration of 
all relevant matters presented, including 
the proposals set forth in the aforesaid 
notice, the following United States Con­
sumer Standards for Fresh Spinach 
Leaves are hereby promulgated pursuant 
to the provisions of the Department of 
Agriculture Appropriation Act, 1948 
(Pub. Law 266, 80th Cong., 1st Sess., ap­
proved Jifty 30, 1947) :
§  51.394 Consumer standards for fresh  
spinach leaves —(a) Grades. (1) U. S. 
Grade A shall consist of spinach leaves 
of similar varietal characteristics which 
are fresh, clean, well trimmed., and of 
reasonably good green color, and which 
are free from coarse stalks, seedstems, 
seedbuds, crowns and roots, sandburs or 
other kinds of burs, soft rot and from 
damage caused by clusters of leaves, leaf 
stems without blades, discoloration, 
freezing, foreign material, disease, in­
sects, mechanical or other means. Spin­
ach on the shown face shall be reasonably 
representative in size and quality of the 
contents of the container.
RULES AND REGULATIONS
(1) Incident to proper grading and 
handling not more than 7 percent, by 
weight, of the spinach in any lot may be 
small pieces of leaves, not more than 3 
percent of the spinach leaves may be 
damaged by clusters, and not more than
3 percent may fail to meet the remaining 
requirements of the grade, including not 
more than 1 percent for serious damage: 
Provided, That no tolerance shall be per­
mitted for sandburs or other kinds of 
burs.
(2) U. S. Grade B shall consist of spin­
ach leaves which meet the requirements 
for U. S. Grade A, except that they shall 
be reasonably clean, and except for the 
increased tolerances for defects specified 
below.
(1) Incident to proper grading and 
handlings not more than 15 percent, by 
weightr of the spinach in any lot may be 
small pieces, not more than 5 percent of 
the spinach leaves may be damaged by 
clusters, and not more than 5 percent 
may fail to meet the remaining require­
ments of the grade, including not more 
than 2 percent for serious damage: 
Provided, That no tolerance shall be per­
mitted for sandburs or other kinds of 
burs.
(b) Off-Grade spinach leaves. Spinach 
leaves which fail to meet the require­
ments of either of the foregoing grades 
shall be Off-Grade spinach leaves.
(c) Definitions. (1) “Similar varietal 
characteristics 0 means that the spinach 
leaves shall be generally of one type, as 
crinkly leaf type, or flat leaf type. No 
mixture of varieties shall be permitted 
which materially affects the appearance 
.  of the lot.
(2) “Fresh” means that the leaves are 
not more than slightly wilted.
(3) “Clean” means that the spinach 
does not show more than a trace of grit, 
sand, dirt, silt, muck or other similar 
water insoluble, inorganic material.
(4) “Well trimmed” means that the 
leaf stems or petioles are not excessively 
long in relation to the size of the leaf 
blades.
(5) “Damage” means any injury or 
defect which materially affects the ap­
pearance, or the edible, shipping or keep­
ing- quality of the individual leaves or of 
the lot as a whole. The following defects 
or any combination of defects the seri­
ousness of which exceeds the amount al­
lowed for any one defect shall be consid­
ered as damage:
4 (i) Clusters, when there are more 
than 3 leaves attached, except that clus­
ters of heart leaves with any number of 
leaves shall not be considered as dam­
aged, provided the length of the longest 
leaf in the cluster is not over 3 inches.
(ii) Leaf stems without blades at­
tached when present to such an extent 
as to materially affect the appearance of 
the lot, or when the individual stem is 
damaged.
(iii) Discoloration, when the appear­
ance of the leaf is materially affected. 
Heart leaves which are yellow or par­
tially blanched shall not be considered 
as damaged by discoloration.
(iv) Mechanical damage, when the 
leaf is very badly crushed, torn, or 
broken. (Owing to the many necessary 
handlings in the harvesting, icing, ship­
ping, sorting, washing, and packing op­
erations In preparing spinach for con­
sumer use some leaves are crushed, torn 
or broken but only those leaves which 
are very badly crushed, torn or broken 
shall be considered as damaged by 
mechanical means.)
(6) “Serious damage” means any in­
jury or defect whjch seriously affects the 
appearance, or the edible, shipping or 
keeping quality of the individual leaves 
or of the lot as a whole. The following 
defects shall be considered as serious 
damage:
(1) Badly discolored leaves.
(ii) Leaves severely affected by mildew 
or white rust.
(iii) Leaves on which insects are pres­
ent, or leaves which are seriously dam­
aged by insects.
(iv) Leaves which are affected by soft 
rot.
(v) Weeds, grass or pieces thereof, 
and other extraneous matter.
(7) “Reasonably clean” means that 
the spinach is reasonably free from grit, 
sand, dirt, silt, muck or other similar 
water insoluble, inorganic material.
(d) Effective time.  The United States 
Consumer Standards for Fresh Spinach 
Leaves contained in this section shall be­
come effective thirty (30) days after the 
date of publication of these standards in 
the F ederal  R egister .
(Pub. Law 266, 80th Cong., 11 F. R. 7713)

day of January 1948.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. In the held text of Executive Order 12553 the number 9936 appears in the number column of the first table page, and the aligned entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, matching this order's title. This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Terminal Railroad Association of St. Louis and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of March 18, 1948 (due by April 17, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

Identity: the held Federal Register text is the order itself (heading and body read in full; signed March 18, 1948). Inventory read and confirmed (correction only where stated). End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25 under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadline option C): a report deadline and an expired standstill are not ends. Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (April 17, 1948, thirty days after signing on March 18, 1948) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. In the held text of Executive Order 12553 the number 9940 appears in the number column of the first table page, and the aligned entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, matching this order's title. This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Railway Express Agency, Inc., and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of March 25, 1948 (due by April 24, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

Identity: the held Federal Register text is the order itself (heading and body read in full; signed March 25, 1948). Inventory read and confirmed (correction only where stated). End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25 under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadline option C): a report deadline and an expired standstill are not ends. Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (April 24, 1948, thirty days after signing on March 25, 1948) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); that statute is an independent source of duty and is untouched by the revocation, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows them still running.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full and contains no saving clause. The residual consequences of the order (the board's investigation and report, any settlement of the dispute) are not shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (recitals, creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). Signature, date line and any attached list identify the parties and contain no separate command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the full held text of Executive Order 12553, because no acting-provision record for this order is in the packet."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 9948 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Aliquippa and Southern Railroad Company and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of April 10, 1948 (due by May 10, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

Creating an E mergency  B oard to I nvesti ­
gate a D ispute  B etw een The A liquippa  
and S outhern  R ailroad C ompany  and 
Certain of I ts E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Aliquippa and Southern Railroad 
Company, a carrier, and certain of its 
employees represented by the Brother­
hood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor or­
ganization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not hereto­
fore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce within the State of 
Pennsylvania to a degree such as to de­
prive that portion of the country of es­
sential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in' any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said dis­
pute within thirty days from the date of 
this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Aliquippa and Southern 
Railroad Company or its employees in 
the conditions out of which the said dis­
pute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text is the order itself (heading and body read in full; signed April 10, 1948). Inventory read and confirmed (correction only where stated). End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25 under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadline option C): a report deadline and an expired standstill are not ends. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete with no coverage warning.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (May 10, 1948, thirty days after signing on April 10, 1948) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); that statute is an independent source of duty and is untouched by the revocation, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows them still running.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full and contains no saving clause. The residual consequences of the order (the board's investigation and report, any settlement of the dispute) are not shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (recitals, creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). Signature, date line and any attached list identify the parties and contain no separate command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the full held text of Executive Order 12553, because no acting-provision record for this order is in the packet."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 9991 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Pittsburgh & West Virginia Railway Company and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of August 26, 1948 (due by September 25, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

Creating an E mergency B oard T o I nves ­

burgh &  West V irginia R ailway C om­
pany  and C ertain of its E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Pittsburgh &  West Virginia Railway 
Company, a carrier, and certain of its  
employees represented by the Brother­
hood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor or­
ganization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions  
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce within the States of  
Ohio and Pennsylvania to a degree such  
as* to deprive those states of essential  
transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U. S. C. ICO), I hereby create a board  
of three members,%to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily  
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said  
dispute within thirty days from the date  
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Pittsburgh &  West Virginia 
Railway Company or its employees in the  
conditions out of which the said dispute  
arose.

Identity: the held Federal Register text is the order itself (heading and body read in full; signed August 26, 1948). Inventory read and confirmed (correction only where stated). End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25 under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadline option C): a report deadline and an expired standstill are not ends. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete with no coverage warning.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (September 25, 1948, thirty days after signing on August 26, 1948) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); that statute is an independent source of duty and is untouched by the revocation, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows them still running.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full and contains no saving clause. The residual consequences of the order (the board's investigation and report, any settlement of the dispute) are not shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (recitals, creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). Signature, date line and any attached list identify the parties and contain no separate command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the full held text of Executive Order 12553, because no acting-provision record for this order is in the packet."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10010 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". This order created a board of three members to investigate the disputes between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company and other carriers named in List A and employees represented by the sixteen cooperating railway labor organizations named in List B; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in an organization of railway employees or in a carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by November 17, 1948); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred the carriers involved and their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the board's own report (a text of PDF pages 1-8 of 70 from the National Mediation Board site, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) carries the date December 17, 1948 on its title page and states that the parties stipulated on the record to extend the time for the board to submit its report to the President until December 17; thirty days after December 17, 1948 is January 16, 1949. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end. Executive Order 10015, signed November 5, 1948 and published at 13 FR 6601 in the Federal Register of November 9, 1948, amended this order effective as of October 18, 1948, the date its own text states: it adds six named carriers to List A and gives new designations to two organizations named in List B, so that after the amendment List A includes those six carriers and the two organizations carry the new designations. It does not change the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report requirement or the standstill, and it does not revoke or supersede this order; it is therefore a later amendment and not an end, and it is recorded as a later event on this clause. The same table in Executive Order 12553 also lists number 10015 with the subject "Amending an order creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes", so the amending order was revoked on the same date by the same sentence.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10010
Creating an E mergency B oard to I nves­
tigate D isputes  B etween  the A kron 
&  Barberton B elt R ailroad C ompany 
and O ther C arriers, and C ertain of 
Their  E mployees
WHEREAS disputes exist between the 
Akron &  Barberton Belt Railroad Com­
pany and certain other carriers desig­
nated in List A attached hereto and made 
a part hereof, and certain of their em­
ployees represented by the sixteen co­
operating railway labor organizations 
designated in List B attached hereto and 
made a part hereof; and 
WHEREAS these disputes have not 
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions jof the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threaten substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate the said disputes.
No member of the said board shall be 
pecuniarily or otherwise interested in 
any organization of railway employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
disputes within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by any of the carriers involved or 
its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said disputes arose.

WHEREAS Executive Order No. 589 of 
March 14,1907, recited in part that pass­
ports issued by the Government of Ja­
pan to Japanese or Korean citizens who 
were skilled or unskilled laborers to go 
to Mexico, Canada, or Hawaii 'were be­
ing used for the purpose of enabling the 
holders thereof to come to the conti­
nental territory of the United States to 
the detriment of labor conditions there­
in, and ordered that such citizens of Ja­
pan or Korea be refused permission to 
enter the continental territory of the 
United States and 
WHEREAS Executive Order No. 1712 
of February 24, 1913, recited that pass­
ports issued by certain foreign govern­
ments to their citizens or subjects, skilled 
or unskilled laborers, to go to countries 
or places other than the continental ter­
ritory of the United States were being 
used for the purpose of enabling the 
holders thereof to come to the x  conti­
nental territory of the United States to
the detriment of labor conditions there­
in, and ordered that such alien laborers, 
skilled or unskilled, be refused permis­
sion to enter the continental territory 
of the United States; and
WHEREAS the continued restraint 
imposed by the said Executive orders 
upon the freedom of Japanese or Korean 
citizens or subjects who entered the Ter­
ritory of Hawaii under the passports 
referred to above to come to the con­
tinental United States has resulted in 
considerable personal hardship to such 
persons; and
WHEREAS the number of Japanese 
or Korean citizens or subjects thus pro­
hibited from entering the continental 
United States from the Territory of Ha­
waii is so small, and the age of such 
persons is so advanced, that their entry 
into the continental United States would 
no longer be a detriment to labor con­
ditions therein:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 3 of the 
Immigration Act of 1917 (39 Stat. 875; 
8 U. S. C. 136), I hereby revoke the said 
Executive Orders No. 589 of March 14, 
1907, and No. 1712 of February 24, 1913, 
to the extent that they are applicable 
to Japanese or Korean citizens or sub­
jects who entered the Territory of Hawaii 
under the aforesaid passports and who 
are now precluded from legally enterr 
ing or remaining in the continental ter­
ritory of the United States by reason of 
such Executive orders.
The Commissioner of Immigration and 
Naturalization is hereby authorized and 
directed, with the approval of the At­
torney General, to take such action and 
to issue such rules and regulations as 
may be necessary for carrying out the 
provisions of this order.
H arry S. Truman
The W hite H ouse,
October 18, 1948.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (13 FR 6104, the issue of October 19, 1948; the order begins on PDF page 6 and its attached lists continue on page 7) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 10010, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company dispute, and is signed by Harry S. Truman at The White House on October 18, 1948. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Prior research: a filed claim for this order exists (research/readiness/claims/claude-2026-10-31-apollo-g03.jsonl, line 11) and carries an independent AI whole-case review, but its reasoning described Executive Order 10015 as an amendment without recording it as a later event with a source; this version records it from the Federal Register text of Executive Order 10015 and keeps the end date. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete with no coverage warning and no scope note. The U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order; the Federal Register catalog search found the two instruments recorded here (the amendment of November 5, 1948 and the revocation of February 25, 1986).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by November 17, 1948), and a standstill that runs from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. A held lead copy of the board's own report (a text of PDF pages 1-8 of 70 from the National Mediation Board site, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) carries the date December 17, 1948 on its title page and states that the parties stipulated on the record to extend the time for the board to submit its report to the President until December 17; thirty days after December 17, 1948 is January 16, 1949. These dates are leads and are not recorded as later events, because no claim-grade source and no reviewed factual-event record for the report is held for this order; they are also not claimed as an end, and the clause is described only as functionally spent. The dossier chain, the Federal Register catalog disposition note for this order (amended by Executive Order 10015 of November 5, 1948; revoked by Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986) and my reading of the held texts of Executive Order 10015 and Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25. Executive Order 10015 is an amendment of the attached lists and is recorded as a later event, not as an end.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and the attached List A and List B follow it. The recitals incorporate the lists by reference to identify the carriers and the railway labor organizations, and the lists contain no command; Executive Order 10015 later amended them. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence of Executive Order 12553."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one railway labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10029 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between Northwest Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of January 19, 1949 (due by February 18, 1949), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10029
Creating an E mergency B oard to I nves­
tigate a D ispute  B etween  the N orth­
west  Airlines , I nc., and Certain of Its 
Employees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Northwest Airlines, Inc., a carrier, 
and certain of its employees represented 
by the International Association of Ma­
chinists, a labor organization; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a large section of the country 
of essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Northwest Airlines, Inc., or 
its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.

End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25 under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadline option C): a report deadline and an expired standstill are not ends. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete with no coverage warning.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (February 18, 1949, thirty days after signing on January 19, 1949) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); that statute is an independent source of duty and is untouched by the revocation, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows them still running.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full and contains no saving clause. The residual consequences of the order (the board's investigation and report, any settlement of the dispute) are not shown to depend on its continued force. Signature, date line and any attached list identify the parties and contain no separate command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10032 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10032_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10032_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_cf5124cbbf.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated April 11, 1949 and a letter of transmittal to the President dated Washington, D.C., April 11, 1949; the board states that the President approved, on February 19, 1949, an extension permitting it to file its report not later than April 13, 1949. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking April 11, 1949 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on April 11, 1949 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to May 11, 1949 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. No earlier end is shown in held evidence. Extension of the report deadline: the held National Mediation Board report copy (a held text lead, not an authenticated original, so it cannot be registered as a later-event source in this sheet) states that the President approved on February 19, 1949 an extension of the report time to not later than April 13, 1949; the extension moves the report deadline and is not an end, and it is disclosed here and not entered as a later event.

§  648.71 Applicability of  §§648.71 to 
648.85.' Sections 648.71 to 648.85 shall 
govern the establishment of farm acre­
age goals for Irish potatoes for use in 
connection with United States Depart­
ment of Agriculture price support opera­
tions relating to the 1949 crop of such 
potatoes. The planting of potatoes in ex­
cess of the 1949 goal established for any 
farm, or, where separate goals are estab­
lished for early and late potatoes, the 
planting or potatoes in excess of either 
of such goals, shall, subsequent to the 
date of such excess planting, render any 
person having an interest in such farm
as operator, owner, landlord, tenant or 
partner ineligible to participate in 1949 
potato price support operations. Such 
ineligibility shall extend also to any cor­
poration or corporate stockholder whose 
operations are subject to substantially 
the same management, ownership, or 
control as those of a corporation or cor­
porate stockholder planting potatoes in 
excess of an acreage goal. Potatoes 
which are produced on a farm owned or 
operated by a partnership shall be in­
eligible in case any partner plants pota­
toes on any other farm in excess of the 
acreage goal for such farm. The entire 
interest in potatoes planted within a 
non-commercial farm goal must be in the 
owner, or in the owner and the operator, 
of such entire farm. Any person having 
an interest, other than as owner or opera­
tor of the entire farm, in potato produc­
tion from one or more non-commercial 
farms, shall be ineligible to participate 
in 1949 potato price support operations. 
Publicly owned experiment stations 
planting potatoes for experimental pur­
poses only do not come within the scope 
of this program; no goal shall be estab­
lished for such experimental plantings 
nor shall the potatoes produced thereon 
be eligible for acquisition under price 
support operations.
§  648.72 Definitions. As used in 
§§ 648.71 to 648.85 and in all instructions, 
forms, and documents in connection 
therewith, the words and phrases defined 
in this section shall have the meanings 
herein assigned to them unless the con­
text or subject matter requires otherwise.
(a) Committees: (1) “County com­
mittee” means the group of persons 
elected within a county to assist in the 
administration of the Agricultural Con­
servation Program in such county.
(2) “State committee” means the 
group of persons designated as the State 
committee of the Production and Market­
ing Administration charged with the re­
sponsibility of administering Production 
and Marketing Administration programs 
within the State.
(b) “Farm” means ah' adjacent or 
nearby farm land under the same owner­
ship which is operated by one person, 
including also: (1) Any other adjacent 
or nearby farm land which the county 
committee, in accordance with instruc­
tions issued by the Production and Mar­
keting Administration, determines is op­
erated by the same persons as part of 
the same unit with respect to rotation of 
crops and with workstock, farm machin­
ery and labor substantially separate from 
that for any other lands;* and (2) any 
field-rented tract (whether operated by
the same or another person) which, to­
gether with any other land included in 
the farm, constitutes a unit with respect 
to the rotation of crops. A farm shall 
be regarded as located in the county in 
which the principal dwelling is situated, 
or if there is no dwelling thereon it shall 
be regarded as located in the county in 
which the major portion of the farm is 
located.
(c) “New farm” means a farm on 
which potatoes have not been planted 
since 1945 and on which the 1949 farm 
operator’ s personal history of potato pro­
duction since 1945 is not used in deter­
mining the farm goal.
(d) “Old farm” means a farm on 
which potatoes have been planted in one 
or more years since 1945 or on which the 
1949 farm operator’ s personal history of 
potato production since 1945 is used in 
determining the farm goal.
(e) “Commercial farm” means a farm 
for which a preliminary 1949 goal of 
three or more acres is established.
(f) “Non-commercial farm” meçms a 
farm on which potatoes are planted in 
1949 and for which a preliminary 1949 
potato acreage goal of three or more 
acres is not established.
(g) “National goal” means the total 
number of acres of Irish potatoes estab­
lished by the United States Department 
of Agriculture as necessary to produce a 
1949 crop sufficient for all domestic and 
export requirements without unduly cur­
tailing production in any area.
(h) “State goal” means the number of 
acres out of the National goal allocated 
by the Production and Marketing Ad­
ministration to be planted within a par­
ticular State.
(i) “Commercial goal” means that part 
of the total goal which is made available 
for apportioning to commercial farms.
(j) “Non-commercial goal” means that 
part of the total goal which is attributed 
to non-commercial farms. No direct ap­
portionment of the non-commercial goal 
to any farm is provided.
(k) “Preliminary goal” is the acreage 
which the county committee preliminar­
ily determines to be the proper goal for a 
farm, in view of the county limit as here­
inafter defined, past goals on the farm, 
topography, crop rotation practice, and 
land, labor, and equipment available for 
the production, handling, and market­
ing of potatoes grown on the farm.
(l) “Final goal” for a farm Is its pre­
liminary goal after such goal has been 
adjusted by the county committee so that 
the total of all final goals in the county 
shall not exceed the county limit, pur­
suant to the procedure specified in 
§§ 648.73 and 648.78.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10032 at 14 FR 429 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed January 28, 1949; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the February 1, 1949 issue. Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 580 to 2224 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence (the sentence barring changes in conditions). Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Akron, Canton & Youngstown Railroad Company and certain other carriers designated in a list attached to the order, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars any of the carriers involved or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. The list of carriers (Eastern, Western and Southeastern regions) follows the signature block in the held text; it identifies the carriers and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10032 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10032_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10032_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_cf5124cbbf.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated April 11, 1949 and a letter of transmittal to the President dated Washington, D.C., April 11, 1949; the board states that the President approved, on February 19, 1949, an extension permitting it to file its report not later than April 13, 1949. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking April 11, 1949 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on April 11, 1949 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to May 11, 1949 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches. Extension of the report deadline: the held National Mediation Board report copy (a held text lead, not an authenticated original, so it cannot be registered as a later-event source in this sheet) states that the President approved on February 19, 1949 an extension of the report time to not later than April 13, 1949; the extension moves the report deadline and is not an end, and it is disclosed here and not entered as a later event.

The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing, the National Mediation Board report copy. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10050 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Railway Express Agency, Inc., and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of April 9, 1949 (due by May 9, 1949), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10050
Creating an E mergency B oard to I nves­
tigate a D ispute  B etween  the R ail­
way Express Agency, Inc., and Certain 
of I ts E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Railway Express Agency, Inc., a car­
rier, and certain of its employees repre­
sented by the Brotherhood of Railway  
and Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers,  
Express and Station Employes, a labor  
organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not hereto­
fore been adjusted under the provisions  
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such, as to  
deprive a large section of the country of  
essential transportation service;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me, to  
investigate said dispute. No member of  
the said board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization^  
of employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said  
dispute within thirty days from the date  
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Railway Express Agency,  
Inc., or its employees in the conditions  
out of which the said dispute arose.

WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Union Railroad Company (Pitts­
burgh) , a carrier, and certain of its em­
ployees represented by the Brotherhood 
of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organiza­
tion; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce within the State of 
Pennsylvania to a degree such as to de­
prive that portion of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 .of- 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No

carrier.

the President with respect to the said

of this order.
