operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10071 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines) and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of July 20, 1949 (due by August 19, 1949), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10071
Creating an E mergency O rder to I nves ­
tigate a D ispute  B etween  the S outh ­
ern P acific C ompany (P acific L ines ) 
and C ertain of its  E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific  
Lines), a carrier, and certain of its em­
ployees represented by the Brotherhood
of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organiza­
tion; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions  
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as  
to deprive a large section of the country  
of essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me, to  
investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily  
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said  
dispute within thirty days from the date  
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Southern Pacific Company  
(Pacific Lines) or its employees in the  
conditions out of which the said dispute  
arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10078 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Monongahela Connecting Railroad Company and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of September 9, 1949 (due by October 9, 1949), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

WHEREAS s l dispute exists between  
the Monongahela Connecting Railroad  
Company, a carrier, and certain of its  
employees represented by the Brother­
hood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor or­
ganization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not hereto­
fore been adjusted under the provisions  
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce within the State of*  
Pennsylvania to a degree such as to de­
prive that portion of the country of essen­

Identity: the held Federal Register text is the order itself (heading and body read in full; signed September 9, 1949). Inventory read and confirmed (correction only where stated). End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25 under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadline option C): a report deadline and an expired standstill are not ends. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete with no coverage warning.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (October 9, 1949, thirty days after signing on September 9, 1949) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10105 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The order creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947 to inquire into the issues in a labor dispute affecting the bituminous coal industry, with a report due on a stated date and a provision that, once the report is submitted, the Board continues in existence to perform other functions required under the Act until the President terminates it. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the Board, its report date, and its continuation until terminated by the President are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10106 with a subject line matching this order (creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10112 (15 FR 1065; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10112 and signed February 24, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the Eastern Carriers' Conference Committee, the Western Carriers' Conference Committee and the Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committee and certain of their employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10112 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

No effective-date wording appears in the enacting provision, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (reading, disclosed for the reviewer); the exclusive and inclusive readings do not differ because this is not an until-date. EXECUTIVE ORDER 10117
Creating an E mergency  B oard T o I n­
vestigate a D ispute  B etween  the 
Carriers  R epresented  by  the W est ­
ern C arriers ’ C onference  C ommittee  
and C ertain of T heir  E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the carriers represented by the Western 
Carriers’ Conference Committee and cer­
tain of their employees represented by 
the Switchmen’s Union of North Amer­
ica, a labor organization; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive the country of essential 
transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U, S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the carriers represented by the 
Western Carriers’ Conference Commit­
tee, or their employees in the conditions 
out of which the said dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10120, whose subject line describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute. No effective-date wording appears in the enacting provision, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (reading, disclosed for the reviewer); the exclusive and inclusive readings do not differ because this is not an until-date. Report deadline and status-quo period are not ends; functionally spent when the board reported and the statutory period ran, but the order remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier express end was found.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10120 (15 FR 2073; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10120 and signed April 11, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees and certain of their employees represented by the Railroad Yardmasters of America, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10120 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The machine dossier did not locate the revoking provision for this pair; the held text of EO 12553 does contain the row for this order (number followed by a subject line) in the No. Subject table on its page 10, and the enacting sentence precedes the table, so the whole held EO 12553 text is cited as the ending source. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.

(1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: the held text of EO 12553 contains no savings or exception clause attached to the revocation list (the enacting provision is a single sentence followed by the table, and the only effective-date or exception wording found anywhere in the order is outside it). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and law s of the  
United States of Am erica, and to eliminate Executive Orders that are no

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10125 at 15 FR 2391 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed April 26, 1950; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the April 28, 1950 issue. Inventory corrected: one operative clause, offsets 1449 to the end of the sentence barring changes in conditions, from the enacting words to the last operative sentence. The dossier's span (offsets 672 to 3814) began at the order's heading and ran past the order's end, which comes at the words 'out of which the said dispute arose.' followed by the President's signature, into an unrelated Department of Agriculture regulation (Part 517, fresh apple export program, F.R. Doc. 50-3600) and the heading of Title 7 Part 201 (Federal Seed Act). The heading and the three recitals before the enacting words contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Chicago & Illinois Midland Railway Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Chicago & Illinois Midland Railway Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10125 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10125_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10125_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_d68f78cdf2.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated May 19, 1950 and a letter of transmittal to the President, signed by the board's chairman and two members (the text layer garbles the month in the letter's date line), which submits the board's report. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking May 19, 1950 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on May 19, 1950 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to June 18, 1950 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Boston & Albany Railroad Company (New York Central R.R. Company, Lessee) and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10130 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.

(2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10138 with a subject line describing an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute. The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer); this is not an until-date, so no inclusive or exclusive reading arises. The thirty-day report deadline and the statutory period after the report are not ends; the board reported on August 11, 1950 (held report title page), after which the order was functionally spent but remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10138
Creating an E mergency B oard T o I nves ­
tigate D ispute  B etween  the T oledo, 
Lorain &  Fairport D ock C ompany  and 
Certain of I ts E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Toledo, Lorain &  Fairport Dock Com­
pany, a carrier, and certain of its 
employees represented by the Interna­
tional Longshoremen’ s Association, A. F. 
of L., a labor organization; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No 
member of the said board shall be pe­
cuniarily or otherwise interested in any 
organization of railway employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Toledo, Lorain &  Fairport 
Dock Company or its employees in the 
conditions out of which the said dispute 
arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10138 at 15 FR 4241, in the Federal Register of July 4, 1950 (PDF page 3; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The page header in the held text reads FEDERAL REGISTER 4241 with the date Tuesday, July 4, 1950; the order is headed Executive Order 10138, is signed July 3, 1950, and its filing line reads Filed, July 3, 1950. The same page also prints Executive Order 10139, which concerns the Toledo Lakefront Dock Company. Text: the order recites a dispute between the Toledo, Lorain & Fairport Dock Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, A. F. of L.; invoking section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, it states "I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to investigate the said dispute." It provides that no member of the board may be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier, directs the board to report its findings to the President "within thirty days from the date of this order", and, as provided by section 10 of the Act, states that from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board has reported "no change, except by agreement, shall be made" by the company or its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the last operative sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10138 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10138_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10138_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_ba0763e74c.txt, PDF page 1) is titled as the report of the emergency board appointed July 3, 1950 by Executive Orders 10138 and 10139, and its title page is dated at Toledo, Ohio, August 11, 1950. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12553 revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in Federal Register text files of the same issue (the files for Executive Orders 10136 to 10139 hold the same pages), a Federal Register codification guide for page 4241, and the front matter of the board's report.

The board's held report is dated August 11, 1950; that date is disclosed here as the date on which the order became functionally spent, not as its end. (2) The thirty-day period after the report during which no change could be made except by agreement comes from section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; the held sources do not show when the President received the report, so no exact end of that period is asserted, and its running out is a spent fact, not an end. (3) No instrument before Executive Order 12553 amends, supersedes or revokes the order: the OFR disposition notes record only that revocation, and the held-text number search found no other instrument naming the order. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command independent of the board it creates. Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10139 at 15 FR 4241, in the Federal Register of July 4, 1950 (PDF page 3; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The page header in the held text reads FEDERAL REGISTER 4241 with the date Tuesday, July 4, 1950; the order is headed Executive Order 10139 and is signed July 3, 1950. Its filing line in the text layer reads Filed, July 8, 1950, which cannot be right for a page published on July 4, 1950 and is read as an OCR error for July 3. The same page also prints Executive Order 10138, which concerns the Toledo, Lorain & Fairport Dock Company. Text: the order recites a dispute between the Toledo Lakefront Dock Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, Local 158, A. F. of L.; invoking section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, it states "I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to investigate the said dispute." It provides that no member of the board may be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier, directs the board to report its findings to the President "within thirty days from the date of this order", and, as provided by section 10 of the Act, states that from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board has reported "no change, except by agreement, shall be made" by the company or its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the last operative sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10139 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10139_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10139_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_fe19979d2d.txt, PDF page 1) is titled as the report of the emergency board appointed July 3, 1950 by Executive Orders 10138 and 10139, and its title page is dated at Toledo, Ohio, August 11, 1950. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12553 revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in Federal Register text files of the same issue (the files for Executive Orders 10136 to 10139 hold the same pages) and a Federal Register codification guide for page 4241.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10140 (15 FR 4333; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10140 and signed July 6, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Pullman Company and certain of its employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10140 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10142, whose subject line describes an emergency board to investigate a airline labor dispute. No effective-date wording appears in the enacting provision, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (reading, disclosed for the reviewer); the exclusive and inclusive readings do not differ because this is not an until-date. Report deadline and status-quo period are not ends; functionally spent when the board reported and the statutory period ran, but the order remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier express end was found.

WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Braniff Airways, Inc., a carrier, and 
certain of its employees represented by 
the Brotherhood of Railway & Steamship 
Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and 
Station Employees, a labor organization; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt 
interstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of es­
sential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I  hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate the said dispute. No member 
of the said board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization 
of employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Braniff Airways, Inc., or its 
employees in the conditions out of which 
the said dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10142 (15 FR 4465; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10142 and signed July 12, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between Braniff Airways, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railway & Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and Station Employees, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10142 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a airline labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The machine dossier did not locate the revoking provision for this pair; the held text of EO 12553 does contain the row for this order (number followed by a subject line) in the No. Subject table on its page 10, and the enacting sentence precedes the table, so the whole held EO 12553 text is cited as the ending source. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: the held text of EO 12553 contains no savings or exception clause attached to the revocation list (the enacting provision is a single sentence followed by the table, and the only effective-date or exception wording found anywhere in the order is outside it). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation has no savings clause and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right: bounded search of the held 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR catalog shows no residual or continuing independent effect.

WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the New York Central Railroad Com­
pany, Lines East of Buffalo, a carrier, 
and certain of its employees represented 
by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engi­
neers, Brotherhood of Locomotive Fire­
men and Enginemen, Order of Railway 
Conductors, and Brotherhood of Rail­
road Trainmen, labor organizations; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of essen­
tial transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board 
of three members, to be appointed by 
me, to investigate the said dispute. No 
member of the said board shall be pe­
cuniarily or otherwise interested in any 
organization of railway employees or any 
carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after thff board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the New York Central Railroad 
Company, Lines East of Buffalo, or by 
its employees, in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10147 (15 FR 5067; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10147 and signed August 4, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the New York Central Railroad Company, Lines East of Buffalo, and certain of its employees represented by four railroad labor organizations, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10147 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.

(1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10150 at 15 FR 5219 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed August 11, 1950; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the August 12, 1950 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3872 to 4182 and 11762 to 12623 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the Atlantic & East Carolina Railway Company and certain other carriers designated in a list A attached to the order, and certain of their employees represented by the sixteen cooperating non-operating labor organizations designated in a list B attached to the order. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; directs that each carrier involved be given independent consideration and that the labor organizations be permitted to function as a unit before the board; permits the board, to the extent it deems necessary or desirable, to make separate and independent findings with respect to each carrier involved; and, as provided by section 10, it bars any of the carriers involved or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Lists A and B (the carriers and the labor organizations) follow the signature block in the held text; they identify the parties and are not separate commands. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10150 describes creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10150_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10150_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_519666f265.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated September 9, 1950. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking September 9, 1950 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on September 9, 1950 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to October 9, 1950 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing, the National Mediation Board report copy. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill and the further commands noted in the inventory all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}

EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10165, whose subject line describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute. No effective-date wording appears in the enacting provision, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (reading, disclosed for the reviewer); the exclusive and inclusive readings do not differ because this is not an until-date. EXECUTIVE ORDER 10165
Creating an E mergency B oard to I nves­
tigate a D ispute  B etween the R ail­
way Express Agency, I nc., and Certain 
op its E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Railway Express Agency, Inc., a car­
rier, and certain of its employees repre­
sented by the International Brotherhood 
of Teamsters, Chauffeurs, Warehouse­
men &  Helpers of America, ft. F. of L., 
Locals 808 and 459, a labor organization; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of essen­
tial transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Railway Express Agency, 
Inc., or by its employees, in the condi­
tions out of which the said dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10165 (15 FR 6737; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10165 and signed October 3, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Railway Express Agency, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, Locals 808 and 459, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10165 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21): the order does not end when the board reports, nor when the statutory thirty-day status-quo period after the report runs out; actual report and standstill dates are spent facts that no reviewed event record in this packet supplies, so they are disclosed here rather than recorded as later events. (2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order has no command independent of the board's creation and reporting. The thirty-day report requirement and the status-quo sentence are parts of the same board-creating order and share its end; the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: EO 12553's enacting provision contains no savings or exception clause (the ACT record for this pair lists none, and the held text has none). The board's work, report and any agreement reached are completed past events rather than continuing commands of this order; the order created no right, appointment or transfer that survives independently of it, and no held source shows any continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: EO 12553 revokes the order by number and the held table row matches its subject; the enacting provision reaches any amendments thereto and has no exception, so it reaches the whole order, not part. WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the American Airlines, Inc., a carrier, 
and certain of its employees represented 
by the Air Line Pilots Association, In­
ternational, a labor organization; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of , the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I  hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No memi 
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
ttie President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the American Airlines, Inc., or 
its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10203 (16 FR 385; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10203 and signed January 13, 1951. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the American Airlines, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10203 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a airline labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.

(2) The statutory standstill in section 10 of the Railway Labor Act is the statute's own effect and not a separate command of this order. (3) No later order amends, supersedes or revokes the order before EO 12553 in the held corpus (OFR catalog and number-citation searches). EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes it. research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10222 at 16 FR 2247, in the Federal Register of March 13, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10222, Providing for Certain Transfers to the Federal Civil Defense Administration, is signed March 8, 1951, and its filing line reads Filed, Mar. 12, 1951. Text and inventory: three numbered paragraphs, confirmed as three clauses. Paragraph 1 transfers to the Federal Civil Defense Administration so much of the health services and special weapons defense functions of the Health Resources Office of the National Security Resources Board as relates to civil defense, to remain under the jurisdiction of the Federal Civil Defense Administrator "until further order of the President." Paragraph 2 transfers the related property and records of the Board, and the personnel of the Health Resources Office engaged primarily in those functions, as the Board's Chairman and the Administrator jointly determine. Paragraph 3 reads "This order shall be effective as of March 4, 1951." Ending: Executive Order 12919, National Defense Industrial Resources Preparedness, signed June 3, 1994 and printed at 59 FR 29525 in the Federal Register of June 7, 1994 (held govinfo text layer), provides in section 904(a) that "The following are superseded or revoked:" and lists as item (2) "Executive Order No. 10222 of March 8, 1951 (16 FR 2247)". Neither section 904 nor any other part of that order states an effective date, so the end is dated on signing, 1994-06-03; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of June 7, 1994 is not used. The machine U.S. Code search found the editorial note under 42 U.S.C. 5195 that records the same revocation by section 904(a)(2) of Executive Order 12919. Unnamed earlier candidates, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments: the editorial note printed with this order in the held OFR 1989 Codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_10222.txt) says that Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958 terminated the Federal Civil Defense Administration, effective July 1, 1958, and consolidated its functions into the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization, and that Executive Order 10952 of July 20, 1961 later transferred civil defense functions to the Secretary of Defense. The text of the reorganization plan is not held; the held Federal Register text of Executive Order 10952 (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10952.txt, 26 FR 6577) does not name this order. Neither instrument names Executive Order 10222, and no held source shows that either extinguished its commands; the same 1989 Codification still printed the order as in force on January 20, 1989. Neither has an evidence record in this dossier, so each is disclosed here rather than recorded as a later event. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12919 supersession or revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in the held texts of Executive Order 12919 and in the OFR 1989 Codification.

(1) Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958, which terminated the Federal Civil Defense Administration, and Executive Order 10952 of July 20, 1961, which moved civil defense functions to the Secretary of Defense, are known here from the editorial note in the held OFR 1989 Codification; neither names Executive Order 10222, and no held source shows the order's commands extinguished by them. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments they are disclosed earlier candidates, not ends. (2) The words until further order of the President in paragraph 1 make the jurisdiction command contingent; the only held presidential order that names this order and ends it is Executive Order 12919. (3) The transfers in paragraph 2 were one-time acts, but no held source dates their completion, so no exhaustion date is asserted. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"Paragraph 1 (jurisdiction over the transferred functions until further order of the President) and paragraph 2 (the transfer of property, records and personnel) are distinct commands of the same order, and paragraph 3 fixes the order's effective date. None has its own source, statute or earlier end shown in held evidence; each shares the supersession by Executive Order 12919, and the executed transfers survive as accrued effects.","savings_check":"The executed transfers are accrued effects (state transferred_or_accrued). The dossier note that the 1989 current-law lead lacks an original-source sha256 does not affect this claim: the order is a NO order, the 1989 Codification is not used as a current predicate, and it is cited only for its editorial observations, which predate the 1994 supersession."}

savings_residuals.reason: The transfers of functions, property, records and personnel made under the order are accrued effects of executed transfers. Section 903 of Executive Order 12919 provides that previously issued orders and other actions relating to any function it affects "shall remain in effect except as they are inconsistent with this order" or are later amended or revoked, and that "Nothing in this order shall affect the validity or force of anything done under previous delegations or other assignment of authority under the Act." The whole held text of Executive Order 12919 is cited as the savings source.

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the Defense Production 
Act of 1950, as amended (64 Stat. 798; 50 U .S.C  App. 2061, e t seq .)  
and section 301 of title 3, United States Code, and as Commander in Chief 
of the Armed Forces of the United States, it is hereby ordered as follows
PART 1 — PURPOSE, POLICY AND IMPLEMENTATION
Section 101. P u rp o se. This order delegates authorities and addresses national 
defense industrial resource policies and programs under the Defense Produc­
tion Act of 1950, as amended (“the A ct”), except for the amendments to 
Title III of the Act in the Energy Security Act of 1980 and telecommunication 
authorities under Executive Order No. 12472.
Sec. 102. P o licy . The United States must have an industrial and technology 
base capable of meeting national defense requirements, and capable of con­
tributing to the technological superiority o f its defense equipment in peace­
time and in times of national emergency. The domestic industrial and techno- 
logical base is the foundation for national defense preparedness. The authori­
ties provided in the Act shall be used to strengthen this base and to ensure 
it is capable of responding to all threats to the national security of the 
United States.
Sec. 103. G en era l F u n ctio n s.  Federal departments and agencies responsible 
for defense acquisition (or for industrial resources needed to support defense 
acquisition) shall:
(a) Identify requirements for the full spectrum of national security emer­
gencies, including m ilitary, industrial, and essential civilian demand;
(b) Assess continually the capability of the domestic industrial and techno­
logical base to satisfy requirements in peacetime and times of national 
emergency, specifically evaluating the availability o f adequate industrial 
resource and production sources, including subcontractors and suppliers 
materials, skilled labor, and professional and technical personnel;
(c) Be prepared, in the event of a potential threat to the security of 
the United States, to take actions necessary to ensure the availability of 
adequate industrial resources and production capability, including services 
and critical technology for national defense requirements;
(d) Improve the efficiency and responsiveness to defense requirements 
of the domestic industrial base; and
(e) Foster cooperation between the defense and commercial sectors for 
research and development and for acquisition of materials, components 
and equipment to enhance industrial base efficiency and responsiveness
Sec. 104. Im p le m e n ta tio n , (a) The National Security Council is the principal 
forum for consideration and resolution of national security resource prepared­
ness policy. -
(b) The Director, Federal Emergency' Management Agency (“Director 
FEM A”) shall:
(1) Serve as an advisor to the National Security Council on issues 
of national security resource preparedness and on the use of the 
authorities and functions delegated by this order-

(2.) Provide for the central coordination of the plans and programs *  
incident to authorities and functions delegated under this order,  
and provide guidance and procedures approved by the Assistant  
to the President for National Security Affairs to the Federal depart­
ments and agencies under this order;
(3) Establish procedures» in consultation with Federal departments  
and agencies assigned functions under this order, to résolve in  
a. timely and effective manner conflicts and issues that may arise  
in implementing the authorities and functions delegated under this  
order; and
(4) Report to the President periodically concerning all program activi­
ties conducted pursuant to this order.
(c) The head of every Federal department and agency assigned functions  
under this, order shall ensure that the performance of these functions is  
consistent with National Security Council policy and guidelines.
PART H— PRtORITIES AND ALLOCATIONS
Sec. 2G T. Delegations of Priorities and Allocations,  (a) The authority of  
the President conferred by section 101 of the Act to require acceptance  
and priority performance of contracts or orders (other than contracts of  
employment) to promote the national defense over performance of any other  
contracts or orders, and to allocate materials, services, and facilities as  
deemed necessary or appropriate to promote the national defense, is delegated  
to the following agency heads;
(1) The Secretary of Agriculture with respect to food resources,  
food resource facilities, and the domestic distribution of farm equip­
ment and commercial fertilizer;.
(2) The Secretary of Energy with respect to all forms of energy;
(3) The Secretary of Health and Human Services with respect to  
health resources;
(4) The Secretary of Transportation with respect to all forms of  
civil transportation;
(5) ;  The Secretary of Defense with respect to water resources; and
(6) The Secretary of Commerce for all other materials, services,  
and facilities, including construction materials.
C & l f  The Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the heads of those  
departments and agencies specified in subsection 201(a) of this order, shall  
administer the Defense Priorities and Allocations System (“DPAS”) regula­
tions that will be used to implement the authority of the President conferred  
by section 1-01 of the Act as delegated to the Secretary of Commerce in  
subsection 201(a)(6) of this order. The Secretary of Commerce will redelegate  
to the-Secretary of Defense, and the heads of other departments and agencies  
as appropriate, authority for the priority rating of contracts and orders for  
all. materials, services, and facilities needed in support of programs approved  
under section 202 of this order. The Secretary of Commerce shall act as  
appropriate upon Special Priorities Assistance requests in a time frame  
consistent with the urgency of the need at hand.
fcl The Director, FEMA, shall attempt to resolve issues or disagreements  
on priorities or allocations between Federal departments or agencies in  
a time frame consistent with the urgency of the issue at hand and, if  
not resolved, such issues will be referred to the Assistant to the President  
for National Security Affairs for final determination.
(dr) The head of each Federal department or agency assigned functions  
under subsection 201(a) of this order, when necessary, shall make the finding  
required under subsection 101(b) of the Act. This finding shall be submitted  
for the President’s approval through the Assistant to the President for Na­
tional Security Affairs. Upon such approval the head, of the Federal depart-
