101(a) of the Act to control the general distribution of any material (including 
applicable services) in the civilian market.
(e) The Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs is hereby 
delegated the authority under subsection 101(c)(3) of the Act, and will 
be assisted by the Director, FEMA* in ensuring the coordinated administration 
of the Act.
Sec. 202. Determinations.  The authority delegated by section 201 of this 
order may be used only to support programs that have been determined 
in writing as necessary or appropriate to promote the national defense:
(a) By the Secretary of Defense with respect to military production and 
construction, military assistance to foreign nations, stockpiling, outer space, 
and directly related activities;
(b) By the Secretary of Energy with respect to energy production and 
construction, distribution and use, and directly related activities; and
(c) By the Director, FEMA, with respect to essential civilian needs support­
ing national defense, including civil defense and continuity of government 
and directly related activities.
Sec. 203. Maximizing Domestic  Energy Supplies.  The authority of the Presi­
dent to perform the functions provided by subsection 101(c) of the Act 
is delegated to the Secretary of Commerce, who shall redelegate to the 
Secretary of Energy the authority to make the findings described in subsection 
101(c)(2)(A) that the m aterials (including equipment), services, and facilities 
are critical and essential. The Secretary of Commerce shall make the finding 
described in subsection 101(c)(2)(A) of the Act that the materials (including 
equipment), services, or facilities are scarce, and the finding described in 
subsection 101(c)(2)(B) that it is necessary to use the authority provided 
by subsection 101(c)(1).
Sec. 204. Chemical and Biological Warfare.  The authority of the President 
conferred by subsection 104(b) of the Act is delegated to the Secretary 
of Defense. This authority may not be further delegated by the Secretary.
PART III— EXPANSION OF PRODUCTIVE CAPACITY AND SUPPLY
Sec. 301. (a) Financing Institution Guarantees.  To expedite or expand produc­
tion and deliveries or services under government contracts for the procure­
ment of industrial resources or critical technology items essential to the 
national defense, the head of each Federal department or agency engaged 
in procurement for the national defense (referred to as “agency head” in 
this part) and the President and Chairman o f the Export-Import Bank of 
the United States (in cases involving capacity expansion, technological d evel­
opment, or production in foreign countries) are authorized to guarantee 
in w hole or in part any public or private financing institution, subject 
to provisions of section 301 of the Act. Guarantees shall be made in consulta­
tion with the Department of the Treasury as to the terms and conditions 
thereof. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget (“OMB”) 
shall be informed when such guarantees are to be made.
(b) Direct Loan Guarantees.  To expedite or expand production and deliv­
eries or services under government contracts for the procurement of industrial 
resources or critical technology items essential to the national defense, each 
agency head is authorized to make direct loan guarantees from funds appro­
priated to their agency for Title HI.
(c) Fiscal Agent.  Each Federal Reserve Bank is designated and authorized 
to act, on behalf of any guaranteeing agency, as fiscal agent in the making 
of guarantee contracts and in otherwise carrying out the purposes of section 
301 of the Act.
(d) Regulations.  The Board of Governors o f the Federal Reserve System 
is authorized, after consultation with heads of guaranteeing departments 
and agencies, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Director, OMB, to

prescribe regulations governing procedures, forms, rates of interest, and fees  
for such guarantee contracts.
Sec. 302. Loans,  (a) To expedite production and deliveries or services to  
aid in carrying out government contracts for the procurement of industrial  
resources or a critical technology item foi the national defense, an agency  
head is authorized, subject to the provisions of section 302 of the Act,  
to submit to the Secretary of the Treasury or the President and Chairman  
of the Export-Import Bank of the United States (in cases involving capacity  
expansion, technological development, or production in foreign countries)  
applications for loans.
(b) To expedite or expand production and deliveries or services under  
government contracts for the procurement of industrial resources or critical  
technology items essential to the national defense, each agency head may  
make direct loans from funds appropriated to their agency for Title III.
(c) After receiving a loan application and determining that financial assist­
ance is not otherwise available on reasonable terms, the Secretary of the  
Treasury or the President and Chairman of the Export-Import Bank of the  
United States (in cases involving capacity expansion, technological develop­
ment, or production in foreign countries) may make loans, subject to provi­
sions of section 302 of the Act.
Sec. 303. Purchase Commitments,  (a) In order to carry out the objectives  
of the Act, and subject to the provisions of section 303 thereof, an agency  
head is authorized to make provision for purchases of, or commitments  
to purchase, an industrial resource or a critical technology item for govern­
ment use or resale.
(b) Materials acquired under section 303 of the Act that exceed the needs  
of the programs under the Act may be transferred to the National Defense  
Stockpile, if such transfer is determined by the Secretary of Defense as  
the National Defense Stockpile Manager to be in the public interest.
Sec. 304. Subsidy Payments.  In order to ensure the supply of raw or non-  
processed materials from high-cost sources, an agency head is authorized  
to make subsidy payments, after consultation with the Secretary of the  
Treasury and the Director, OMB, and subject to the provisions of section  
303(c) of the Act.
Sec. 305. Determinations and Findings.  When carrying out the authorities  
in sections 301 through 303 of this order, an agency head is authorized  
to make the required determinations, judgments, statements, certifications,  
and findings, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, Secretary of  
Energy or Director, FEMA, as appropriate. The agency head shall provide  
a copy of the determination, judgment, statement, certification, or finding  
to the Director, OMB, to the Director, FEMA, and, when appropriate, to  
the Secretary of the Treasury.
Sec. 306. Strategic and Critical Materials, [a)  The Secretary of the Interior  
in consultation with the Secretary of Defense as the National Defense Stock­
pile Manager and subject to the provisions of section 303 of the Act, is  
authorized to encourage the exploration, development, and mining of critical  
and strategic.materials and other materials.
(b) An agency head is authorized, pursuant to section 303(g) of the Act,  
to make provision for the development of substitutes for strategic and critical  
materials, critical components, critical technology items, and other industrial  
resources to aid the national defense.
(c) An agency head is authorized, pursuant to section 303(a)(1)(B) of  
the Act, to make provisions to encourage the exploration, development  
and mining of critical and strategic materials and other materials.
Sec. 307 . Government-owned Equipment.  An agency head is authorized,  
pursuant to section 303(e) of the Act, to install additional equipment, facili­
ties, processes, or improvements to facilities owned by the government and  
to install government-owned equipment in industrial facilities owned by  
private persons.

Sec. 308. Identification o f Shortfalls.  Except during periods of national emer­
gency or after a Presidential determination in accordance with sections  
301{e)(l)(D)(ii), 302(c)(4)(B), or 303(a)(7)(B) of the Act, no guarantee, loan  
or other action pursuant to sections 301, 302, and 303 of the Act to correct  
an industrial shortfall shall be taken unless the shortfall has been identified  
in the Budget of the United States or amendments thereto.
Sec. 309. D efense Production Act Fun d  Manager.  The Secretary of Defense  
is designated the Defense Production Act Fund Manager, in accordance  
with section 304(f) of the Act, and shall carry out the duties specified  
in that section, in consultation with the agency heads having approved  
Title H I projects and appropriated Title III funds.
Sec. 310. Critical Items List,  (a) Pursuant to section 107(b)(1)(A) of the  
Act, the Secretary of Defense shall identify critical components and critical  
technology items for each item on the Critical Items List of the Commanders-  
in-Chief of the Unified and Specified Commands and other items within  
the inventory of weapon systems and defense equipment.
(b) Each agency head shall take appropriate action to ensure that critical  
components or critical technology items are available from reliable sources  
when needed to meet defense requirements during peacetime, graduated  
mobilization, and national emergency. “Appropriate action” may include  
restricting contract solicitations to reliable sources, restricting contract solici­
tations to domestic sources (pursuant to statutory authority), stockpiling  
critical components, and developing substitutes for critical components or  
critical technology items.
Sec. 311. Strengthening Domestic Capability.  An agency head, in accordance  
with section 107(a) of the Act, may utilize the authority of Title III of  
the Act or any other provision of law, in consultation with the Secretary  
of Defense, to provide appropriate incentives to develop, maintain, modern­
ize, and expand the productive capacities of domestic sources for critical  
components, critical technology items, and industrial resources essential  
for the execution of the national security strategy of the United States.
Sec. 312. Modernization o f Equipment.  An agency head, in accordance with  
section 108(b) of the Act, may utilize the authority of Title III of the Act  
to guarantee the purchase or lease of advance manufacturing equipment  
and any related services with respect to any such equipment for purposes  
of the Act.
J  PART IV— IMPACT OF OFFSETS
Sec. 401. Offsets. (a) The responsibilities and authority conferred upon the  
President by section 309 of the Act with respect to offsets are delegated  
to the Secretary of Commerce, who shall function as the President’s Executive  
Agent for carrying out this authority.
(b) The Secretary of Commerce shall prepare the annual ^report required  
by section 309(a) of the Act in consultation with the Secretaries of Defense,  
Treasury, Labor, State, the United States Trade Representative, the Arms  
Control and Disarmament Agency, the Director of Central Intelligence, and

(c) The offset report shall be subject to the normal interagency clearance  
process conducted by the Director, OMB, prior to the report’s submission  
by the President to Congress.
PART V— VOLUNTARY AGREEMENTS AND ADVISORY COMMITTEES
Sec. 501. Appointments.  The authority of the President under sections 708(c)  
and (d) of the Act is delegated to the heads of each Federal department  
or agency, except that, insofar as that authority relates to section 101 of  
the Act, it is delegated only to the heads of each Federal department or  
agency assigned functions under section 201(a) of this order. The authority

PART VI— EMPLOYMENT OF PERSONNEL
Sec. 601. National Defense Executive Reserve, (a) In accordance with section 
710(e) of the Act, there is established in the Executive Branch a National 
Defense Executive Reserve (“NDER”) composed of persons of recognized 
expertise from various segments of the private sector and from government 
(except full-time federal employees) for training for employment in executive 
positions in the Federal Government in the event of an emergency that 
requires such employment.
(b) The head of any department or agency may establish a unit of the 
NDER in the department or agency and train members of that unit.
(c) The head of each department or agency with an NDER unit is authorized 
to exercise the President’s authority to employ civilian personnel in accord­
ance with section 703(a) of the Act when activating all or a part of its 
NDER unit. The exercise of this authority shall be subject to the provisions 
of subsections 601(d) and (e) of this order and shall not be redelegated.
(d) The head of a department or agency may activate an NDER unit,

exists and that the activation of the unit is necessary to carry out the 
emergency program functions of the department or agency.
(e) At least 72 hours prior to activating the NDER unit, the head of 
the department or agency shall notify, in writing, the Assistant to the Presi­
dent for National Security Affairs of the impending activation and provide

(f) The Director, FEMA, shall coordinate the NDER program activities

(g) This order suspends any delegated authority, regulation, or other re­
quirement or condition with respect to the activation of any NDER unit, 
in whole or in part, or appointment of any NDER member that is inconsistent 
with the authorities delegated herein, provided that the aforesaid suspension 
applies only as long as sections 703(a) an(K710(e) of the Act are in effect. 
Sec. 602. Consultants. The head of each department or agency assigned 
functions und’ er this order is delegated authority under sections 710(b) and 
(c) of the Act to employ persons of outstanding experience and ability 
without compensation and to employ experts, consultants, or organizations. 
The authority delegated by this section shall not be redelegated.
PART VII— LABOR SUPPLY
Sec. 701. Secretary of Labor. The Secretary of Labor, identified in this 
section as the Secretary, shall;
(a) Collect, analyze, and maintain data needed to make a continuing ap-
|  praisal of the nation’s labor requirements and the supply of workers for
purposes of national defense. All agencies of the government shall cooperate 
I with the Secretary in furnishing information necessary for this purpose,
to the extent permitted by law;
(b) In response to requests from the head of a Federal department or 
agency engaged in the procurement for national defense, Consult with and 
advise that department or agency with respect to (1) the effect of contemplated

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10285 with a subject line describing an emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between certain workers and a railroad operated by the Secretary of the Army. The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer); this is not an until-date, so no inclusive or exclusive reading arises. The thirty-day report deadline is not an end; the board reported on September 19, 1951 (held report), after which the order was functionally spent but remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10285 at 16 FR 9135, in the Federal Register of September 8, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10285 and is signed September 6, 1951. Text: the order recites a dispute between The Denver & Rio Grande Western Railroad Company, including the Denver & Salt Lake Railroad Company, a carrier under Federal management, and certain workers represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, and recites that by Executive Order No. 10155 of August 25, 1950 the President, through the Secretary of the Army, assumed possession, control and operation of the carrier's transportation system. Invoking the Constitution and laws, including section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, and subject to that section, it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute. Its operative text then has three more sentences: "Nothing in this order shall be construed to derogate from the authority of the Secretary of the Army under the said Executive Order No. 10155."; a sentence directing the board to "report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order" (the text layer drops the sentence's first word); and "In performing its functions under this order the Board shall comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended." Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the Defense Production Act sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10285 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between certain workers and a railroad operated by the Secretary of the Army". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10285_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10285_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_ec5eddd465.txt) is titled as the report of the emergency board created September 6, 1951 by Executive Order 10285, and its title page and letter of transmittal are dated at Denver, September 19, 1951. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records the Executive Order 12553 revocation and a cross-reference between this order and Executive Order 10155. The held-text number search found this number only in Federal Register text files of the same issue (the files for Executive Orders 10285, 10286 and 10287) and the front matter of the board's report.

(2) The order acts subject to section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; any period that statute fixes after the report is the statute's own effect and a spent fact, not an end of the order. (3) The Defense Production Act sentence governs how the board performs its functions; the statute is not held in this repository, and the board's functions ended in practice with its report, so no expiry of that statute is claimed as an end. (4) Executive Order 10155 is recited as the basis of federal operation and in the sentence preserving the Secretary of the Army's authority; it predates this order and does not act on it. WHEREAS a dispute exists between

men and Enginemen, a labor organiza­
tion; and
WHEREAS by Executive Order No. 
10155 of August 25,1950, possession, con­
trol, and operation of the transportation 
systems owned or operated by the said 
carriers, together with the transporta-, 
tion systems owned or operated by cer­
tain other carriers, were assumed by the

amended; and

deprive certain sections of the country

also threatens to interfere with the op­
eration by the Secretary of the Army of 
transportation systems taken pursuant 
to the said Executive Order No. 10155;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by the Consti­
tution and the laws of the United States, 
including section 10 of the Railway Labor 
Act, as amended (45 U. S. C. 160), and 
subject to the provisions of that section, 
I hereby create a board of three mem­
bers, to be appointed by me, to investi­
gate the said dispute. Nothing in this
order shall be construed to derogate from 
the authority of the Secretary of the 
Army under the said Executive Order No. 
10155.
The Board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.

order the Board shall comply with the 
requirements of section 502 of the De­
fense Production Act of 1950, as 
amended.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10303 at 16 FR 11321, in the Federal Register of November 8, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10303, is signed November 6, 1951, and its filing line reads Filed, Nov. 7, 1951. Text: the order recites a dispute between the Baltimore & Ohio Railroad Company, the Chicago & North Western Railway Company, the Louisville & Nashville Railroad Company, the Terminal Railroad Association of St. Louis and all other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western, and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees, carriers under Federal management, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, and recites that by Executive Order No. 10155 of August 25, 1950 the President, through the Secretary of the Army, assumed possession, control and operation of those carriers' transportation systems. Invoking the Constitution and laws, including section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, and subject to that section, it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute. Its operative text then has three more sentences: a sentence that nothing in the order shall be construed to derogate from the authority of the Secretary of the Army under Executive Order No. 10155; "The Board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order."; and a sentence requiring the Board, in performing its functions, to comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended. Inventory: the dossier split the order into two clauses at the number 10155, which ends the sentence on the Secretary of the Army's authority. The order has no numbered paragraphs, so the inventory is corrected to one whole-order clause from the heading through the Defense Production Act sentence. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10303 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between employees and transportation systems operated by the Secretary of the Army". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10303_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10303_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_502ff45635.txt) is titled as the report of the emergency board created November 6, 1951 by Executive Order 10303, and its title page is dated at Washington, D. C., January 25, 1952. The same report states that the parties obtained an extension of the time for the report after the hearings began late. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records the Executive Order 12553 revocation and a cross-reference between this order and Executive Order 10155. The held-text number search found this number only in the Federal Register text file of the order's own printing and the front matter of the board's report.

The board's held report bears the date January 25, 1952 on its title page; that date is disclosed here as the date on which the order became functionally spent, not as its end. (2) The order acts subject to section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; any period that statute fixes after the report is the statute's own effect and a spent fact, not an end of the order. (3) The Defense Production Act sentence governs how the board performs its functions; the statute is not held in this repository, and the board's functions ended in practice with its report, so no expiry of that statute is claimed as an end. (4) Executive Order 10155 is recited as the basis of federal operation and in the sentence preserving the Secretary of the Army's authority; it predates this order and does not act on it. (5) No instrument before Executive Order 12553 amends, supersedes or revokes the order: the OFR disposition notes record only that revocation and the cross-reference to Executive Order 10155. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"The order's operative text has four elements: the creation of the board subject to section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the sentence preserving the Secretary of the Army's authority under Executive Order 10155, the thirty-day report command, and the Defense Production Act compliance sentence. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10306 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10306_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10306_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_97b6e5c39e.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated February 14, 1952; the board states that the President, on December 13, 1951, extended its time to January 15, 1952 and later granted a further extension directing it to file its report by February 15, 1952 (the date of the further extension is not stated). The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking February 14, 1952 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on February 14, 1952 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to March 15, 1952 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. No earlier end is shown in held evidence. Extension of the report deadline: the held National Mediation Board report copy (a held text lead, not an authenticated original, so it cannot be registered as a later-event source in this sheet) states that the President extended the report time on December 13, 1951 to January 15, 1952; the extension moves the report deadline and is not an end, and it is disclosed here and not entered as a later event.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10306 at 16 FR 11709 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed November 15, 1951; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the November 20, 1951 issue. Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 3795 to 6308 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence. Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company and certain other carriers designated in a list A attached to the order, carriers under Federal management, and certain workers represented by the seventeen cooperating (non-operating) railway labor organizations designated in a list B attached to the order, and that the President had assumed possession, control and operation of the carriers' transportation systems through the Secretary of the Army under Executive Order No. 10155 of August 25, 1950. Acting under the Constitution and the laws, including section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; states that nothing in the order is to be construed to derogate from the authority of the Secretary of the Army under Executive Order No. 10155 (the order under which the President had assumed possession of these carriers' transportation systems through the Secretary of the Army); it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; permits the board, to the extent it deems necessary or desirable, to make separate and independent findings with respect to each carrier involved; and directs that, in performing its functions under the order, the board comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended. It contains no sentence imposing a status-quo standstill on the carriers or employees. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10306 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10306_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10306_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_97b6e5c39e.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated February 14, 1952; the board states that the President, on December 13, 1951, extended its time to January 15, 1952 and later granted a further extension directing it to file its report by February 15, 1952 (the date of the further extension is not stated). The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking February 14, 1952 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on February 14, 1952 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to March 15, 1952 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10314 with a subject line describing an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute. The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer); this is not an until-date, so no inclusive or exclusive reading arises. The thirty-day report deadline and the statutory period after the report are not ends; the board's report is dated February 16, 1952 (held report title page), after which the order was functionally spent but remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Pan American World Airways, Inc., 
a carrier, and certain of its employees 
represented by the Transport Workers 
Union of America, CIO, a labor organi­
zation; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce, to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I  hereby create a board of

rier.'

way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President,, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Pan American World Air­
ways, Inc., or its employees in the con­
ditions out of which the said dispute 
arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10314 at 16 FR 12709, in the Federal Register of December 19, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10314 and is signed December 17, 1951. Text: the order recites a dispute between the Pan American World Airways, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, CIO; invoking section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute, and provides that no member may be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier. It directs that "The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order."; requires the board, in performing its functions, to comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and, as provided by section 10 of the Act, states that from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board has reported "no change, except by agreement, shall be made" by the company or its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Inventory: one whole-order clause, from the heading through the last operative sentence, confirmed against the held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10314 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10314_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10314_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_522918d862.txt) is titled as the report of the emergency board appointed on January 9, 1952 pursuant to Executive Order 10314, and its title page is dated at New York, February 16, 1952; the report states that the parties stipulated to extend the time for the report to February 18, 1952 and that the President approved the extension. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12553 revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in the front matter of the board's report.

(1) The thirty-day report requirement is a deadline, not an end; the held report records an approved extension to February 18, 1952, and its title page is dated February 16, 1952. That date is disclosed here as the date on which the order became functionally spent, not as its end. (2) The thirty-day period after the report during which no change could be made except by agreement comes from section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; the held sources do not show when the President received the report, so no exact end of that period is asserted, and its running out is a spent fact, not an end. (3) The Defense Production Act sentence governs how the board performs its functions; the statute is not held in this repository, and the board's functions ended in practice with its report, so no expiry of that statute is claimed as an end. (4) No instrument before Executive Order 12553 amends, supersedes or revokes the order: the OFR disposition notes record only that revocation. No earlier end is shown, so none is claimed.","independent_command_check":"The order's operative text has four elements: the creation of the board with the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report command, the Defense Production Act compliance sentence, and the sentence on unchanged conditions. None is independent of the board: the compliance sentence is a condition on how the board works, and the sentence on unchanged conditions opens by stating that it is made as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, so its force comes from that statute. All share the order's end.","savings_check":"The enacting sentence of Executive Order 12553 contains no saving or exception clause, and the ACT record for this pair lists none. The board's investigation, its report and any settlement that followed are completed past events, not continuing commands of this order; the order created no appointment, transfer or right that survives it, and no held source shows any continuing effect.","scope_check":"Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, its table row matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence has no exception, so it reaches the whole order. The order has no amendment in the held corpus."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10319, signed 1952-01-04 (17 FR 188), recites a dispute between the Northwest Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees represented by the International Association of Machinists, and under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute. Its four operative sentences are: the creation sentence, with the rule that no member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; the direction that the board report its findings to the President "within thirty days from the date" of the order; the direction that "the board shall comply with the" requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and the status-quo sentence, which, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, bars any change except by agreement in the conditions out of which the dispute arose from the date of the order until thirty days after the board reports. The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. Later event: the National Mediation Board's held record for Emergency Board No. 100 states that the parties returned to direct negotiations, which resulted in an agreement dated April 24, 1952, that no effort was made to name the board members, that the board "functioned until said agreement was reached", and that no report to the President was made. The board was therefore never constituted and never reported; the agreement of 1952-04-24 is recorded as a spent fact, and the order is disclosed as functionally spent on 1952-04-24. Under the owner rulings of 2026-10-21 (report deadlines; a board never constituted) the order nevertheless stayed on the books until its express revocation. The three thirty-day extensions of reporting time named in the same record are disclosed without dates, because neither their dates nor any extension instrument is held; an extension of a deadline is not an end. The record is held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10319_Report_of_the_emergency_board_created_by_EO_10319_of_January_4_1952_Northwest_Airline_121b7de808.txt; it is pinned here by path and quotation because the claim kit's working-text gate treats a report file registered under this order's number as a copy of the order itself and refuses it as an event or note source while the official order text is held. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and" "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" Its table on page 10 of the held text prints this order as the one-line row "10319 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute", which agrees with the order's title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective and take effect; the only hit is a word inside another order's subject line), so the signing date, 1986-02-25, is recorded; the filing date 1986-02-26 (the held text prints "Filed 2-26-86") and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 are the alternative readings, and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Northwest Airlines, Inc., a carrier, 
and certain of its employees represented 
by the International Association of Ma­
chinists, a labor organization; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of essen­
tial transportation service;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by ifie, to 
investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of employees,or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
In performing its functions under this 
order the board shall comply with the 
requirements of section 502 of the De­
fense i Production Act of 1950, as 
amended.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Northwest Airlines, Inc., or 
its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10319 (17 FR 188, Federal Register of January 8, 1952; the govinfo PDF text layer), headed Executive Order 10319, signed by Harry S. Truman and dated January 4, 1952; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier listed seventeen clauses, but sixteen of them are fee-schedule paragraphs (spirits of turpentine, rosin, drums, tank cars) of a Department of Agriculture naval-stores rule printed on the same Federal Register page after the order. I replace them with one whole-order clause running from the heading to the sentence ending "dispute arose." The order has three recitals and four operative sentences: the creation of a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act with the rule that no member be interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; the direction to report within thirty days from the date of the order; the direction that the board comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 of the Railway Labor Act. The order does not mention any other Executive order or any officer other than the President. Later facts: the National Mediation Board's held record for Emergency Board No. 100 (PEB-100-Report.pdf) states that the board members were never named because the parties returned to direct negotiations, that the President granted three thirty-day extensions of time, that the parties reached an agreement dated April 24, 1952, and that no report to the President was made. The agreement date is recorded here as a spent fact and the order is disclosed as functionally spent on 1952-04-24; The record is held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10319_Report_of_the_emergency_board_created_by_EO_10319_of_January_4_1952_Northwest_Airline_121b7de808.txt; it is pinned here by path and quotation because the claim kit's working-text gate treats a report file registered under this order's number as a copy of the order itself and refuses it as an event or note source while the official order text is held.  the board was never constituted (owner rulings of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines and on a board never constituted). Ending: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 revokes the order by number. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the revocation note on this order naming EO 12553 and the matching note on EO 12553 naming this order. The held-text number-citation scan in the packet lookups found no other held text citing 10319.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) The thirty-day report deadline is a deadline and not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines); here no report was ever made, according to the National Mediation Board record. (2) The three thirty-day extensions of reporting time named in that record extended the deadline only; their dates and instruments are not held, and an extension is not an end. (3) The status-quo period runs, by the order's own words, until thirty days after the board reports; no report was made, and the dispute was settled by agreement on April 24, 1952, so the order was functionally spent on that date but stayed on the books (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on a board never constituted: treat it like the other emergency-board orders until express revocation). (4) The section 502 compliance sentence is a condition on how the board performs its functions; the Defense Production Act is not held in this packet and no expiry of it is claimed as an end. (5) The OFR catalog and the number-citation scan show no instrument other than EO 12553 that revokes, supersedes or amends this order. No earlier end is shown.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command independent of the board: the report direction and the section 502 compliance direction concern the board's work, and the status-quo sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, whose force comes from that statute and which ran only until thirty days after a report. The order creates no office, fund, delegation or right that outlived the board.","savings_check":"No savings or exception wording attaches to the EO 12553 revocation list. The settlement of the dispute is a completed private agreement, not a residual effect of the order.","scope_check":"EO 12553 revokes the order by number with no exception and reaches any amendments, so the single whole-order clause ends in full on that date. No amendment of the order is held."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 attaches no savings or exception clause to its revocation list (its enacting provision is one sentence followed by the table). The board was never constituted and made no report; the dispute was settled by the parties' own agreement of April 24, 1952, which is not a command of this order. No continuing right or duty arising from the order is shown.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10371
Creating an E mergency  B oard T o I nves ­
tigate a D ispute  B etween  the  T rans
W orld A irlines , I nc., and C ertain  op
I ts E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Trans World Airlines, Inc., a carrier, 
and certain of its employees represented 
by the Plight Engineers’  International 
Association, TWA Chapter, a labor 
organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
T J . S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No 
member of the said board shall be 
pecuniarily or otherwise interested in 
any organization of employees or any 
carrier.
The Board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Trans World Airlines, Inc., 
or its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.
In performing its functions under this 
order the Board shall comply with the 
requirements of section 502 of the De­
fense Production Act of 1950, as 
amended.

research_rationale:
EO 10371 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline , a Defense Production Act section 502 compliance direction and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The board's report date 1952-08-29 is a spent fact recorded in the clause reason. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.

research_rationale:
EO 10372 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline , a Defense Production Act section 502 compliance direction and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The board's report date 1952-08-29 is a spent fact recorded in the clause reason. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Checked for an earlier end: (1) the order's own terms contain a report deadline and a post-report standstill but no sunset, so the report and standstill dates are spent facts and not ends under the report-deadline ruling; (2) no extension, amendment or revocation of EO 10372 other than EO 12553 appears in the dossier chain or in the number-citation scan of held texts; the report-time extensions described in the held report (where a report is held) were stipulations approved by the President, not held instruments, and affect only the deadline; (3) a general later rule is not treated as an end, only EO 12553, which names the order by number.","independent_command_check":"The standstill is recited as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, so any no-change duty it describes arises under that statute and not only from the order; by the order's own terms it ran only to thirty days after the board's report, which was long before 1986. The order creates no continuing right, office or appropriation. No other command in the order survives the board's report.","savings_check":"The text of EO 12553 contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording (the held text was searched for those terms). The board's investigation, report and the standstill were spent in the 1950s, and the order created no accrued right or later-effective duty. The statute the order invokes is not affected by revoking the order.","scope_check":"One clause covers the whole order; the order has no partial-scope command, no exception and no delayed effective date. The revocation in EO 12553 has no exception text, so it reaches the whole order."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: the order's single operative sentence amends sec. 403 of EO 10161 by redesignating para. (b) as (c) and inserting a new para. (b) providing up to two labor and two industry alternate members of the Wage Stabilization Board (held FR text 17 FR 7995, offsets 794-2450). First end: EO 10480 sec. 607(11), 1953-08-14, which names EO 10390 by number and date; EO 10480 sec. 607(1) also supersedes the parent EO 10161 in the same sentence. The order has no term, sunset or condition of its own. Disclosed earlier candidates (not ends under the 2026-10-21 unnamed-instruments ruling, because none names EO 10390): (a) EO 10434 of 1953-02-06 (held, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10434.txt, para. 1 at offset 1715) suspends 'All regulations and orders issued pursuant to the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, stabilizing wages, salaries, and other compensation'; it does not name EO 10390 or EO 10161 and does not abolish the Board or its alternate-member paragraph; (b) EO 10467 of 1953-06-30 sec. 1 (held, EO_10467.txt offsets 3783-4200) keeps DPA delegation orders in force only 'with respect to such of the said functions as are continued by the Defense Production Act Amendments of 1953'; if those Amendments did not continue Title IV wage stabilization, the alternate-member paragraph may have been displaced from 1953-06-30 or the Title IV expiry; the Amendments are not held (FETCH_QUEUE line 317 already requests them); EO 10467 does not name EO 10390. Neither is an end under the ruling; both are disclosed for the human reviewer. No later amendment of the inserted para. 403(b) was found: EO 10433 sec. 2 (1953-02-04) rewrites only sec. 401(a) of EO 10161. No later event is attached.

By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Defense Production Act of 1950, 
as amended (50 U. S. C. App. 2061 et 
seq.), and as President of the United 
States, it is ordered that section 403 of 
Executive Order No. 10161 of September 
9, 1950 (15 P. R. 6105), as amended, be, 
and it is hereby, further amended by 
redesignating paragraph (b) thereof as 
paragraph (c) and by inserting im­
mediately after paragraph (a) thereof 
the following new paragraph:
“(b) In addition to the members of 
the Wage Stabilization Board provided 
for in section 403 (a) of this order, the 
Board shall have not more than two 
alternate members who shall be repre­
sentative of labor and not more than 
two alternate members who shall be 
representative of business and industry. 
Alternate members shall be appointed 
by the President, by and with the advice 
and consent of the Senate, at such times 
as he may deem necessary. Any alter­
nate member shall participate as a mem­
ber of the Board only in lieu of a member 
appointed under section 403 (a) of this 
order who is not participating, and only 
when called upon by the Chairman of the 
Wage Stabilization Board to so partici­
pate, and when so participating each 
alternate member shall have the same 
status and functions as a member ap­
pointed under the said section 403 (a). 
The designation by the Chairman of the 
Board of alternate members to partici­
pate as members of the Board shall be 
so ordered as to preserve the equal rep- ' 
resentation required by the provisions of 
section 403 (a) hereof and of section 
403 (b) of the Defense Production Act 
of 1950, as amended.”
x  Harry S. T ruman

The dossier's single clause covers the whole operative text to the signature. Ending: EO 10480 (signed 1953-08-14, 18 FR 4939-4944) sec. 607 supersedes or revokes '(11) Executive Order No. 10390 of August 30, 1952 (17 F. R. 7995)' (held FR text EO_10480.txt offsets 39234-39302) and its parent EO 10161 (item (1)); no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 1953-08-14. The ACT record cited is APP-sourced; its wording matches the held FR text except the APP year misprint '1962'. D6: dossier chain (only EO 10480), ACT provisions (three EO 10480 records, same sec. 607), draft later-event proposals (EO 10480 only), OFR catalog note 'Superseded by: EO 10480, August 14, 1953', by-number scan of the held FR texts, and the held EO 10161-related orders of 1952-1953 (EO 10433, 10434, 10461, 10467). Earlier candidates disclosed, not ends (unnamed-instruments ruling 2026-10-21): EO 10434 (1953-02-06, wage-control suspension, does not touch the alternate-member paragraph) and EO 10467 sec. 1 with the unheld Defense Production Act Amendments of 1953 (possible statutory displacement of Title IV functions from mid-1953; FETCH_QUEUE line 317). The 2026-10-20 Lambertini i04 review rejected an earlier claim for this order because that claim called the EO 10480 date an upper bound while listing no gap; under the 2026-10-21 ruling the end is the naming instrument (EO 10480) and the statutory lead is a disclosed candidate only. Conflicts: none listed. Savings: transferred_or_accrued under EO 10480 sec. 606. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

Actions already taken under EO 10161 sec. 403(b) as inserted by EO 10390 (appointments of alternate members, their participation) keep their validity; the alternate-member rule itself is not re-enacted by EO 10480, and EO 10480 sec. 605 continues the Economic Stabilization Agency only to October 31, 1953 for winding up. No command in the order has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. The thirty-day report period and the post-report standstill are timing provisions, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C). The held National Mediation Board report for this board (Emergency Board No. 103; jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10406_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10406_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_0afc851ff8.txt) bears the cover date JANUARY 2,1953 (date line at offsets 1147-1161 of that held text), so the board's reporting command was functionally spent on 1953-01-02. The report states that, before the hearings closed, the parties agreed to a 30-day extension of the time limit stated in the Executive order and that on December 1, 1952 the President approved it (report text offsets 4991-5200); its letter of transmittal is also dated January 2, 1953. The extension approvals are not held instruments and bear only on the report deadline. The thirty-day standstill that the order recites ran, by its own terms, for thirty days after the report, that is to 1953-02-01 (computed, not stated in a held source); that period also ended long before 1986. Both dates are spent facts, not ends. Creating an E mergency B oard T o I n ­
vestigate a D ispute  B etween  the

WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the United Air Lines, Inc., a carrier, and 
certain of its employees represented by 
the Flight Engineers’  International As­
sociation, UAL Chapter, a labor organi­
zation; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions

interstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:

authority vested in me by section 10 of
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of

change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the United Air Lines, Inc., or its 
employees in the conditions out of which 
the said dispute arose.

order the Board shall comply with the 
requirements of section 502 of the De­
fense Production Act of 1950, as 
amended.

research_rationale:
EO 10406 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline , a Defense Production Act section 502 compliance direction and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The board's report date 1953-01-02 is a spent fact recorded in the clause reason. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 845-1416 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10415.txt, 17 FR 10899): signed 1952-12-02; amends Executive Order 9949 (a one-person order of April 17, 1948 modifying paragraph 3(a) of Executive Order 9721 for a named Federal Communications Commission employee transferring to the International Frequency Registration Board) by striking the words that limit his reemployment rights to service terminated within five years from the date of his transfer and inserting a limit of on or before December 31, 1953. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments (option B), the amendment is a clause that continues, as amended, until the parent order ends; the parent EO 9949 is itself named in the EO 12553 table (offset 5212 of the held EO 12553 text), as is EO 9721 (offset 1105). The December 31, 1953 date limits the time within which the employee's service had to end to qualify; it is a condition deadline written into the clause, not an end of the order, and is treated as functionally spent on 1953-12-31 by analogy to the report-deadline ruling (owner ruling 2026-10-21, option C). Alternative reading, disclosed for the reviewer: the clause could be read to lapse by its own terms after 1953-12-31 because the modified condition could no longer be met by a later termination; the held evidence does not show whether the employee's service ended before that date or whether any reemployment right accrued, so no earlier end is established. Earlier candidate end under the unnamed-instruments ruling (owner ruling 2026-10-21, option C): Executive Order 10804, signed 1959-02-12 (held text jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_10804.txt, section 2 at offsets 1193-2145), revoked Executive Order 9721 and Executive Order 10103 except for employees then serving with an international organization and for rights vested before the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act; it does not name EO 9949 or EO 10415, so it is not treated as their end. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10415 appears in the table's column of order numbers at offset 10390 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The board's report date 1954-02-17 is a spent fact recorded in the clause reason. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.

research_rationale:
EO 10511 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The board's report date 1954-05-15 is a spent fact recorded in the clause reason. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Checked for an earlier end: (1) the order's own terms contain a report deadline and a post-report standstill but no sunset, so the report and standstill dates are spent facts and not ends under the report-deadline ruling; (2) no extension, amendment or revocation of EO 10511 other than EO 12553 appears in the dossier chain or in the number-citation scan of held texts; the report-time extensions described in the held report (where a report is held) were stipulations approved by the President, not held instruments, and affect only the deadline; (3) a general later rule is not treated as an end, only EO 12553, which names the order by number.","independent_command_check":"The standstill is recited as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, so any no-change duty it describes arises under that statute and not only from the order; by the order's own terms it ran only to thirty days after the board's report, which was long before 1986. The order creates no continuing right, office or appropriation. No other command in the order survives the board's report.","savings_check":"The text of EO 12553 contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording (the held text was searched for those terms). The board's investigation, report and the standstill were spent in the 1950s, and the order created no accrued right or later-effective duty. The statute the order invokes is not affected by revoking the order.","scope_check":"One clause covers the whole order; the order has no partial-scope command, no exception and no delayed effective date. The revocation in EO 12553 has no exception text, so it reaches the whole order."}

savings_residuals.reason: The text of EO 12553 contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording (the held text was searched for those terms). The board's investigation, report and the standstill were spent in the 1950s, and the order created no accrued right or later-effective duty. The statute the order invokes is not affected by revoking the order.

research_rationale: EO 10622 (signed 1955-07-01, 20 FR 4762, FR issue of 1955-07-06; held official FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10622.txt read in full) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate a dispute between the Railway Express Agency and employees represented by the Teamsters, orders a report within thirty days, and restates the statutory standstill. The FR page prints a Civil Service Commission Part 6 amendment in the neighbouring column (offsets 1552-2618); the dossier's machine clauses mixed it in, so the inventory is corrected by three inventory_overrides covering the whole operative text (offsets 2884-3247, 3248-3384, 3385-3705); the recitals are not operative. Rulings applied: report deadline (2026-10-21; a board order ends on express revocation, and the report date and standstill end are recorded as spent later events with a 'functionally spent' note), unnamed instruments (end is the instrument naming the order). The board report is held (PEB-111-Report.pdf, nmb.gov, jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10622_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10622_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_e26d59e5ee.txt): transmittal dated August 1, 1955 (offsets 1235-1251); the standstill therefore ran through August 31, 1955 (inclusive reading; alternative August 30). First and whole-order end: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237; held text offsets 691-966; '10622' at offset 10521; no effective-date wording, so effective on signing). D6: the dossier chain, actor provisions and missing list name only EO 12553; the draft's later-event proposals name only EO 12553 (OFR catalog and 1989 Codification); the by-number scan finds no other acting instrument. No conflicts were listed. Functionally spent on 1955-08-31; on the books until 1986-02-25. Savings: none_after_bounded_search. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 1616-3177 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10630.txt, 20 FR 5911): signed 1955-08-13; creates under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the New York Central System, Lines East, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen; directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and recites that, as provided by section 10 of that Act, from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board's report no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the parties in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. No command in the order has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. The thirty-day report period and the post-report standstill are timing provisions, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadline, option C). The held National Mediation Board report for this board (Emergency Board No. 112; jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10630_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10630_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_814b8eb677.txt) bears the cover date SEPTEMBER 14, 1955 (date line at offsets 1176-1194 of that held text), so the board's reporting command was functionally spent on 1955-09-14. The held front-matter excerpt of the report records no extension of the time limit; its letter of transmittal bears the same city and a September date whose day is OCR-damaged. The extension approvals are not held instruments and bear only on the report deadline. The thirty-day standstill that the order recites ran, by its own terms, for thirty days after the report, that is to 1955-10-14 (computed, not stated in a held source); that period also ended long before 1986. Both dates are spent facts, not ends. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986), which orders that the Executive Orders in its table, and any amendments thereto, are revoked. The number 10630 appears in the table at offset 10528 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt in the column of order numbers (the held OCR prints the numbers and the subjects in separate blocks, so identification rests on the number). EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, February 25, 1986; the filing date (2-26-86) and the printing date are not effective dates. No earlier instrument is shown: the dossier chain for this order contains only EO 12553 and the number-citation scan lists no other later order that revokes, amends, extends or supersedes it.

research_rationale:
EO 10630 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The board's report date 1955-09-14 is a spent fact recorded in the clause reason. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Checked for an earlier end: (1) the order's own terms contain a report deadline and a post-report standstill but no sunset, so the report and standstill dates are spent facts and not ends under the report-deadline ruling; (2) no extension, amendment or revocation of EO 10630 other than EO 12553 appears in the dossier chain or in the number-citation scan of held texts; the report-time extensions described in the held report (where a report is held) were stipulations approved by the President, not held instruments, and affect only the deadline; (3) a general later rule is not treated as an end, only EO 12553, which names the order by number.","independent_command_check":"The standstill is recited as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, so any no-change duty it describes arises under that statute and not only from the order; by the order's own terms it ran only to thirty days after the board's report, which was long before 1986. The order creates no continuing right, office or appropriation. No other command in the order survives the board's report.","savings_check":"The text of EO 12553 contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording (the held text was searched for those terms). The board's investigation, report and the standstill were spent in the 1950s, and the order created no accrued right or later-effective duty. The statute the order invokes is not affected by revoking the order.","scope_check":"One clause covers the whole order; the order has no partial-scope command, no exception and no delayed effective date. The revocation in EO 12553 has no exception text, so it reaches the whole order."}

Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10635 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10635_Emergency_Board_report_to_the_President_Pennsylvania_Railroad_and_Transport_Workers_U_4282a7bfa7.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated October 26, 1955; the board states that by stipulation of the parties the time for making the report was extended to October 31, 1955. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking October 26, 1955 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on October 26, 1955 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to November 25, 1955 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. No earlier end is shown in held evidence. This is the first part of the order's operative text (the enacting words).
