research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10635 at 20 FR 6485 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed September 1, 1955; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the September 2, 1955 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3901 to 4520 and 11882 to 12075 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Pennsylvania Railroad, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, C.I.O., Railroad Division, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Pennsylvania Railroad or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10635 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10635_Emergency_Board_report_to_the_President_Pennsylvania_Railroad_and_Transport_Workers_U_4282a7bfa7.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated October 26, 1955; the board states that by stipulation of the parties the time for making the report was extended to October 31, 1955. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking October 26, 1955 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on October 26, 1955 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to November 25, 1955 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10643 at 20 FR 8359 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed November 7, 1955; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the November 9, 1955 issue. Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 638 to 3187 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence (the sentence barring changes in conditions). Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the Albany Port District Railroad and other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees, designated in lists A and C attached to the order, and certain of their employees represented by the cooperating (non-operating) railway labor organizations designated in lists B and D attached to the order, on wage demands and on demands for changes in health and welfare agreements. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Albany Port District Railroad and other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10643 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10643_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10643_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_84f930ce02.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated December 12, 1955; the board states that, upon stipulation of the parties, the President extended the time for filing the report to December 12, 1955. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking December 12, 1955 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on December 12, 1955 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to January 11, 1956 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.

The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing, the National Mediation Board report copy. The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10693, signed 1956-12-22 (21 FR 10325), creates under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act a board of three members to investigate the disputes between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad and other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees (listed in the attachment printed after the signature) and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen; directs the board to report its findings to the President "within thirty days from the date" of the order; and provides, as section 10 of that Act provides, that from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board's report no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the parties in the conditions out of which the disputes arose. No command has its own fixed end date, sunset or termination clause. Later event: the held report of Emergency Board No. 116, created by this order, is dated "MARCH 15, 1957" on its cover, and its letter of transmittal to the President bears the same date and states that the board "has the honor to submit its report herewith." I record 1957-03-15 as the report date (a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report). On that date the thirty-day status-quo period after the report ran through 1957-04-14 (inclusive reading; the exclusive reading ends it when that day begins), and the order was functionally spent on 1957-04-14. Both are spent facts and not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, both dates recorded). The report text is held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10693_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10693_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_c19da2b877.txt; it is pinned here by path and quotation because the claim kit's working-text gate treats a report file registered under this order's number as a copy of the order itself and refuses it as an event or note source while the official order text is held. First end: Executive Order 12553, Revocation of Various Executive Orders, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and" "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The number 10693 appears in the table on page 11 of the held text (offset 10583). On that page the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards; 10693 is entry 34 of 64 and entry 34 of the subject list is "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes", which agrees with the order's title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it against the page image. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective and take effect; the only hit is a word inside another order's subject line), so the signing date, 1986-02-25, is recorded; the filing date 1986-02-26 (the held text prints "Filed 2-26-86") and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 are the alternative readings, and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

WHEREAS disputes exist between the  
Akron &  Barberton Belt Railroad and  
other carriers represented by the Eastern,  
western and Southeastern Carriers'  
Conference Committees, designated in
list attached hereto and made a part  
hereof, and certain of their employees  
represented by the Brotherhood of Rail­
road Trainmen, a labor organization;  
and
WHEREAS these disputes have not  
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Hoard,  
threaten substantially to interrupt inter­
state commerce to a degree such as to  
deprive the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me, to  
investigate the said disputes. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily  
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said  
disputes within thirty days from the date  
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Akron &  Barberton Belt  
Railroad Company and other carriers  
represented by the Eastern, Western and  
Southeastern Carriers’  Conference Com­
mittees or their employees in the condi­
tions out of which the said disputes arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10693 (21 FR 10325, Federal Register of December 27, 1956), signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower and dated December 22, 1956; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: one whole-order clause covers the heading, the three recitals and the three operative sentences: creation of a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the disputes between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad and other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen; the direction to report within thirty days from the date of the order; and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 of the Railway Labor Act. The list of carriers that the recitals incorporate is printed after the signature and continues on later pages; it identifies parties and states no command. The order contains no Defense Production Act sentence and no other command. Later facts: the packet holds the National Mediation Board's report of Emergency Board No. 116 (PEB-116-Report.pdf, front matter and transmittal letter), dated March 15, 1957 on its cover and on its letter of transmittal to the President. The report date is recorded here as a spent fact; the thirty-day period after a report made on that date ran through 1957-04-14 (inclusive reading), and the order is disclosed as functionally spent on 1957-04-14 (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, both dates recorded). The report text is held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10693_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10693_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_c19da2b877.txt; it is pinned here by path and quotation because the claim kit's working-text gate treats a report file registered under this order's number as a copy of the order itself and refuses it as an event or note source while the official order text is held. Ending: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 revokes the order by number. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): the U.S. Code release point 119-121 and eCFR searches record no citation of this order; the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (two machine hits) are the revocation note on this order naming EO 12553 and the matching note on EO 12553. The held-text number-citation scan found the number only on the order's own Federal Register page.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10709 at 22 FR 3309 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed May 9, 1957; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the May 11, 1957 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3442 to 3599 and 11071 to 11840 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Toledo, Lorain & Fairport Dock Company, the Toledo Lakefront Dock Company and the Cleveland Stevedore Company, carriers, and certain of their employees represented by District 50, United Mine Workers of America, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the three dock companies or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10709 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a dock company labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10709_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10709_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_ee5c57b97f.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated June 7, 1957. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking June 7, 1957 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on June 7, 1957 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to July 7, 1957 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.

The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing, the National Mediation Board report copy. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. research_rationale:
EO 10749 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10750, signed 1958-01-28, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between Eastern Air Lines, Inc., and employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("thirty days after the Board"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10750_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10750_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_c69ca7f6fc.txt) gives the date 1958-07-21 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1958-07-21, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1958-08-20, and the order was functionally spent on 1958-08-20 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10750 at character offset 10644 as entry 44 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 44 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10757, signed 1958-02-27, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between seven airlines (Eastern, Trans World, United, Northwest, Northeast, Capital and National) and employees represented by the International Association of Machinists. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10757_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10757_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_22203830f5.txt) gives the date 1958-09-15 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1958-09-15, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1958-10-15, and the order was functionally spent on 1958-10-15 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10757 at character offset 10651 as entry 45 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 45 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10760_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10760_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_b9c925cf50.txt) gives the date 1958-07-25 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1958-07-25, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1958-08-24, and the order was functionally spent on 1958-08-24 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10760 at character offset 10658 as entry 46 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 46 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

EO 10760 is a Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency-board order with provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed the order’s identity from its heading and number, and confirmed a single-clause inventory. It has no own-terms end. The only held instrument that revokes it is EO 12553 (1986-02-25), which I read; the report date and the end of the status-quo period are disclosed spent facts, not ends. The searches chosen (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) carry no coverage warning and show no hit for this order that contradicts the ending.

The order’s own terms contain only the report direction and the status-quo period, which are report-relative deadlines and not ends. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10770, signed 1958-06-19, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between American Airlines, Incorporated, and employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. No held text gives the actual date of this board’s report, so neither the report date nor the end of the thirty-day period after it is established from held evidence; the claim does not depend on them because a report deadline and a status-quo period are not ends (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The dossier holds no located acting-provision record for this pair, so the cited source is the whole held Federal Register text of EO 12553 (the dossier’s actor context); its enacting sentence says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10770 at character offset 10665 as entry 47 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 47 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
EO 10770 is a Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency-board order with provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed the order’s identity from its heading and number, and confirmed a single-clause inventory. It has no own-terms end. The only held instrument that revokes it is EO 12553 (1986-02-25), which I read; the report date and the end of the status-quo period are disclosed spent facts, not ends. The searches chosen (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) carry no coverage warning and show no hit for this order that contradicts the ending.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Searched for an end earlier than 1986-02-25. The order’s own terms contain only the report direction and the status-quo period, which are report-relative deadlines and not ends. The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md finds this number cited only in the order’s own held texts, in the NMB report text where one is held, and in EO 12553. No held later order other than EO 12553 revokes, supersedes, amends or terminates it, and no statute held in the packet does so; an unnamed statute or order would in any case not end it (owner ruling 2026-10-21 unnamed instruments). The dossier’s conflicts and missing lists are empty or concern only a number citation without a change provision (no held text gives the actual report date).","independent_command_check":"No independent command survives: the board’s creation was performed when the order issued; the report direction and the status-quo period are time-limited by the order itself and by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; the order creates no standing office, delegation, rule or continuing duty that would outlast the report and the thirty-day period. Those spent commands nonetheless remained formally in the order until EO 12553, and the order is recorded as ending on revocation under the owner’s report-deadline ruling.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no saving, exception or pending-matters language: a search of the whole held text for except, notwithstanding, nothing in, saving, pending and similar words found only incidental uses inside other orders’ subject lines. The board’s report and any agreement or later change in working conditions between the parties are accrued consequences that rest on the Railway Labor Act and the parties’ own acts, not on this order, and none keeps the order operative.","scope_check":"The whole order is covered: EO 12553 revokes listed orders \"and any amendments thereto\" with no exception, so no part of this one-paragraph order was left in force. The clause inventory is one clause (the whole order); I read the held text and confirm that it contains the creation, report and status-quo commands and nothing else operative."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10811 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10811_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10811_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_baa6c6b760.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated June 15, 1959 and a letter of transmittal dated Washington, D.C., June 12, 1959; the board states that the parties agreed to extend the time for the report to June 15, 1959. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking June 15, 1959 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on June 15, 1959 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to July 15, 1959 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. No earlier end is shown in held evidence. This is the first part of the order's operative text (the enacting words).

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10811 at 24 FR 3179 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed April 22, 1959; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the April 24, 1959 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 4297 to 4413 and 13450 to 14152 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Pan American World Airways, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO, Air Transport Division, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars Pan American World Airways, Inc., or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10811 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10811_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10811_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_baa6c6b760.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated June 15, 1959 and a letter of transmittal dated Washington, D.C., June 12, 1959; the board states that the parties agreed to extend the time for the report to June 15, 1959. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking June 15, 1959 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on June 15, 1959 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to July 15, 1959 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing, the National Mediation Board report copy and in the printing of Executive Order 10810, on whose Federal Register page this order's heading also appears; none of those texts acts on this order. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10862, signed 1960-02-12, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway Company--Coast Lines and certain of its employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10862_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10862_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_e38f8f604e.txt) gives the date 1960-07-15 on its cover (the letter of transmittal’s year is misread by the text layer as 1980, an apparent recognition error); a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1960-07-15, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1960-08-14, and the order was functionally spent on 1960-08-14 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10862 at character offset 10715 as entry 55 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 55 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 10862
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN THE ATCHISON, TOPEKA  
AND SANTA FE RAILWAY COM­
PANY— COAST LINES AND CER­
TAIN OF ITS EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Rail­
way Company— Coast Lines, a carrier,  
and certain of its employees represented 
by the Brotherhood of Locomotive En­
gineers, a labor organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to  
deprive a section of the country of es­
sential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate this dispute. No member  
of the board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization  
of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the dispute  
within thirty days from the date of this  
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Atchison, Topeka and Santa  
Fe Railway Company— Coast Lines, or by 
its employees, in the conditions out of  
which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10874, signed 1960-04-18, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Long Island Railroad Company and certain of its employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10874_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10874_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_d2e83e92e5.txt) gives the date 1960-05-18 on its letter of transmittal (the cover’s year is misread by the text layer as 1969, an apparent recognition error); a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1960-05-18, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1960-06-17, and the order was functionally spent on 1960-06-17 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10874 at character offset 10733 as entry 58 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 58 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (25 FR 3567, the issue of April 26, 1960) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 10875, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated April 22, 1960. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by May 22, 1960), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 130 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated June 8, 1960; the report's table of contents lists a letter of extension of the time limit. Thirty days after June 8, 1960 is July 8, 1960. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on June 8, 1960, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on July 8, 1960. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10877, signed 1960-05-20, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Pennsylvania Railroad Company and certain of its employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. No held text gives the actual date of this board’s report, so neither the report date nor the end of the thirty-day period after it is established from held evidence; the claim does not depend on them because a report deadline and a status-quo period are not ends (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The dossier holds no located acting-provision record for this pair, so the cited source is the whole held Federal Register text of EO 12553 (the dossier’s actor context); its enacting sentence says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10877 at character offset 10745 as entry 60 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 60 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

Executive Order 10877
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN THE PENNSYLVANIA RAIL­
ROAD COMPANY AND CERTAIN  
OF ITS EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Pennsylvania Railroad Company, a 
carrier, and certain of its employees 
represented by the Transport Workers’ 
Union of America, Railroad Division, 
AFL-CIO, and System Federation No. 
152, Railway Employes’ Department, 
AFL-CIO, labor organizations; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of es­
sential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U.S.C. 160), I  hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member 
of the board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization 
of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the dispute 
within thirty days from the date of this 
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way -Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Pennsylvania Railroad 
Company, or by its employees, in the 
conditions out of which the dispute 
arose.,

I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed the order’s identity from its heading and number, and confirmed a single-clause inventory. It has no own-terms end. The only held instrument that revokes it is EO 12553 (1986-02-25), which I read; the report date and the end of the status-quo period are disclosed spent facts, not ends. The searches chosen (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) carry no coverage warning and show no hit for this order that contradicts the ending.

Those spent commands nonetheless remained formally in the order until EO 12553, and the order is recorded as ending on revocation under the owner’s report-deadline ruling.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no saving, exception or pending-matters language: a search of the whole held text for except, notwithstanding, nothing in, saving, pending and similar words found only incidental uses inside other orders’ subject lines. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10888 in the number column of the table (the text layer separates the number column from the subject column for this part of the table, so its subject text is not quoted). This order (25 FR 9361, Federal Register of September 30, 1960, signed September 28, 1960) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between certain carriers represented by the New York Harbor Carriers' Conference Committee (listed in attached List A) and certain of their employees represented by labor organizations that are members of the Railroad Marine Harbor Council, AFL-CIO (listed in attached List B); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by October 28, 1960); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 133 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated December 10, 1960; the report states that the time for filing it was extended to December 10, 1960 by the President on the consent of the parties. Thirty days after December 10, 1960 is January 9, 1961. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on December 10, 1960, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on January 9, 1961.

Executive Order 10888
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN CERTAIN CARRIERS REP­
RESENTED BY THE NEW YORK  
HARBOR CARRIERS’ CONFERENCE  
COMMITTEE A N D  CERTAIN OF  
THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
certain carriers represented by the New 
York Harbor Carriers’  Conference Com­
mittee, designated in List A attached 
hereto and hereby made a part hereof, 
and certain of their employees repre­
sented by labor organizations, members 
of the Railroad Marine Harbor Council, 
AFL-CIO, designated in List B attached 
hereto and hereby made a part hereof; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended 
(45 U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board 
of three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member 
of the board shall be pecuniarily or other­
wise interested in any organization of 
railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the dispute 
within thirty days from the date of this 
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by carriers represented by the New 
York Harbor Carriers’  Conference Com­
mittee, or by their employees, in the con­
ditions out of which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10904, signed 1961-01-12, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between carriers represented by the New York Harbor Carriers’ Conference Committee and certain of their employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10904_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10904_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_3afb8d1c9a.txt) gives the date 1961-03-06 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1961-03-06, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1961-04-05, and the order was functionally spent on 1961-04-05 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 11 of the held Federal Register text) lists the number 10904 at character offset 10765 as entry 63 of 64; the text layer prints the 64 numbers first and the 64 subjects afterwards, and entry 63 of the subject list is the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. The alignment is by position, not by a printed row, and a reviewer should confirm it. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 10904
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN CERTAIN CARRIERS REP­
RESENTED BY THE NEW YORK  
HARBOR CARRIERS’ CONFERENCE  
COMMITTEE AND CERTAIN OF  
THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
certain carriers represented by the New 
York Harbor Carriers’  Conference Com­
mittee, designated in the List of Carriers 
attached hereto and hereby made a part 
hereof, and certain of their employees 
represented by the Lighter Captains’  
Union, Local 996, I.L.A., a labor organi­
zation; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of es­
sential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U.S.C. 160) , I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member 
of the board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization 
of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the dispute 
within thirty days from the date of this 
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by carriers represented by the 
New York Harbor Carriers’ Conference 
Committee, or by their employees, in the 
conditions out of which the dispute arose.

The dossier’s clause span began mid-sentence at the words "1961. The thirty-day period" and left out the authorizing sentence, so I replaced it with the complete operative text, from "By virtue of the authority" through "provided by this Order." (offsets 827-1362 of the held text). The extension is a report deadline and not an end. The held NMB report text for Emergency Board No. 136 (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10933_Actual_date_of_the_Emergency_Board_No._136_Northwest_Airlines_Inc._created_by_EO_1092_f900c4013d.txt) gives the date May 24, 1961 on its cover and letter of transmittal, the same day as the authorized-before date in this order; a dated letter is not proof of when the President received the report, and the thirty-day period after that date would have run through 1961-06-23. The order was functionally spent by then if the board reported on that date (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded); that is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 12 of the held Federal Register text, outside the cited enacting sentence) lists this order on its own row beginning at character offset 16007: the number 10933 followed by the subject Extending an emergency board to investigate airline labor disputes, which agrees with this order’s own title. EO 12553 also lists EO 10923, the order this one amends. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10951, signed 1961-06-29, is a one-sentence order under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947. It commands one thing: it extends the time within which the board of inquiry created by Executive Order 10949 must report to the President ("I hereby extend until" 9 a.m., July 3, 1961). That is a report deadline, recorded inclusively as running through 9 a.m. on 1961-07-03, with the exclusive reading (the extension ends when that moment begins) as the alternative; it is a deadline and a later event of EO 10949, and it is not an end (owner rulings 2026-10-21 until-dates and report deadline). The order has no termination clause of its own, and no held text gives the date on which the board actually reported, so the order was functionally spent no later than 1961-07-03 only if the board reported by then, which the held evidence does not establish. First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 12 of the held Federal Register text, outside the cited enacting sentence) lists this order on its own row beginning at character offset 16252: the number 10951 followed by the subject Amending Executive Order No. 10949 creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting, which agrees with this order’s own title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10953 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order (26 FR 6578, Federal Register of July 22, 1961, signed July 20, 1961) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines), a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Order of Railroad Telegraphers, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by August 19, 1961); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines) or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 138 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated September 15, 1961. Thirty days after September 15, 1961 is October 15, 1961. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on September 15, 1961, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on October 15, 1961.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10963, signed 1961-09-01, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Pullman Company and the Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul & Pacific Railroad Company and certain of their employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10963_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10963_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_a3eb3dd50c.txt) gives the date 1961-12-11 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1961-12-11, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1962-01-10, and the order was functionally spent on 1962-01-10 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 12 of the held Federal Register text, outside the cited enacting sentence) lists this order on its own row beginning at character offset 16624: the number 10963 followed by the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes, which agrees with this order’s own title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

Executive Order 10963
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE PULLMAN COMPANY  
AND THE CHICAGO, MILWAUKEE,  
ST. PAUL &  PACIFIC RAILROAD  
COMPANY AND CERTAIN OF THEIR  
EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS disputes exist between the  
Pullman Company and the Chicago,  
Milwaukee, St. Paul &  Pacific Railroad  
Company, carriers, and certain of their  
employees represented by the Order of  
Railway Conductors and Brakemen, a  
labor organization; and  
WHEREAS these disputes have not  
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threaten substantially to interrupt inter­
state commerce to a degree such as to  
deprive a section of the country of  
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate these disputes. No mem­
ber of the board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization  
of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to these dis­
putes within thirty days from the date  
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Pullman Company and the  
Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul &  Pacific  
Railroad Company, or by their em­
ployees, in the conditions out of which  
these disputes arose.
