operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10965 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". This order (26 FR 9451, Federal Register of October 7, 1961, signed October 5, 1961) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Trans World Airlines, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by November 4, 1961); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by the Trans World Airlines, Inc. or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 140 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated November 3, 1961; the board's letter of transmittal is dated November 1, 1961 and the printed report cover is dated November 3, 1961, so the report date is disclosed as November 1-3, 1961. Thirty days after November 3, 1961 is December 3, 1961. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on November 3, 1961, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on December 3, 1961.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10969, signed 1961-10-11, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between the Reading Company and certain of its employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. The held NMB report text for this board (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10969_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10969_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_347bde63bb.txt) gives the date 1961-12-05 on its cover and letter of transmittal; a dated transmittal letter is not proof of the day the President received the report, so this is a disclosed spent fact and not an end. If the report was made on 1961-12-05, the thirty-day period after the report ran through 1962-01-04, and the order was functionally spent on 1962-01-04 (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md, both dates recorded). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 12 of the held Federal Register text, outside the cited enacting sentence) lists this order on its own row beginning at character offset 16771: the number 10969 followed by the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 10971, signed 1961-11-01, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between Trans World Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees. Its single paragraph carries three commands that belong to one procedure: creation of the board ("hereby create a board of"), the direction that the board report to the President ("within thirty days from the date"), and the status-quo rule that, from the order’s date and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions out of which the dispute arose is to be made except by agreement ("except by agreement"). The order has no termination clause, fixed end date or revocation clause of its own. The thirty-day report date and the end of the thirty-day period after the report are spent facts and not ends. No held text gives the actual date of this board’s report, so neither the report date nor the end of the thirty-day period after it is established from held evidence; the claim does not depend on them because a report deadline and a status-quo period are not ends (owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-report-deadline.md). First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 12 of the held Federal Register text, outside the cited enacting sentence) lists this order on its own row beginning at character offset 16845: the number 10971 followed by the subject Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute, which agrees with this order’s own title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

Executive Order 10975
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN PAN AMERICAN WORLD
AIRWAYS, INC. AND CERTAIN OF  
ITS EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
Pan American World Airways, Inc. a 
carrier, and certain of its employees rep­
resented by the Air Line Pilots Associa­
tion, International, a labor organization; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by Section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member 
of the board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization 
of airline employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the dispute 
within thirty days from the date of this 
order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by Pan American World Airways, 
Inc. or by its employees, in the condition 
out of which the dispute arose.

§ 403.1 Availability o f peach crop in­
surance.
Peach crop insurance shall be offered 
for the 1062 and succeeding crop years 
under the provision of §  403.1 through 
§  403.6 in counties within limits pre­
scribed by and in accordance with the 
provision of the Federal Crop Insurance 
Act as amended. The counties shall be 
designated by the Manager of the Cor­
poration from a list of counties approved 
by the Board of Directors of the Cor­
poration for peach crop insurance. The 
counties designated by the Manager shall 
be published by appendix to this section.
§ 403.2 Premium rates and amounts of  
insurance.
The Manager shall establish premium 
rates and the amounts of insurance per 
acre which shall be shown on the county 
actuarial table on file in the county of­
fice. Such premium rates and amounts 
of insurance may be changed from year 
to year.
§ 403.3 Application for insurance.
Application for insurance may be sub­
mitted as provided in §  403.6 at the 
county office for the Corporation. The 
Corporation reserves the right to dis­
continue the acceptance of applications 
in any county upon its determination 
that the insurance risk involved is exces-

(b) Losses shall be determined separately  
for each unit. The amount of loss with  
respect to any unit shall be determined by  
(1) multiplying the insured acreage of

(c) Reported damages from insured causes  
shall be indemnified on the basis of ap­
praisals made by the Corporation and the  
percent of any damage shall be the ratio of  
the number of bushels of peaches damaged  
by an insured cause as determined by the  
Corporation to the number of bushels which  
would have been produced as determined by  
the Corporation (hereinafter called the “po­
tential” ) had no insured or uninsured dam­
age occurred. Any indemnity payable on  
a unit in any crop year shall be based upon  
and limited to the following:
First Period.  Loss from an insured cause  
occurring during the period February 1 to  
April 15 inclusive— Damage in excess of 50  
percent of the potential for this period.
The potential herein shall be based upon  
the age, size, condition, and other produc­
tive capabilities of the trees.
Second Period.  Loss from an insured cause  
occurring during the period April 16 to May  
15 inclusive— Damage in excess of 20 percent  
of the potential for this period: Provided,  
however,  That any damage reported and ap­
praised in the First Period of 20 percent or  
more shall satisfy this deductible.
The potential herein shall be based upon  
the undamaged peaches on the trees at the  
time damage occurred; but, shall not exceed  
the potential, if any, which was or could  
have been established as provided in the  
First Period.
The aggregate of indemnities payable for  
any unit through this period shall not ex­
ceed 80 percent of the amount of insurance.
Third Period.  Loss from an insured cause  
occurring after May 15— Damage in excess of  
10 percent of the potential for this period:  
Provided, however,  That any damage re­
ported and appraised in one of the previous  
periods of 10 percent or more shall satisfy  
this deductible.
The potential herein shall be based upon  
the undamaged peaches on the trees at the  
time damage occurred but prior to the  
normal droppage shall not exceed the poten­
tial, if any, last established or which was  
or could have been established as provided  
in the First Period.
The aggregate indemnities payable for any  
unit through this period shall not exceed 90  
percent of the amount of insurance.
If damage occurs in more than one period  
and the damage applicable to each period is  
indeterminable, it shall be distributed  
equally to each period involved and adjusted  
on the basis of establishing potentials as  
though the damages thus distributed had  
been determined in the usual manner and  
the indemnity payable shall be based upon  
the amount of insurance provided for the  
respective periods involved.

fer shall be made on assignment or transfer  
forms prescribed by the Corporation and  
shall be subject to all the terms set forth  
thereon and to the terms hereof.
18. Insured interest.  For the purpose of  
determining the amount of indemnity the in­
terest insured shall not exceed the inter­
est of the insured at the time of damage as  
determined by the Corporation.
19. Misrepresentation and fraud.  The  
Corporation may void the contract without  
affecting the insured’s liability for any earned  
premium(s) if at any time the insured has  
concealed or misrepresented any material  
fact or committed any fraudulent act against  
the Corporation and such voidance shall be  
effective as of the beginning of the crop  
year which relates to the insured crop with  
respect to which any such act or omission  
occurred,
20. Subrogation.  The insured (including  
his assignee or transferee) assigns to the Cor­
poration all rights of recovery against any  
person for loss or damage to the extent that  
payment hereunder is made and «hn.ii ex­
ecute all papers required and take appropri­
ate action to secure such rights.
21. Cause of loss not insured against.  
The contract shall not cover any loss due  
to neglect or malfeasance of the insured, any  
member of his household, his tenants, or em­
ployees, or failure to follow recognized good  
farming practices, or to any cause other  
than a cause insured against.
22. Payment of indemnity,  (a) Any in­
demnity will be paid within 30 days after  
a claim therefor is approved by the Cor­
poration but in no event shall the Corpora­
tion be liable for interest or damages in  
connection with such claim.
(b) If the insured dies or is judicially  
declared incompetent before insurance at­

terminate as of the date of death or Judicial

insurance attaches in any crop year the con­
tract shall terminate at the end of such  
crop year and any indemnity payable shall  
be paid to the person or persons the Corpo­
ration determines to be beneficially entitled  
thereto.

23. Meaning of terms.  For purposes of In­
surance on peaches the terms:
(a) “County actuarial table” means the  
forms and related material which are ap­
proved by the Corporation which are on file  
for public inspection in the county office  
and which show the applicable amounts of  
insurance, premium rates, and related in­
formation with respect to peach crop in­
surance for each crop year in the county.
(b) “County office” means the Corpora­
tion’s office for the county shown in this  
application and policy or such office as may  
be designated by the Corporation from time  
to time.
(c) “ County” means the area shown on  
the county actuarial table which may in­
clude units located in a local producing area  
bordering on the county.
(d) “Crop year” means the calendar year  
in which insurance attaches.
(e) “Harvest” means any severance of  
peaches from the trees by picking or pickr  
ing the marketable peaches from the ground.
(f) “Insurance unit” means all insurable  
acreage of peaches in the county ( 1) in  
which the insured has 100 percent interest  
on the date insurance attaches for the crop  
year that is located on contiguous land un­
der the same ownership, or ( 2) in which  
two or more persons have 100 percent in­
terest on the date insurance attaches for  
the crop year that is located on contiguous  
land under the saihe ownership, excluding  
any other acreage of peaches in which such  
persons do not have 100 percent interest on  
such date. Land rented for cash or for a  
fixed commodity payment shall be consid­
ered as owned by the lessee. Contiguous  
land shall include only land that is touching  
at any point except that land that is sepa­
rated only by a public or private way shall  
be considered contiguous. The Corporation  
may by agreement in writing with the in­
sured before insurance attaches in any crop  
year combine units for the purpose of pro­
viding premium benefits resulting from the  
acreage of the varieties of peaches on the  
unit.

PART 1070— ONIONS 
Import Restrictions
Findings, (a) Notice of rule making 
regarding proposed restrictions on the 
importation of onions into the United 
States, to be made effective under the 
Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act 
of 1937, as amended (7 U.S.C. 601-674; 
P.L. 87-128), was published in the Fed­
eral R egister September 16, 1961 (26 
F.R. 8674). The notice afforded inter­
ested persons an opportunity to file data, 
views, or arguments in regard thereto 
not later than 20 days after publication. 
Subsequent to publication of this notice 
a number of statements and views were 
filed establishing good cause for extend­
ing the filing period. Accordingly, an 
amended notice was published in the Oc­
tober 10,1961, F teD E R A L  R egister (26 F.R. 
9555), extending the filing period to Oc­
tober 21,1961, and the proposed effective 
date was changed. Within the period 
specified, a number of statements were 
filed indicating a need for modification 
of the proposal. Also, a number of 
statements were filed supporting the 
published proposal. After consideration 
of all relevant matters presented, in­
cluding the, proposals set forth in the 
aforesaid notice, and the data, views, 
and arguments submitted by interested 
parties, it is hereby found that the 
restrictions on the importation of onions 
into the United States, as hereinafter 
provided, comply with the grade, size, 
and quality requirements applicable to 
onions produced in the United States, 
and effective under Marketing Order 
No. 117 (7 CFR Part 1017) regulating 
the handling of onions grown in desig­
nated counties of Idaho and eastern 
Oregon.
(b) It is hereby further found that 
good cause exists for not postponing the 
effective date of this regulation beyond 
December 4, 1961 (5 U.S.C. 1001-1011) 
in that (1) the requirements established 
by this import regulation are issued pur­
suant to Section 8e of the said Agricul­
tural Marketing Agreement Act, as 
amended, which makes such regulation 
mandatory; (2) all known onion imr 
porters were notified of the proposed 
regulation, many of whom filed views 
on it; (3) notice that this action was
being considered was published in the 
F ederal R egister on September 16, 1961 
(26 F.R. 8674), and such notice is hereby 
determined to be reasonable.
§ 1070.1 Onion Regulation No. 1.
(a) Import restrictions. During the 
period from December 4,1961, to June 30, 
*1962, both dates inclusive, no person 
shall import dry onions of any variety, 
unless the onions are inspected and meet 
the requirements of the U.S. No. 2 grade, 
or better, and for yellow varieties, 2  
inches minimum diameter.
(b) Condition. Due consideration 
shall be given to the time required for 
transportation and entry of onions into 
the United States. For onions with 
transit time from country of origin to 
entry into the United States of ten or 
more days, onions otherwise meeting 
import quality and size requirements 
may be entered if they meet an average 
tolerance for decay of not more than 5  
percent.
(c) Minimum quantity. Any impor­
tation which in the aggregate does not 
exceed 100 pounds in any day, may be 
imported without regard to the provi­
sions of paragraph (a) of this section.
(d) Plant quarantine. Provisions of 
this section shall not supersede the re­
strictions or prohibitions on onions 
under the Plant Quarantine Act of 1912.
(e) Designation of governmental in­
spection service. The Federal or the 
Federal-State Inspection Service, Fruit 
and Vegetable Division, Agricultural 
Marketing Service, United States De­
partment of Agriculture, is the inspec­
tion service for certifying the grade, 
size, quality, and maturity of onions that 
are imported into the United States 
under the provisions of section 8e of the 
act.
(f) Inspection and official inspection 
certificates. (1) Inspection by the Fed­
eral or Federal-State Inspection Service, 
with appropriate evidence thereof in the 
form of an official inspection certificate, 
issued by the respective service, appli­
cable to the particular shipment of 
onions is required, on all imports of 
onions. Each lot shall be madO available 
and accessible for inspection. Inspection 
and certification will be available in ac- 
cordanée with the rules and regulations 
governing inspection and certification of 
fresh fruits, vegetables and other prod­
ucts (Part 51 of this title). Since in­
spectors may not be stationed in the 
immediate vicinity of some smaller ports 
of entry, importers of onions should 
make advance arrangements for inspec­
tion by ascertaining whether or not 
there is an inspector located at their 
particular port of entry. For all ports of 
entry where an inspection office is not 
located, each importer must give the 
specified advance notice to the applica­
ble office listed below prior to the tim e 
the onions will be imported.

On January 19, 1961, there was pub­
lished in the Federal R egister (26 F.R. 
488) a notice of a hearing to be held for 
the custodial and janitorial service in­
dustry to determine the appropriate 
small business size standards to be ap­
plied to that industry. On February 23, 
1961, such hearing was held and testi­
mony received.
On June 10, 1961, there was published 
in the Federal R egister (26 F.R. 5236) 
a notice that the Administrator of the 
Small Business Administration proposed 
to amend the definition of small business 
for the custodial and janitorial service 
industry for the purpose of Government 
procurements and SBA business loans 
based on the aforementioned hearing. 
The proposed amendment would have 
changed the definition so that a small 
business in this industry would be defined 
as a concern which has average annual 
receipts of $500,000 or less for its preced­
ing three fiscal years.
Interested persons were given an op­
portunity to present their comments or 
suggestions pertaining thereto, to the 
Office of Small Business Size Standards, 
within 30 days after the date of publica­
tion of the notice in the Federal R eg­
ister . The comments indicated gen­
erally that the proposed size-standard of 
average annual receipts of $500,000 or 
less for the preceding three fiscal years 
was too low and, therefore, would deny 
many small businesses within this in­
dustry the opportunity to receive as­
sistance from the Small Business Ad­
ministration. However, there was a clear 
indication that a higher figure of average 
annual receipts would be more equitable 
and it was suggested ,that the size stand­
ard for the purpose of Government pro­
curement for the custodial and janitorial 
service industry be the same as the size 
standard for that industry for-  the pur-

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (26 FR 10629) prints Executive Order 10975 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1961-11-10; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate a dispute between Pan American World Airways, Inc., and certain of its employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving Pan American World Airways, Inc., and certain of its employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "10975 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).

Executive Order 11006
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN EASTERN AIR LINES, INC., AND CERTAIN OF ITS EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S  a dispute exists between the Eastern A ir Lines, Inc., 
a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Flight Engi­
neers’ International Association, E  A L  Chapter, a labor organization; 
and
W H E R E A S  this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended ; and
W H E R E A S  this dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation 
Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a 
degree such as to deprive a section o f the country of essential trans­
portation service:
N O W , T H E R E F O R E , by virtue o f the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I  
hereby create a board o f three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization o f airline employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the dispute within thirty days from the date o f this order.
As provided by Section 10 o f the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
Eastern A ir Lines, Inc., or by its employees, in the condition out of 
which the dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 2143) prints Executive Order 11008 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1962-03-03; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate dispute between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company and other carriers and certain of their employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company and other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees (List A) and certain of their employees represented by the Eleven Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations (List B); it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11008 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).

No held source shows an earlier revocation, supersession, expiry or termination. The first ending shown by held evidence is the express revocation by number in EO 12553, effective 1986-02-25. Later orders that merely recite or list this order would not be ends; none was found that does more than EO 12553.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command independent of the board: the standstill is recited from the statute and depends on the board's creation and report. No other command in the order, and no other order that incorporates it, was found in the held texts.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception (searched as described); the board's report and any settlement or later legislation are not obligations created by this order and are not claimed as surviving effects.","scope_check":"Single clause, whole order. The dossier's inventory spans the recitals, the creation of the board, the report command and the statutory standstill recital to the signature; I confirm it as complete. EO 12553 revokes the whole order (it lists the order itself and its amendments), so no part of the order is left outside the ending."}

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 2677) prints Executive Order 11011 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1962-03-20; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Trans World Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving Trans World Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11011 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own-terms periods (report deadline and standstill) are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21. No held source shows an earlier revocation, supersession, expiry or termination. The first ending shown by held evidence is the express revocation by number in EO 12553, effective 1986-02-25. Later orders that merely recite or list this order would not be ends; none was found that does more than EO 12553.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command independent of the board: the standstill is recited from the statute and depends on the board's creation and report. No other command in the order, and no other order that incorporates it, was found in the held texts.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception (searched as described); the board's report and any settlement or later legislation are not obligations created by this order and are not claimed as surviving effects.","scope_check":"Single clause, whole order. The dossier's inventory spans the recitals, the creation of the board, the report command and the statutory standstill recital to the signature; I confirm it as complete. EO 12553 revokes the whole order (it lists the order itself and its amendments), so no part of the order is left outside the ending."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause, the whole of Executive Order 11015, terminated on 1986-02-25 when EO 12553 revoked the order by number. Mechanism: express revocation by a numbered list ("Revocation of Various Executive Orders"; "any amendments thereto, are revoked:"); the target is identified by this row: "11015 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". The report deadline and standstill are spent facts recorded without an end date, and they did not end the order. The effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (alternative: publication on 1986-03-03).
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11015
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CHICAGO AND NORTH WESTERN RAILWAY COMPANY,
THE FORMER CHICAGO, ST. PAUL, MINNEAPOLIS AND OMAHA
RAILWAY COMPANY, NOW A PART OF THE CHICAGO AND NORTH
WESTERN RAILWAY COMPANY BY MERGER, AND CERTAIN OF
THEIR EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S disputes existbetween the Chicago and North Western 
Railway Company, the former Chicago, St. Paul, Minneapolis, and 
Omaha Railway Company, now a part o f the Chicago and North 
Western Railway Company by merger, and certain o f their employees 
represented by the Order of Railroad Telegraphers; and
W H E R E A S these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W H E R E A S these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential 
transportation service:
NOW, TH E R E FO R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me 
by section 10 o f the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 TJ.S.C. 160), 
I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
these disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers, or by their employees, in the conditions out of which these 
disputes arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 3905) prints Executive Order 11015 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1962-04-23; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate disputes between the Chicago and North Western Railway Company, the former Chicago, St. Paul, Minneapolis and Omaha Railway Company, now a part of the Chicag). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the Chicago and North Western Railway Company, the former Chicago, St. Paul, Minneapolis and Omaha Railway Company, and certain of their employees represented by the Order of Railroad Telegraphers; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11015 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The packet holds no located acting-provision record for this pair (the dossier lists the target provision as not located), so the end is cited to the complete held text of EO 12553 (Federal Register copy, 51 FR 7237), which contains both the enacting paragraph and the table row quoted above; I read the whole text and the row is present on its own line. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).

No held source shows an earlier revocation, supersession, expiry or termination. The first ending shown by held evidence is the express revocation by number in EO 12553, effective 1986-02-25. Later orders that merely recite or list this order would not be ends; none was found that does more than EO 12553.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command independent of the board: the standstill is recited from the statute and depends on the board's creation and report. No other command in the order, and no other order that incorporates it, was found in the held texts.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception (searched as described); the board's report and any settlement or later legislation are not obligations created by this order and are not claimed as surviving effects.","scope_check":"Single clause, whole order. The dossier's inventory spans the recitals, the creation of the board, the report command and the statutory standstill recital to the signature; I confirm it as complete. EO 12553 revokes the whole order (it lists the order itself and its amendments), so no part of the order is left outside the ending."}

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11027
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE  
BETWEEN THE NEW YORK CENTRAL RAILROAD COMPANY SYSTEM  
AND THE PITTSBURGH AND LAKE ERIE RAILROAD COMPANY AND  
CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS a dispute exists between the New York Central Rail­
road Company System and the Pittsburgh and Lake Erie Railroad 
Company and certain of their employees represented by the Order 
of Railroad Telegraphers; and
W HEREAS this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the 
provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended ; and
W HEREAS this dispute, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential 
transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me 
by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I  hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
this dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its re­
port to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made 
by the New York Central Railroad Company System and the Pitts­
burgh and Lake Erie Railroad Company, or by their employees, in 
the conditions out of which this dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 5533) prints Executive Order 11027 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1962-06-08; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the New York Central Railroad Company System and the Pittsburgh and Lake Erie Railroad Company and certain of their employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the New York Central Railroad Company System and the Pittsburgh and Lake Erie Railroad Company and certain of their employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11027 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).

Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 5903) prints Executive Order 11033 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1962-06-20; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate disputes between the American Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving American Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11033 Creating an emergency board to investigate airline labor disputes". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 11042
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE  
BETWEEN THE SOUTHERN PACIFIC COMPANY (PACIFIC LINES) AND  
CERTAIN OF ITS EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS a dispute exists between the Southern Pacific Com­
pany (Pacific Lines), a carrier, and certain of its employees repre­
sented by the Brotherhood of Railway and Steamship Clerks, Freight  
Handlers, Express and Station Employes, a labor organization; and
W HEREAS this dispute has not heretofore been-  adjusted under  
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS this dispute, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce  
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential  
transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by  
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S C. 160),  
I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to  
investigate this dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily  
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or  
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to  
this dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended,  
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report  
to the President, no change, except by agreement, -shall be made by  
the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines), or by its employees,  
in the conditions out of which this dispute arose.
T he  W hite  H ouse,
August 10 ,1962.
J ohn  F. K ennedy
[F.R. Doc. 62-8237 ;  Filed, Aug. 13,1962 ; 12:04 p.m.]

Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 8067) prints Executive Order 11042 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1962-08-10; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines) and certain of its employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines) and certain of its employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11042 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11054 with the subject "Creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime industry". This order (27 FR 9695, Federal Register of October 2, 1962, signed October 1, 1962) created, under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 (61 Stat. 155; 29 U.S.C. 176), a Board of Inquiry of three named members to inquire into the issues in labor disputes between maritime-industry employers (steamship companies, operators or agents of ships serving Atlantic and Gulf Coast ports from Searsport, Maine, to Brownsville, Texas, contracting stevedores, contracting marine carpenters, lighterage operators and other employers in related pier activities) and certain of their employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, AFL-CIO, disputes that had resulted in a strike; gave the Board the powers and duties set forth in Title II of the Act; directed it to report to the President in accordance with section 206 by a Thursday in October 1962 (the day of the month is garbled in the text layer); and provided that upon submission of its report the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act. The report date is a deadline, not an end, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), and the continuing-existence sentence means the order's own text does not end the Board at the report. No report of this Board is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so none is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent as to its reporting deadline, and the order stayed on the books until this express revocation. The text layer of this order is badly garbled in places, so this description is a paraphrase of the legible words and no part of it is quoted.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 9695, the issue of October 2, 1962) is Executive Order 11054, dated October 1, 1962; its title (a board of inquiry to report on certain labor disputes affecting the maritime industry of the United States) and its text, partly garbled in the text layer, identify it, and it is dated October 1, 1962. The dossier's clause inventory for this order covers unrelated Federal Register rules on neighbouring pages, so I replaced it with the order's own operative text. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier. 
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states a report deadline (a Thursday in October 1962) and a sentence that the Board shall continue in existence after its report; it states no date on which the Board or the order ends. The deadline is not an end and the continuing-existence sentence is the opposite of an own-terms end at the report. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553, and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 shows no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create and appoint the Board, state its powers by reference to Title II of the Act, set the report deadline, continue the Board in existence) depends on this order and on the disputes it addressed; the Board's statutory powers come from the Labor-Management Relations Act, a separate statute.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself and the disputes were one-time disputes.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried by correction: the whole operative text (the recitals of the maritime disputes and strike, the creation and membership of the Board of Inquiry, its powers and duties, the report deadline and the continuing-existence sentence). The dossier's nine clauses are neighbouring rules and are not clauses of this order. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself and the disputes were one-time disputes. No held claim-grade source shows any command of this order continuing when it was revoked.

Executive Order 11078
CREATING A BOARD OF INQUIRY TO REPORT ON A LABOR DISPUTE  
AFFECTING THE BALLISTICS MISSILE, SPACE VEHICLE AND MILITARY  
AIRCRAFT INDUSTRY
W H ER E AS, there exists a labor dispute between the Boeing Com­
pany and certain of its employees represented by the International 
Association of Machinists, A F L-C IO , the International Guards Union 
of America (Ind.), the International Union of United Weldors 
(Ind.), the International Union of Operating Engineers, A F L-C IO , 
the Vertol Division of the Boeing Company and certain of its em­
ployees represented by the United Automobile, Aerospace and A gri­
cultural Implement Workers of America, A F L-C IO , and the Auburn, 
Washington, plant of the Rohr Aircraft Corporation, a subcontractor 
of the Boeing Company, almost all of whose production is utilized 
by the Boeing Company, and certain of its employees represented by 
the International Association of Machinists, A F L -C IO ; and
W H ER E AS, in my opinion such dispute threatens to result in a 
strike affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade or 
commerce among the several States or with foreign nations, or in 
the production of goods for commerce, which strike, if ■  permitted 
to occur or to continue, will imperil the national safety:
NO W  TH ER E FO RE , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947, 61 Stat. 
155 (29 U.S.C. 176), I  hereby create a Board of Inquiry, consisting 
of Honorable Benjamin Aaron, Chairman, Honorable J. B. Gilling­
ham and the Honorable Lloyd Ulman as members, to inquire into 
the issues involved in such dispute.
The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title I I  
of such Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance 
with the provisions of section 206 of such Act on or before Friday, 
January 25,1963.
Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence 
to perform such other functions as may be required under such Act.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11101 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". This order (28 FR 3305, Federal Register of April 5, 1963, signed April 3, 1963) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the Eastern, Western, and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees (listed in attached List A) and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, and the Switchmen's Union of North America, labor organizations; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by May 3, 1963); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 154 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated May 13, 1963. Thirty days after May 13, 1963 is June 12, 1963. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on May 13, 1963, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on June 12, 1963.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11115 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". This order (28 FR 6905, Federal Register of July 6, 1963, signed July 4, 1963) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between The Pullman Company, The Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific Railroad Company, the New York Central System and The Soo Line Railroad Company, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by August 3, 1963); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those four carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 155 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated November 2, 1963; the board report states that the parties agreed to extensions of time to September 19, October 19 and finally to November 2, 1963 with the approval of the President. Thirty days after November 2, 1963 is December 2, 1963. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on November 2, 1963, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on December 2, 1963.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11115
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE PULLMAN COMPANY, THE CHICAGO, ROCK ISLAND &
PACIFIC RAILROAD COMPANY, THE NEW YORK CENTRAL SYSTEM,
AND THE SOO LINE RAILROAD COMPANY AND CERTAIN OF THEIR
EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between The Pullman Company, The  
Chicago, Rock Island &  Pacific Railroad Company, the New York  
Central System and The Soo Line Railroad Company, and certain  
of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car  
Porters, a labor organization;  and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under  
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce  
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by  
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I  
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to  
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees  
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to  
these disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended,  
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report  
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by  
The Pullman Company, the Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific Railroad  
Company, the New York Central System and The Soo Line Railroad  
Company, or by its employees, in the conditions out of which this  
dispute arose.

CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE
BETWEEN THE UNITED AIR LINES, INC., AND CERTAIN OF ITS
EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S  a dispute exists between the United A ir Lines, Inc., 
a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Interna­
tional Association of Machinists, A F L-C IO , a labor organization; 
and
W H E R E A S this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway.  Labor Act, as amended; and
W H E R E A S  this dispute, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential 
transportation service:
NOW, TH ER E FO RE , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I  hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate,this dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect 
to the disputejvithin thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this dale and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the United A ir Lines, Inc., or by its employees, in the conditions 
out of which the dispute arose.
