research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (28 FR 10855) prints Executive Order 11121 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1963-10-09; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the United Air Lines, Inc., and certain of its employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving United Air Lines, Inc., and certain of its employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11121 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own-terms periods (report deadline and standstill) are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21. No held source shows an earlier revocation, supersession, expiry or termination. The first ending shown by held evidence is the express revocation by number in EO 12553, effective 1986-02-25. Later orders that merely recite or list this order would not be ends; none was found that does more than EO 12553.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command independent of the board: the standstill is recited from the statute and depends on the board's creation and report. No other command in the order, and no other order that incorporates it, was found in the held texts.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception (searched as described); the board's report and any settlement or later legislation are not obligations created by this order and are not claimed as surviving effects.","scope_check":"Single clause, whole order. The dossier's inventory spans the recitals, the creation of the board, the report command and the statutory standstill recital to the signature; I confirm it as complete. EO 12553 revokes the whole order (it lists the order itself and its amendments), so no part of the order is left outside the ending."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: After a bounded search of the full text of EO 12553, the U.S. Code and eCFR (no hits for this order), and the Federal Register catalog notes, no savings clause, exception or surviving legal effect was found; EO 12553 revokes the order without any reservation.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause, the whole of Executive Order 11127, terminated on 1986-02-25 when EO 12553 revoked the order by number. Mechanism: express revocation by a numbered list ("Revocation of Various Executive Orders"; "any amendments thereto, are revoked:"); the target is identified by this row: "11127 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". The report deadline and standstill are spent facts recorded without an end date, and they did not end the order. The effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (alternative: publication on 1986-03-03).
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11127
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE; BE­
TWEEN THE FLORIDA EAST COAST RAILWAY COMPANY AND CER­
TAIN OF ITS EMPLOYEES
W H E R E AS a dispute exists between the Florida East Coast Rail­
way Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by 
the Eleven Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations, designated m 
L IS T  A  attached hereto and made a part hereof; and
W H E R E AS this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended ; and
W H E R E A S this dispute, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential 
transportation service:
NOW, TH E R E FO RE , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I  hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees 
or any carrier.
The Board shall report its findings to the President with respect 
to this dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section-10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
Florida East Coast Railway Company, or by its employees, in the con­
ditions out of which the dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (28 FR 12079) prints Executive Order 11127 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1963-11-09; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Florida East Coast Railway Company and certain of its employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the Florida East Coast Railway Company and certain of its employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11127 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The packet holds no located acting-provision record for this pair (the dossier lists the target provision as not located), so the end is cited to the complete held text of EO 12553 (Federal Register copy, 51 FR 7237), which contains both the enacting paragraph and the table row quoted above; I read the whole text and the row is present on its own line. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own-terms periods (report deadline and standstill) are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21. No held source shows an earlier revocation, supersession, expiry or termination. The first ending shown by held evidence is the express revocation by number in EO 12553, effective 1986-02-25. Later orders that merely recite or list this order would not be ends; none was found that does more than EO 12553.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command independent of the board: the standstill is recited from the statute and depends on the board's creation and report. No other command in the order, and no other order that incorporates it, was found in the held texts.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception (searched as described); the board's report and any settlement or later legislation are not obligations created by this order and are not claimed as surviving effects.","scope_check":"Single clause, whole order. The dossier's inventory spans the recitals, the creation of the board, the report command and the statutory standstill recital to the signature; I confirm it as complete. EO 12553 revokes the whole order (it lists the order itself and its amendments), so no part of the order is left outside the ending."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11131 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate airline labor disputes". This order (28 FR 13485, Federal Register of December 13, 1963, signed December 11, 1963) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Braniff Airways, Inc., Continental Airlines, Inc., Eastern Air Lines, Inc., National Airlines, Inc., Northwest Airlines, Inc., and Trans World Airlines, Inc., air carriers, and certain of their employees represented by the International Association of Machinists, AFL-CIO, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by January 10, 1964); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those six air carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by January 10, 1964) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (28 FR 13485, the issue of December 13, 1963) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 11131, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated December 11, 1963. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by January 10, 1964), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by January 10, 1964) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: the dossier's single clause covers the complete operative text (29 FR 125, held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11135.txt offsets 542-2300): the order creates a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the disputes between the carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees (List A) and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen ('I hereby create; a board of three members', offset 1559 onward), directs it to report 'within thirty days from the date o f this order' (offset 1798 onward) and recites the section 10 status quo (offset 2075 onward). The carrier list (List A) after the signature is an attached schedule identifying the parties, not a separate command. First end: EO 12553, effective on signing 1986-02-25, which names this order ('11135 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes', jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt offsets 19627-19699). Earlier-end test: the order has no sunset, term, condition or termination clause of its own; its report deadline (1964-02-02 (signing date 1964-01-03 plus 30 days; counting convention not ruled)) is never an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, option C), and the status-quo recital is a statutory consequence, not an end of the order. The board's actual report (its date, and so the end of the 30-day status quo) is not held in the repository (no NMB report text under jobs/source-ladder/output/texts; no FETCH_QUEUE line yet), so the 'functionally spent' date is disclosed as unknown; under the report-deadline ruling it is not an end and does not change the first end. No amendment, extension, suspension or partial end by any other instrument was found before 1986-02-25 (D6: dossier chain, actor provisions, draft proposals, by-number scans), so no later event is attached.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11135
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE EASTERN, WESTERN  
AND SOUTHEASTERN CARRIERS’ CONFERENCE COMMITTEES, AND  
CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S  disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers’ Conference Committees, 
designated in List A  attached hereto and made a part hereof, and 
certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad 
Signalmen, a labor organization; and
W H E R E A S  these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W H E R E A S  these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NO W , T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (4:5 U.S.C. 160), I  
hereby create; a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date o f this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern 
Carriers’ Conference Committees, or by their employees, in the condi­
tions out of which the disputes arose.

research_rationale: EO 11135 (signed 1964-01-03, 29 FR 125), read in full from the held official FR text layer (29 FR 125, held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11135.txt offsets 542-2300; the representation is the official FR page OCR, location_verified false, page check not required by the record). Status provisional NO, unchanged. The order creates a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the disputes between the carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees (List A) and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen ('I hereby create; a board of three members', offset 1559 onward), directs it to report 'within thirty days from the date o f this order' (offset 1798 onward) and recites the section 10 status quo (offset 2075 onward). The carrier list (List A) after the signature is an attached schedule identifying the parties, not a separate command. Deciding source: EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt), whose operative sentence (offsets 691-966) revokes 'the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto', and whose table names this order ('11135 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes', offsets 19627-19699); no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 1986-02-25. The dossier lists 'target provision not located: EO:12553' because the machine scanner found no ACT record; I located the naming entry myself ('11135 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes' at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt offsets 19627-19699, inside the table introduced by the operative sentence at 691-966), so the end cites the held EO 12553 text as a whole (ACTOR_TEXT) with those offsets named here. Report-deadline ruling (2026-10-21, option C) applied: the report deadline (1964-02-02 (signing date 1964-01-03 plus 30 days; counting convention not ruled)) and the report itself are spent facts, not ends. The board's actual report (its date, and so the end of the 30-day status quo) is not held in the repository (no NMB report text under jobs/source-ladder/output/texts; no FETCH_QUEUE line yet), so the 'functionally spent' date is disclosed as unknown; under the report-deadline ruling it is not an end and does not change the first end. D6 / later events: the dossier chain and actor provisions show only EO 12553; the draft's later-event and whole-order-end proposals (OFR disposition note 'Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986' and the 1989 Codification table 'Revoked by EO 12553') point to the same instrument and are attached as the end itself; a by-number scan of all held FR order texts and APP texts found no other naming instrument (EO_10298 and EO_10299 (16 FR 11135 page number), EO_11912 (FR Doc. 76-11135), EO_12553 (the revocation)). Quotations in this claim are copied from the held OCR or text layers with line breaks, soft hyphens and letter-spacing normalized; the exact spans are at the stated offsets. No conflicts are listed in the draft or dossier. Own-residual check, reading EO 11135 in full (29 FR 125, held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11135.txt offsets 542-2300): it created an ad hoc fact-finding board for one labor dispute and set its report duty; it created no office, fund, property or private right that could outlast the board, and any status-quo obligation was the statute's own and long spent. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause, the whole of Executive Order 11168, terminated on 1986-02-25 when EO 12553 revoked the order by number. Mechanism: express revocation by a numbered list ("Revocation of Various Executive Orders"; "any amendments thereto, are revoked:"); the target is identified by this row: "11168 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". The report deadline and standstill are spent facts recorded without an end date, and they did not end the order. The effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (alternative: publication on 1986-03-03).
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11168
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY  
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees rep­
resented by the Eleven Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations, 
labor organizations, designated in List B attached hereto and made a 
part hereof; and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (29 FR 11885) prints Executive Order 11168 as an order of the President (Lyndon B. Johnson) dated 1964-08-18; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11168 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The packet holds no located acting-provision record for this pair (the dossier lists the target provision as not located), so the end is cited to the complete held text of EO 12553 (Federal Register copy, 51 FR 7237), which contains both the enacting paragraph and the table row quoted above; I read the whole text and the row is present on its own line. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11169
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees rep­
resented by the Six Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations func­
tioning through the Railway Employes’  Department, AFL-CIO, 
labor organizations, designated in the List B attached hereto and made 
a part hereof; and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree siich as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a board, to be appointed by me, to investigate these 
disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise 
interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, 
or by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (29 FR 11889) prints Executive Order 11169 as an order of the President (Lyndon B. Johnson) dated 1964-08-18; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating an emergency board to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, 45 U.S.C. 160, to investigate the dispute involving the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees; it bars board members from pecuniary or other interest in any carrier or employee organization; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and it recites the statutory standstill: from the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change except by agreement is to be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11169 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The packet holds no located acting-provision record for this pair (the dossier lists the target provision as not located), so the end is cited to the complete held text of EO 12553 (Federal Register copy, 51 FR 7237), which contains both the enacting paragraph and the table row quoted above; I read the whole text and the row is present on its own line. The thirty-day report deadline and the standstill that runs to thirty days after the report are periods measured by the order's own terms. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, neither the report nor the end of the standstill ends the order; each is a spent fact, and the order stayed on the books until it was expressly revoked. The order was functionally spent once the board had reported and the standstill had run, but this claim assigns no date to that point because no report date is cited from a registered source here; a board report held as a lead-grade Government printing is not cited, and a dated transmittal letter is not proof of receipt or of standstill expiry. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own-terms periods (report deadline and standstill) are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21. No held source shows an earlier revocation, supersession, expiry or termination. The first ending shown by held evidence is the express revocation by number in EO 12553, effective 1986-02-25. Later orders that merely recite or list this order would not be ends; none was found that does more than EO 12553.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command independent of the board: the standstill is recited from the statute and depends on the board's creation and report. No other command in the order, and no other order that incorporates it, was found in the held texts.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception (searched as described); the board's report and any settlement or later legislation are not obligations created by this order and are not claimed as surviving effects.","scope_check":"Single clause, whole order. The dossier's inventory spans the recitals, the creation of the board, the report command and the statutory standstill recital to the signature; I confirm it as complete. EO 12553 revokes the whole order (it lists the order itself and its amendments), so no part of the order is left outside the ending."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Five Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11170 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11170
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part thereof, and certain of their employees rep­
resented by the Five Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations, labor 
organizations, designated in List B attached hereto and made a part 
hereof; and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10, of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 TJ.S.C. 160), 
I  hereby create a board to be appointed by me, to investigate these 
disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise 
interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or 
by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11170 (1964-08-18, 29 FR 11893) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Five Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11170.txt, 29 FR 11893, PDF pages 13-16) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"within thirty days from the date of this order\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

whole_order_end.mechanism_note: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11170 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11180 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.

CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR.CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S  disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
N ational R ailw ay L abor C onference, designated in L ist A  attached 
hereto and made a part h ereof, and certain o f  their em ployees repre­
sented by the B rotherhood o f L ocom otive Firem en and Enginem en, a 
labor organ ization ; and
W H E R E A S  these disputes have not h eretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions o f  the R ailw ay L abor A ct, as am ended; and
W H E R E A S  these disputes, in the judgm ent o f the N ational M edi­
ation B oard, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate com m erce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country o f essential transportation 
service:
N O W , T H E R E F O R E , by virtue o f the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 o f  the R ailw ay L abor A ct,' as amended (45 U .S.C . 160), I  
hereby create a board, to be appointed by me, to investigate these 
disputes. N o member o f the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise 
interested in any organization o f railroad em ployees o r any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President w ith respect to 
the disputes w ithin th irty days from  the date o f this order.

from  this date and fo r  th irty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made b y the 
carriers represented by the N ational R ailw ay L abor C onference, or by 
their em ployees, in  the conditions out o f w hich the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11180 (1964-09-24, 29 FR 13365) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11180.txt, 29 FR 13365, PDF pages 7-9) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (thirty days) and a standstill running (thirty days after the report). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11181 with the subject "Creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime indusiry". This order (29 FR 13557, Federal Register of October 2, 1964, signed September 30, 1964) created, under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 (61 Stat. 155; 29 U.S.C. 176), a Board of Inquiry of three named members (Herbert Schmertz as chairman, James J. Healy and Theodore W. Kheel) to inquire into the issues in labor disputes between maritime-industry employers (steamship companies, operators or agents of ships, contracting stevedores, contracting marine carpenters, lighterage operators and other employers in related pier activities) and certain of their employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, AFL-CIO; gave the Board the powers and duties set forth in Title II of the Act; directed it to report to the President in accordance with section 206 on or before Thursday, October 1, 1964; and provided that upon the submission of its report the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act. The report date is a deadline, not an end, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), and the order's own continuing-existence sentence means its text does not end the Board when the report is submitted. No report of this Board is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent as to its reporting deadline, and the order stayed on the books until this express revocation.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (29 FR 13557, the issue of October 2, 1964) is Executive Order 11181, dated September 30, 1964; the order creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 for labor disputes affecting the maritime industry, and carries the signature date September 30, 1964. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier. 
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states a report deadline (on or before Thursday, October 1, 1964) and a sentence that the Board shall continue in existence after its report to perform other functions required under the Act; it states no date on which the Board or the order ends. The report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the continuing-existence sentence is the opposite of an own-terms end at the report. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553, and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 shows no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create and appoint the Board, state its powers and duties by reference to Title II of the Act, set the report deadline, continue the Board in existence after the report) depends on this order and on the dispute it addressed; the powers and procedures are those of the Labor-Management Relations Act, a separate statute that does not depend on this order.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself, not of this order, and the dispute was a one-time dispute.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text (the recitals of the maritime disputes and threatened strike, the creation and membership of the Board of Inquiry, its powers and duties, the report deadline and the continuing-existence sentence). Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, so every command in the clause ends on the same date."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself, not of this order, and the dispute was a one-time dispute. No held claim-grade source shows any command of this order continuing when it was revoked.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 amends section 1 of EO 11189 by adding the item that follows it (the Level IV addition). It ended with the whole order: first end Executive Order 12060, signed 1978-05-15 (43 FR 21315, Federal Register of May 17, 1978), whose section 3 provides that Executive Order No. 11189 of November 23, 1964, Executive Order No. 11195 of January 30, 1965, and Executive Order No. 11995 of June 8, 1977 "are revoked." EO 12060 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, 1978-05-15; the filing date 1978-05-16 and publication date 1978-05-17 are the alternative readings. The amendment continued until the amended order ended, and EO 11189 was revoked by the same sentence. Earlier candidate end that does not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; it is not the end because it does not name EO 11195): Pub. L. 89-554 (Sept. 6, 1966, 80 Stat. 378), which enacted title 5 of the United States Code, lists in 5 U.S.C. 5315 "(73) Chief of Protocol, Department of State." and in 5 U.S.C. 5316 item (101), the Assistant Director (Program Planning, Analysis and Research), Office of Economic Opportunity, "(110) General Counsel of the Veterans' Administration." and "(114) Staff Director, Commission on Civil Rights.", so every position this order added appears in the statute (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11195_Pub._L._89-554_Sept._6_1966_80_Stat._378_et_seq._including_5_U.S.C._5315_and_5316_as__c629b8a1e7.txt; it is not an evidence record of this dossier, so it is pinned here by path). The Federal Register catalog note on EO 11189 says that order was "Nullified by 80 Stat. 460, 461 (5 U.S.C. 5315, 5316)" because the statute included all positions added by EO 11189 and its amendment EO 11195 (jobs/later-events/output/CATALOG_INDEX.csv), but the catalog note on EO 11195 itself records only the EO 12060 revocation. Section 7(c) of the same Act provides that an order in effect under a replaced law continues in effect under the corresponding provision "until repealed, amended, or superseded.", which points the other way. I did not establish that the statute extinguished this order, so EO 12060 is recorded as the first end.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 6103(a) of the  
Internal Revenue Code of 1954 (68A Stat. 753; 26 U.S.C. 6103(a )),  
as amended by section 3(c) of the Interest Equalization Tax Act  
(78 Stat. 844), it is hereby ordered that returns made in respect of  
the tax imposed by chapter 41 of such Code shall be open to inspec­
tion by certain classes of persons and State and Federal government  
establishments in accordance and upon compliance with the rules and  
regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury in Treasury  
Decision 6543, relating tor inspection and use of returns by such classes  
of persons and State and Federal government establishments, ap­
proved by the President on January 17,1961, the amendment thereto  
approved by the President on April 4, 1963, and the amendment  
thereto approved by me this date.
This order shall be effective upon its filing for publication in the  
F ederal  R egister .
L tndon  B. J ohnson

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The first sentence opens to inspection by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and the Federal Reserve Banks any information return made by a commercial bank under the Interest Equalization Tax Act, under Treasury rules. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11213 Providing for inspection of certain interest equalization tax information returns by the Board of"). Earlier candidate ends that do not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; none is the end because none names EO 11213): (1) Pub. L. 93-17, section 2 (Apr. 10, 1973), amended section 4911(d) of the Internal Revenue Code to read 'June 30,1974' in place of 'March 31, 1973' (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11206_Tax_Reform_Act_of_1976_Pub._L._94-455_sec._1202_90_Stat._1667_same_request_as_for_EO__e9de5b9dcd.txt, 87 Stat. 12); (2) the Tax Reform Act of 1976, Pub. L. 94-455 (Oct. 4, 1976), which repealed chapter 41 (interest equalization tax) with the repeal applying to acquisitions made after June 30, 1974, and rewrote section 6103 effective January 1, 1977 under section 1202(i) (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11206_Tax_Reform_Act_of_1976_Pub._L._94-455_sec._1202_90_Stat._1667_same_request_as_for_EO__1a89ddecb7.txt, 90 Stat. 1520, 1667-1668). The order rests on section 6103(a) as amended by the Interest Equalization Tax Act; I did not establish that either enactment extinguished this order's command, and the 26 U.S.C. 6103 note in the U.S. Code release point records that this order was revoked by EO 12553.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 6103(a) of the 
Internal Revenue Code of 1954 (68A Stat. 753; 26 U.S.C. 6103(a)), 
as amended by section 3(c) of the Interest Equalization Tax Act 
(Pub. L. 88-563, 78 Stat.844), it is hereby ordered that any informa­
tion return made by a commercial bank under the Interest Equaliza­
tion Tax Act shall be open to inspection by the Board of Governors 
of the Federal Reserve System and the Federal Reserve Banks. Such 
inspection shall be in accordance and upon compliance with the rules 
and regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury in a 
Treasury decision, relating to inspection of certain interest equaliza­
tion tax information returns by the Board of Governors of the Federal 
Reserve System and the Federal Reserve Banks, approved by me this 
date.

The consequence of the supersession (EO 11176 no longer in force) is an accrued result; EO 12553's table does not list EO 11176, so the revocation does not purport to revive it. The order was filed April 5, 1965 at 11:30 a.m. according to its printed filing line; the date of the first operative effect is a disclosed fact, not an end.

first_end.mechanism_note: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11213 Providing for inspection of certain interest equalization tax information returns by the Board of" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.

Executive Order 11213
INSPECTION OF CERTAIN INTEREST EQUALIZATION TAX INFORMA­
TION RETURNS BY THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS OF THE FEDERAL

By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 6103(a) of the 
Internal Revenue Code of 1954 (68A Stat. 753; 26 U.S.C. 6103(a)), 
as amended by section 3(c) of the Interest Equalization Tax Act 
(Pub. L. 88-563, 78 Stat.844), it is hereby ordered that any informa­

and regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury in a 
Treasury decision, relating to inspection of certain interest equaliza­
tion tax information returns by the Board of Governors of the Federal 
Reserve System and the Federal Reserve Banks, approved by me this 
date.

research_rationale:
EO 11213 (1965-04-02, 30 FR 4389) is an order under section 6103(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, as amended by section 3(c) of the Interest Equalization Tax Act, opening certain interest equalization tax returns to inspection. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11213.txt, 30 FR 4389, PDF pages 9-9) and confirmed its number, title and signature date against the census register. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes it by number; the dossier already carries the agent-located, independently upheld ACT record for that revocation, which I checked against the held EO 12553 text (operative sentence and table row "11213 Providing for inspection of certain interest equalization tax information returns by the Board of"). The first end is that express revocation. Earlier candidate ends that do not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; none is the end because none names EO 11213): (1) Pub. L. 93-17, section 2 (Apr. 10, 1973), amended section 4911(d) of the Internal Revenue Code to read 'June 30,1974' in place of 'March 31, 1973' (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11206_Tax_Reform_Act_of_1976_Pub._L._94-455_sec._1202_90_Stat._1667_same_request_as_for_EO__e9de5b9dcd.txt, 87 Stat. 12); (2) the Tax Reform Act of 1976, Pub. L. 94-455 (Oct. 4, 1976), which repealed chapter 41 (interest equalization tax) with the repeal applying to acquisitions made after June 30, 1974, and rewrote section 6103 effective January 1, 1977 under section 1202(i) (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11206_Tax_Reform_Act_of_1976_Pub._L._94-455_sec._1202_90_Stat._1667_same_request_as_for_EO__1a89ddecb7.txt, 90 Stat. 1520, 1667-1668). The order rests on section 6103(a) as amended by the Interest Equalization Tax Act; I did not establish that either enactment extinguished this order's command, and the 26 U.S.C. 6103 note in the U.S. Code release point records that this order was revoked by EO 12553. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate a dispute between the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway Company, Lines East and West, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11243 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11243
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTE BETWEEN
THE ATCHISON, TOPEKA AND SANTA FE RAILWAY COMPANY, LINES
EAST AND WEST, AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S  a dispute exists between the Atchison, Topeka and 
Santa Fe Railway Company, Lines East and West, and certain of their 
employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a 
labor organization; and
W H E R E A S  this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the 
provisions^ the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
, W H E R E A S  this dispute, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential 
transportation service:
N O W , T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 o f the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I  hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute..  N o member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the dispute within thirty days from the date o f this order.
As provided by Section 10 o f the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no .change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carrier or by their employees, in the conditions out o f which the 
dispute arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11243 (1965-09-11, 30 FR 11709) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate a dispute between the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway Company, Lines East and West, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11243.txt, 30 FR 11709, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the air carriers represented by the Five Carriers Negotiating Committee and certain of their employees represented by the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11276 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.

Presidential Documents
Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive O rder 11276
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE FIVE CARRIERS NEGO­
TIATING COMMITTEE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S disputes exist between the air carriers represented by 
the Five Carriers Negotiating Committee, designated in List A, at­
tached hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees 
represented by the International Association of Machinists and Aero­
space Workers, A FL -C IO , a labor organization; and
W H E R E A S these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W H E R E A S these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I  
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees 
or in any air carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect 
to the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the Five Carriers Negotiating Committee, 
or by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.
