research_rationale:
EO 11276 (1966-04-21, 31 FR 6233) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the air carriers represented by the Five Carriers Negotiating Committee and certain of their employees represented by the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11276.txt, 31 FR 6233, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"within thirty days from the date of this order\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate a dispute between American Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America (sections 10 and 201 of the Railway Labor Act), directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11291 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11291
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE
BETWEEN THE AMERICAN AIRLINES, INC., AND CERTAIN OF ITS
EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS a dispute exists between the American Airlines, Inc., a  
carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport  
Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO, a labor organization; and
W HEREAS this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under  
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  and
W HEREAS this dispute, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to  
a degree such as to deprive, a section of the country of essential  
transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by  
Sections 10 and 201 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C.  
160 and 181, respectively), I hereby create a board of three members, 
to be appointed by me, to investigate this dispute. No member of the  
board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization  
of airline employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to  
this dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended,  
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report  
to the President, no change, except by agreement', shall be made by the  
American Airlines, Inc., or by its employees, in the conditions out of  
which this dispute arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11291 (1966-07-27, 31 FR 10175) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate a dispute between American Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America (sections 10 and 201 of the Railway Labor Act), directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11291.txt, 31 FR 10175, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate a dispute between Pan American World Airways, Inc., and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America (sections 10 and 201 of the Railway Labor Act), directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11308 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11308
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN THE PAN AMERICAN WORLD AIRWAYS, INC., AND CERTAIN
OF ITS EMPLOYEES
W H E R E AS a dispute exists between the Pan American World 
Airways, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by 
the Transport Workers Union of America, A F L-C IO , a labor orga­
nization ; and
W H E R E AS this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the 
provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W H E R E AS this dispute, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to 
a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, TH EREFO RE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Sections 10 and 201 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45U.S.C. 
160 and 181, respectively) ^  I  hereby create a board of three members, 
to be appointed by me, to investigate.this dispute. No member of the 
board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization 
of airline employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
this dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
Pan American World Airways, Inc., or by its employees, in the con­
ditions out of which this dispute arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11308 (1966-09-30, 31 FR 12919) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate a dispute between Pan American World Airways, Inc., and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America (sections 10 and 201 of the Railway Labor Act), directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11308.txt, 31 FR 12919, PDF pages 7-7) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"within thirty days from the date of this order\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11321 with the subject "Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the military aircraft engine industry". This order (31 FR 16301, Federal Register of December 21, 1966, signed December 19, 1966) created, under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act of 1947 (61 Stat. 155; 29 U.S.C. 176), a Board of Inquiry of three named members (Laurence E. Seibel as chairman, Frank J. Dugan and Garth L. Mangum) to inquire into the issues in the labor dispute between the Union Carbide Corporation and certain of its employees represented by the United Steelworkers of America, AFL-CIO, and Local Union No. 2958 thereof, involving the Stellite Division plant at Kokomo, Indiana, a dispute that had resulted in a strike affecting the military aircraft engine industry; gave the Board the powers and duties set forth in Title II of the Act; directed it to report to the President in accordance with section 206 on or before December 20, 1966; and provided that upon submission of its report the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act. The report date is a deadline, not an end, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), and the continuing-existence sentence means the order's own text does not end the Board at the report. No report of this Board is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent as to its reporting deadline, and the order stayed on the books until this express revocation.

CREATING A BOARD OF INQUIRY TO REPORT ON A LABOR DISPUTE
AFFECTING THE MILITARY AIRCRAFT ENGINE INDUSTRY OF THE
UNITED STATES
W HEREAS, there exists a labor dispute between the Union Carbide  
Corporation, a New York Corporation, and certain of its employees  
represented by the United Steelworkers of America, AFL-CIO, and  
Local Union No. 2958 thereof, involving the Stellite Division plant of  
Union Carbide Corporation located at Kokomo, Indiana; and
W HEREAS, such dispute has resulted in a strike which will, in  
my opinion, if permitted to continue, affect a substantial part of the  
military aircraft engine industry, which industry isengaged in trade,  
commerce, transportation, transmission, or communication among the  
several States or with foreign nations, or engaged in the production of  
goods for commerce, and which strike, if permitted to continue, will  
imperil the national safety:
NOW THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by  
Section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act of 1947 (61 Stat.  
155; 29 U.S.C. 176), I hereby create a Board of Inquiry, consisting of  
Mr. Laurence E. Seibel, Chairman, Mr. Frank J. Dugan and Mr.  
Garth L. Mangum, whom I appoint to inquire into the issues involved  
in this dispute.
The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II  
of such Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance  
with the provisions of Section 206 of such Act on or before December  
20,1966.
Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence  
to perform such other functions as may be required under such Act.

Identity: the held Federal Register text (31 FR 16301, the issue of December 21, 1966) is Executive Order 11321, dated December 19, 1966; it is headed with the title Creating a Board of Inquiry to Report on a Labor Dispute Affecting the Military Aircraft Engine Industry of the United States, names the Union Carbide Corporation dispute, and is dated December 19, 1966. The dossier's clause inventory for this order covers neighbouring Federal Register documents, not this order, so I replaced it with the order's own operative text. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier. 
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states a report deadline (on or before December 20, 1966) and a sentence that the Board shall continue in existence after its report; it states no date on which the Board or the order ends. The deadline is not an end and the continuing-existence sentence is the opposite of an own-terms end at the report. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553, and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 shows no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create and appoint the Board, state its powers by reference to Title II of the Act, set the report deadline, continue the Board in existence) depends on this order and on the one dispute it addressed; the Board's statutory powers come from the Labor-Management Relations Act, a separate statute.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself and the dispute was a one-time dispute.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried by correction: the whole operative text (the recitals of the dispute and strike, the creation and membership of the Board, its powers and duties, the report deadline and the continuing-existence sentence). The dossier's sixteen clauses are neighbouring documents on the same pages and are not clauses of this order. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself and the dispute was a one-time dispute. No held claim-grade source shows any command of this order continuing when it was revoked.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11324 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order (32 FR 1075, Federal Register of January 31, 1967, signed January 28, 1967) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference (designated in attached List A) and certain of their employees represented by the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, International Brotherhood of Boilermakers, Iron Ship Builders, Blacksmiths, Forgers & Helpers, Sheet Metal Workers' International Association, International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, Brotherhood Railway Carmen of America, and International Brotherhood of Firemen and Oilers, functioning through the Railway Employes' Department, AFL-CIO (disputes); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by February 27, 1967); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by February 27, 1967) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date.

CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES
BETWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace 
Workers; International Brotherhood of Boilermakers, Iron Ship­
builders, Blacksmiths, Forgers &  Helpers; Sheet Metal Workers’  
International Association; International Brotherhood of Electrical 
Workers; Brotherhood Railway Carmen of America; International 
Brotherhood of Firemen and Oilers functioning through the Railway 
Employes’  Department, AFL-CIO, labor organizations; and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 TJ.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a board ox three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, 
or by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

Presidential Documents
Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES
BETWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace 
Workers; International Brotherhood of Boilermakers, Iron Ship­
builders, Blacksmiths, Forgers &  Helpers; Sheet Metal Workers’  
International Association; International Brotherhood of Electrical 
Workers; Brotherhood Railway Carmen of America; International 
Brotherhood of Firemen and Oilers functioning through the Railway 
Employes’  Department, AFL-CIO, labor organizations; and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 TJ.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a board ox three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, 
or by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (32 FR 1075, the issue of January 31, 1967) is the order itself: its number, Executive Order 11324, is printed in a displaced heading after the text, and it creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated January 28, 1967. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by February 27, 1967), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by February 27, 1967) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11343 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order (32 FR 6085, Federal Register of April 18, 1967, signed April 12, 1967) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between The Long Island Rail Road, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers and International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, labor organizations (three disputes); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by May 12, 1967); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by The Long Island Rail Road or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 170 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated May 12, 1967. Thirty days after May 12, 1967 is June 11, 1967. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on May 12, 1967, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on June 11, 1967.

Executive Order 11343
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE THE DISPUTES
BETWEEN THE LONG ISLAND RAIL ROAD AND CERTAIN OF ITS
EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS, three disputes exist between The Long Island Rail  
Road, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the  
Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, International Brotherhood of  
Electrical Workers and International Association of Machinists and  
Aerospace Workers, labor organizations;  and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce  
to such a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essen­
tial transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by  
Section 10 of the Railway Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I hereby 
create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to investigate  
these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or other­
wise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to  
these disputes within 30 days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended,  
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report  
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by  
The Long Island Rail Road, or by its employees, in the conditions out  
< ? f which these disputes arose.

Identity: the held Federal Register text (32 FR 6085, the issue of April 18, 1967) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 11343, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated April 12, 1967. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11356 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11356
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, a labor 
organization; and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended ; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service :
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a board oi three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The Board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or 
by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11356 (1967-05-30, 32 FR 8019) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11356.txt, 32 FR 8019, PDF pages 7-8) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"within thirty days from the date of this order\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause adds the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Domestic and International Business to section 305 of Executive Order No. 10973. Executive Order 12163 (signed September 29, 1979; 44 FR 56673) states in section 1-903(a) that the following are revoked: "(1) Executive Order No. 10973 of November 3,1961, as amended;" and in section 1-905 "The provisions of this order shall become effective as of October 1,1979." Its section 1-505 establishes a Development Loan Committee and its section 1-506 a Development Coordination Committee, which are new committees under that order and are not treated as keeping this order in force. Executive Order 11579 section 4(d) (1971) supersedes Executive Order No. 10973 only insofar as provisions conflict; it names no section of this order's insertion and no source shows it extinguished the amendment, so it is not an end. Executive Order 11841 adds a separate section 306 to the same parent and does not touch section 305.

1969 C o u n ty A creage A llotm ents  
§ 728.356 Basis and purpose.
(a) The county acreage allotments  
for 1969 crop wheat contained herein

of the Agricultural Adjustm ent Act of  
1938, as amended. The purpose of this

State wheat acreage allotm ents, less re­

mended by the respective ASC State com­
m ittees for 1969.

ments for wheat, less a reserve of not to

farm s, shall be apportioned by the Secre-
tary among the counties in the State on

allotm ent in each county, including all  
amounts allotted to the county, adjusted  
to the extent deemed necessary by the  
Secretary in order to establish a fair  
and equitable apportionment base for  
each county, taking into consideration  
established crop rotation practices, esti­
m ated decrease in farm  allotm ents be­
cause of loss of history, and other rele­
vant factors.
(c) The 1969 State acreage allotm ents  
for wheat less reserves for (1) new farm s, 
and (2) appeals, corrections, and missed  
farm s were apportioned among the  
counties in the various States as follows :
(d) (1) T o each 1968 county wheat  
allotm ent determined under section  
334(b) of the Act, as amended, and pub­
lished in the F ederal  R egister  of August  
11, 1967 (32 F.R . 11609) was added the  
sum of 1968 allotm ent acreage allocated  
to counties in each State from  the na­
tional acreage reserve and the special  
acreage reserve to increase allotments on  
eligible farm s in designated counties  
where wheat is a m ajor incom e-produc­
ing crop. The resulting preliminary  
apportionment bases for each county  
were (i) adjusted to reflect the net plus  
or minus change in 1968 wheat allotm ent 
resulting from  the transfer of farm s to  
other counties for administrative pur­
poses, and (ii) were adjusted downward  
to the extent of the sum of 1968 wheat  
allotm ent received from  farm s going out 
of agricultural production.
(2) Adjustm ents in county prelim i­
nary apportionment bases for estab­
lished crop rotation practices and other  
relevant factors were made to the exr  
tent deemed necessary to establish a fair  
and equitable .apportionm ent base for  
each county. The State wheat acreage  
allotm ent less a reserve for new farm s  
and a reserve for appeals and correc­
tions and missed farm s was distributed

county’s apportionment base determined

hereof show the apportionment of the  
1969 State wheat acreage allotm ent to  
counties. The reserve acreage for new  
farm s and the reserve for appeals, cor­
rections of errors and missed farm s w ith­

tion.

erations shortly, it is hereby found that

date of the filing of this document with  
the Director, Office of the Federal  
Register.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (33 FR 10625, issue of July 26, 1968) is Executive Order 11417, adding an Assistant Secretary of Commerce to the membership of the Development Loan Committee. I read the whole order, a single operative paragraph: Executive Order No. 10973, as amended, "is hereby further amended by inserting in section 305" the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Domestic and International Business. The held text layer also carries neighbouring Commerce regulations on the same pages, which are not part of the order. End: the parent was revoked by Executive Order 12163, effective October 1, 1979, Executive Order 12163 (signed September 29, 1979; 44 FR 56673) states in section 1-903(a) that the following are revoked: "(1) Executive Order No. 10973 of November 3,1961, as amended;" and in section 1-905 "The provisions of this order shall become effective as of October 1,1979." Its section 1-505 establishes a Development Loan Committee and its section 1-506 a Development Coordination Committee, which are new committees under that order and are not treated as keeping this order in force. Executive Order 11579 section 4(d) (1971) supersedes Executive Order No. 10973 only insofar as provisions conflict; it names no section of this order's insertion and no source shows it extinguished the amendment, so it is not an end. The amendment lived only as text inside section 305 of the parent, so it ended with the parent on 1979-10-01. Other held amendments of the parent (Executive Orders 11685, 11816, 11959 and 12118) were checked and do not mention section 305 or this insertion; Executive Order 11841 adds a different section 306. The machine search lists these as chain items only.

Presidential Documents
Executive Order 12163 of September 29, 1979
Administration of Foreign Assistance and Related Functions
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Foreign Assistance A ct of 1961, 
Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1979, the International Development Cooperation 
A ct of 1979, and section 301 of title 3 of the United States Code, and as 
President of the United States, it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-1. UNITED ST A T ES IN TER N A TIO N A L DEVELOPM ENT CO O P E R A T IO N  
A G E N C Y
1-101. E stablish m en t o f the U n ited  Sta tes International D evelopm en t C ooper­
ation A g e n cy . Sections 1, 5, 6, and 8 of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1979 are 
declared effective and the United States International Development Coopera­
tion Agency (hereinafter referred to as “ID C A ” ) is hereby established.
1-102. D elegation o f  Fu n ction s, (a) Exclusive of the functions otherwise 
delegated, or reserved to the President, by this order, and subject to the 
provisions of this order, there are hereby delegated to the Director of ID C A  
(hereinafter referred to as the “Director” ) all functions conferred upon the 
President by:
(1) the Foreign Assistance A ct of 1961 (22 U .S .C . 2151 et seg.); (hereinafter 
referred to as the “A c t” );
(2) the latin American Development A ct (22 U .S .C . 1942 et seq.)\
(3) section 402 of the Mutual Security Act of 1954 (22 U.S.C. 1922);
(4) section 413(b) of the International Security Assistance and Arms Export 
Control Act of 1976 (22 U.S.C. 2431); and
(5) title IV  of the International Development Cooperation A ct of 1979 (22 
U .S .C . 3501 et se q.) (hereinafter referred to as the “ID C A ct of 1979” ).
(b) The functions under sections 116(e), 491(b), 491(c), 607, 627, 628, 630(3), and 
666 of the A ct, and section 403(e) of the ID C A ct of 1979, delegated to the 
Director shall be exercised in consultation with the Secretary of State.
(c) The functions under section 125(b) of the A ct delegated to the Director 
shall be exercised in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury and, with 
regard to the United Nations Development Program, in consultation with the 
Secretary of State.
\
(d) The Director shall exercise the functions of the President under sections 
301(a), 301(e)(1), 301(e)(3), and 305 of the A ct only insofar as they pertain to 
the United Nations Development Program, U NICEF, the Organization of 
American States Technical Assistance Funds, the United Nations Capital 
Development Fund, the United Nations Educational and Training Program for 
Southern Africa, the United Nations/Food and Agriculture Organization 
World Food Program, the Food and Agriculture Organization Post-Harvest 
Losses Fund, the United Nations Disaster Relief Organization, and any other 
international programs whose purpose is primarily developmental.
(e) In carrying out the functions under section 653 of the A ct that are delegated 
to the Director, the Director shall consult with the Director of the O ffice of 
Management and Budget.
(f) To the extent practicable, the Director will exercise functions relating to 
Foreign Service personnel in a manner that will assure maximum compatibil-

ity among agencies authorizied by law to utilize the Foreign Service personnel

(g) In exercising functions under the A ct arising from later-enacted amend­
ments to any law specified in subsection (a) of this section that relate directly

ment Loan Committee in accordance with section 122(e) of the A ct which shall

tary of Labor; the Under Secretary of Energy; a Deputy Special Representative

interest to Federal agencies not represented on the Committee under subsec­
tion (a) of this section, the Chair of the Committee may consult with such 
agencies and may invite them to designate representatives to participate in 
meetings and deliberations of the Committee.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the Illinois Central Railroad Company, the Louisville & Nashville Railroad Company and the Belt Railway Company of Chicago and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11433 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11433
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE ILLINOIS CENTRAL RAILROAD COMPANY, LOUISVILLE &
NASHVILLE RAILROAD COMPANY, AND THE BELT RAILWAY COM­
PANY OF CHICAGO, AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S disputes exist between the Illinois Central Railroad 
Company, Louisville & Nashville Railroad Company, and the Belt 
Railway Company of Chicago, carriers, and certain of their employees 
represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organi­
zation ; and
W H E R E A S these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions o f the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W H E R E A S these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential 
transportation service:
N OW  T H E R E FO R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a Board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member o f the Board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The Board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
these disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the Board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
Illinois Central Railroad Company, Louisville and Nashville Railroad 
Company, and the Belt Railway Company of Chicago, or by their 
employees, in the conditions out of which these disputes arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11433 (1968-11-06, 33 FR 16379) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the Illinois Central Railroad Company, the Louisville & Nashville Railroad Company and the Belt Railway Company of Chicago and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11433.txt, 33 FR 16379, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"within thirty days from the date of this order\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the Board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's sole operative sentence suspends section 6372 of title 10 of the United States Code under the authority of section 6386(c) of that title. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11436 Suspending provisions of section 6372 of title 10, U.S.C., relating to retirement or retention on the"). The order states no duration, so no own-terms end applies. Earlier candidate ends that do not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; neither is the end because neither names EO 11436): (1) the National Emergencies Act, Pub. L. 94-412 (Sept. 14, 1976), whose section 101(a) terminated, two years after enactment, powers possessed as a result of national emergencies then in effect; its section 502(a)(8) provides that the Act shall not apply to "Sections 3313, 6386(c), and 8313 of title 10, United States" Code, so that termination did not reach the section 6386(c) authority this order rests on (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10976_Pub._L._94-412_National_Emergencies_Act_sec._101_a_90_Stat._1255_Sept._14_1976_status_d1e4940870.txt, text sha256 9af91c5062c556d26e97baaad68d89a4aa6cbfbb51937898bc13ef801d78a350). (2) The Defense Officer Personnel Management Act, Pub. L. 96-513 (Dec. 12, 1980), whose section 335 provides that "The following sections of chapter 573 are repealed:" and lists, among others, sections 6372 (the section this order suspends) and 6386 (the section whose subsection (c) is the order's authority), effective September 15, 1981 under section 701(a) (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11436_Defense_Officer_Personnel_Management_Act_Pub._L._96-513_Dec._12_1980_94_Stat._2835_in_bdcccb89ac.txt, text sha256 c3ab6a35c6abc89d1a7cf8da82a3857809878054424edc8731240edb46dc7970). Section 702 of that Act preserves the suspended status of a provision that is amended, not repealed, so it does not apply to the repealed section 6372; section 703 preserves matured rights, penalties and proceedings. After September 15, 1981 the suspension had no statutory provision left to operate on, but under the ruling the repeal is a disclosed candidate, and the order's end remains the instrument that names it.

EO 11436 (signed 1968-12-02; 33 FR 17943, Federal Register of December 4, 1968) suspends section 6372 of title 10, United States Code (retirement or retention on the active list of certain rear admirals in the Navy), citing as its sole authority "section 6386 (c) of title 10" of the United States Code. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11436.txt, PDF page 7); its number, title and the December 4, 1968 issue line match the census register row, but the extracted text prints no page number, so I did not confirm the page 17943 citation from it. Its single operative sentence is the whole order, and it states no duration. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes it by number; that express revocation is the first end. L. 94-412 (Sept. 14, 1976), whose section 101(a) terminated, two years after enactment, powers possessed as a result of national emergencies then in effect; its section 502(a)(8) provides that the Act shall not apply to "Sections 3313, 6386(c), and 8313 of title 10, United States" Code, so that termination did not reach the section 6386(c) authority this order rests on (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10976_Pub._L._94-412_National_Emergencies_Act_sec._101_a_90_Stat._1255_Sept._14_1976_status_d1e4940870.txt, text sha256 9af91c5062c556d26e97baaad68d89a4aa6cbfbb51937898bc13ef801d78a350). operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11443 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". This order (34 FR 541, Federal Register of January 15, 1969, signed January 13, 1969) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference (designated in attached List A) and certain of their employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, a labor organization (disputes); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by February 12, 1969); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by February 12, 1969) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, a labor 
organization; and
WHEREAS these disputes haye not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the Board shall be pecuniar­
ily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or 
by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (34 FR 541, the issue of January 15, 1969) is the order itself: its number, Executive Order 11443, is printed in a displaced heading after the text, and it creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated January 13, 1969. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.

The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by February 12, 1969) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11444 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.

Executive Order 11444
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, a labor organi­
zation ; and
WHEREAS these disputes have not heretofore Keen adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to 
a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to in­
vestigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or 
by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.
