research_rationale:
EO 11444 (1969-01-13, 34 FR 543) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11444.txt, 34 FR 543, PDF pages 7-8) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"within thirty days from the date of this order\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11445 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.

Executive Order 11445
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen, a labor organiza­tion ; and
WHEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended ; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of thè National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to 
a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as aihended (45 TJ.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create à board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As prpvided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or by 
their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11445 (1969-01-13, 34 FR 545) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11445.txt, 34 FR 545, PDF pages 9-10) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"within thirty days from the date of this order\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(a)(4) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11578, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2 of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(a)(4) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11578, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3(2) of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(a)(4) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11578, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause. The Federal agency member list in this clause was amended by EO 11882 (Atomic Energy Commission replaced by the Energy Research and Development Administration), by EO 12038 (that Administration replaced by the Department of Energy, effective as of October 1, 1977) and by EO 12148 (Federal Emergency Management Agency added, effective July 15, 1979); each is a later event and none ended the clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3(3) of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(a)(4) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11578, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3(4) of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(a)(4) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11578, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 4 of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(a)(4) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11578, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause.

Title 3—The President
EXECUTIVE ORDER 11578
Establishment of the O hio River Basin Commission
W H ERE A S . the Water Resources Planning Act (79 Stat. 244, 42  
U.S.C . 1962 et seq.)  provides for the establishment of river basin water  
and related land resources commissions; and
W H EREAS the Governors of the States of the Ohio River drainage  
basin, excluding the Tennessee River drainage basin, and the Water  
Resources Council have requested, or concurred in, the establishment  
of such a commission :
N O W , T H E R E FO R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 201 of the Water Resources Planning Act (42 U.S.C,. 1962b),  
and as President of the United States, it is ordered as follows :
Section  1. Ohio River Basin Commission.  It is hereby declared that  
the Ohio River Basin Commission is established under the provisions of  
Title II of the Water Resources Planning Act (42 U .S.C . 1962b et seq.).
Sec. 2. Jurisdiction of the Commission.  It is hereby determined  
that the jurisdiction of the Ohio River Basin Commission referred to in  
section 1  of this order shall extend to those portions of the States of Ken­
tucky, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, N ew  York, North Carolina, Ohio,  
Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia, and West Virginia that are located  
.within the Ohio River drainage basin, excluding the Tennessee River  
drainage basin.
Sec. 3. Membership of the Commission.  It is hereby determined that,  
in accordance with section 202 of the Act (42 U .S.C . 1962b— 1  ), the  
Commission shall consist of the following members:
( 1  ) a Chairman to be appointed by the President,
(2 ) one member from each of the following Federal departments and  
agencies :  Department of Agriculture, Department of the Army, Depart­
ment of Commerce, Department of Health, Education, and Welfare,  
Department of Housing and Urban Development, Department of the  
Interior, Department of Transportation, Federal Power Commission,  
Atomic Energy Commission, and the Environmental Protection Agency,
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 36, NO. 11— SATURDAY, JANUARY 16, 1971

(3 ) one member from each of the following States: Kentucky, Illi­
nois, Indiana, Maryland, N ew  York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsyl­
vania, Tennessee, and West Virginia, and a member from Virginia when  
authorized by the legislature of that State, and
(4 ) one member from each interstate agency created by an inter­
state compact to which the consent of Congress has been given and  
whose jurisdiction extends to the waters of the area specified in section 2.
Sec . 4. Functions, Powers, and Duties.  T he Commission and its  
officers, members, and employees shall perform and exercise, with respect  
to the area specified in section 2 of this order, their respective functions,  
powers, and duties as set out in Title II of the Water Resources Planning  
Act.

sion shall report to the President through the Water Resources Council.

research_rationale:
EO 11578 (Establishment of the Ohio River Basin Commission), signed 1971-01-13. The order establishes the Ohio River Basin Commission (Section 1), fixes its jurisdiction (Section 2) and membership (Section 3: a Chairman, Federal agency members, State members and interstate agency members), its functions (Section 4) and a reporting section (Section 5). Its held text has no sunset or termination provision.  First end: Section 5(a)(4) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11578, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end.  Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, 4 hits for this order), the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 (4 hits) and the Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition-note search (5 hits). They are leads only; the end, the later events and the savings were decided from the held Federal Register texts named in this claim. Search of the held order texts for this order's number (the packet records a bounded number-citation search over its lookup corpus, excluding clause-draft copies): apart from the order's own copies, the matching files are EO 11882, EO 12038, EO 12148, EO 12319.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11650 (signed 1972-02-16, 37 FR 3739) orders, under section 6103(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, that returns for stated taxes 'shall be open to inspection' by certain classes of persons and State and Federal Government establishments in accordance with Treasury Decision 6543 and its amendments. The order is a single continuing authorization. The operative words include "is hereby ordered that returns made in respect of the taxes imposed by". First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25): "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the entry at offset 25703 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11650 Providing for inspection of tax returns by certain persons and State and Federal establishments", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986". Held U.S. Code editorial note (release point 119-121): "Executive Orders 10738, 10906, 10954, 10962, 11102, 11206, 11213, 11650, and 11706, listed above, were revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12553, Feb. 25, 1986, 51 F.R. 7237." (26 note to 26 U.S.C. 6103)
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 6103(a) of the 
Internal Revenue Code of 1954, as amended (26 U.S.C. 6 1 0 3 (a)), it 
is hereby ordered that returns made in respect of the taxes imposed by 
chapters 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 11, 12, and 32, subchapters B and C of chapter 33, 
subchapter B of chapter 37, and chapter 41 of such Code shall be open 
to inspection by certain classes of persons and State and Federal Govern­
ment establishments in accordance and upon compliance with the rules 
and regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury in Treasury 
decision 6543, relating to inspection and use of returns by such classes 
of persons and State and Federal Government establishments, approved 
by the President on January 17, 1961, the amendments thereto approved 
by the President on April 4, 1963, and March 18, 1965, and the amend­
ment thereto approved by me this date.

The Federal Register provides a uniform system for making 
available to the public regulations and legal notices issued by 
Federal agencies. These include Presidential proclamations and 
Executive Orders and Federal agency documents having general 
applicability and legal effect, documents required to be 
published by Act of Congress and other Federal agency 
documents of public interest. Documents are on file for public 
inspection in the Office of the Federal Register the day before 
they are published, unless earlier filing is requested by the 
issuing agency.

free of postage, for $75.00 per year, or $45.00 for six months, 
payable in advance. The change for individual copies is $1.00 
for each issue, or $1.00 for each group of pages as actually 
bound. Remit check or money order, made payable to the 
Superintendent of Documents, U.S. Government Printing Office, 
Washington, D.C. 20402.

appearing in the Federal Register.

to the telephone numbers listed under INFORMATION AND

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3 of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(a)(5) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11658, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3(1) of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(a)(5) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11658, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3(2) of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(a)(5) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11658, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause. The Federal agency member list in this clause was amended by EO 11882 (Atomic Energy Commission replaced by the Energy Research and Development Administration), by EO 12038 (that Administration replaced by the Department of Energy, effective as of October 1, 1977) and by EO 12148 (Federal Emergency Management Agency added, effective July 15, 1979); each is a later event and none ended the clause.

Section 2. Management of Emergency Planning and Assistance
2-1. G eneral.
2-101. The Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency shall 
establish Federal policies for, and coordinate, all civil defense and civil 
emergency planning, management, mitigation, and assistance functions of 
Executive agencies.
2-102. The Director shall periodically review and evaluate the civil defense 
and civil emergency functions of the Executive agencies. In order to improve 
the efficiency and effectiveness of those functions, the Director shall recom­
mend to the President alternative methods of providing Federal planning, 
management, mitigation, and assistance.
2-103. The Director shall be responsible for the coordination of efforts to 
promote dam safety, for the coordination of natural and nuclear disaster 
warning systems, and for the coordination of preparedness and planning to 
reduce the consequences of major terrorist incidents.
2-104. The Director shall represent the President in working with State and 
local governments and private sector to stimulate vigorous participation in 
civil emergency preparedness, mitigation, response, and recovery programs.
2-105. The Director shall provide an annual report to the President for 
subsequent transmittal to the Congress on the functions of the Federal Emer­
gency Management Agency.The report shall assess the current overall state of 
effectiveness of Federal civil defense and civil emergency functions, organiza­
tions, resources, and systems and recommencé measures to be taken to im­
prove planning, management, assistance, and relief by all levels of govern­
ment, the private sector, and volunteer organizations.
2-2. Im plem entationv
2-201. In executing the functions under this Order, the Director shall develop 
policies which provide that all civil defense and civil emergency functions, 
resources, and systems of Executive agencies are:
(a) founded on the use of existing organizations, resources, and systems to the 
maximum extent practicable;
(b) integrated effectively with organizations, resources, and programs of State 
and îocal governments, the private sector and volunteer organizations; and
(c) developed, tested and utilized to prepare for, mitigate, respond to and 
recover from the effects on the population of all forms bf emergencies.
2-202. Assignments of civil emergency functions shall, whenever possible, be 
based on extensions (under emergency conditions) of the regular missions of 
the Executive agencies.
2-203. For purposes of this Order, “civil emergency” means any accidental, 
natural, man-caused, or wartime emergency or threat thereof, which causes or 
may cause substantial injury or harm to the population or substantial damage 
to or loss of property.
2-204. In order that civil defense planning continues to be fully compatible 
with the Nation’s overall strategic policy, and in order to maintain an effective 
link between strategic nuclear planning and nuclear attack preparedness 
planning, the development of civil defense policies and programs by the 
Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency shall be subject to 
oversight by the Secretary of Defense and the National Security Council.
2-205. To the extent authorized by law and within available resources, the 
Secretary of Defense shall provide the Director of the Federal Emergency 
Management Agency with support for civil defense programs in the areas of 
program development and administration, technical support, research, commu­
nications, transportation, intelligence, and emergency operations.
2-206. All Executive agencies shall cooperate with and assist the Director in 
the performance of his functions.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3(3) of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(a)(5) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11658, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 4 of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(a)(5) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11658, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause.

Establishment of the Missouri River Basin Commission
The Water Resources Planning Act (79 Stat. 244; 42 U.S.G. 1962 
et seq. ) provides for the establishment of river basin water and related 
land resources commissions. In conformity with the requirements of that 
act a majority of the Governors of the States of the Missouri River drain­
age basin, as defined in Section 2 of this order, and the Water Resources 
Council have requested, or concurred in, the establishment of such 
a Commission.
N O W , TH E RE FO R E, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 201 of the Water Resources Planning Act (42 U.S.C. 1962b), 
and as President of the United.States, it is ordered as follows:
Section  1. Missouri River Basin Commission.  It is hereby declared 
that the Missouri Riyer Basin Commission is established under the provi­
sions of Title I I  of the Water Resources Planning Act (42 U.S.C. 1962b 
et seq.).
S e c. 2. Jurisdiction of the Commission.  It is hereby determined that 
the jurisdiction of the Missouri River Basin Commission referred to in 
Section 1  of this order shall extend to the State of Nebraska and those 
portions of the States of Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, 
Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Wyoming that are located 
within the Missouri River drainage basin, defined as the drainage basin 
of the Missouri River above a point immediately below the mouth of the 
Gasconade River.
S e c. 3. Membership of the Commission.  It is hereby determined that, 
in accordance with Section 202 of the Act (42 U.S.C. 1962b— 1  ), the 
Commission shall consist of the following members :
( 1  ) a Chairman to be appointed by the President,
(2 ) one member from each of the following Federal departments and 
agencies: Department of Agriculture; Department of the Army; Depart­
ment of Commerce; Department of Health, Education, and Welfare; 
Department of Housing and Urban Development; Department of the 
Interior; Department of Transportation; Federal Power Commission; 
Atomic Energy Commission; and the Environmental Protection Agency; 
such member to be appointed by the head of the department or inde­
pendent agency he represents.
(3 ) one member from each of the following States: Colorado, Iowa, 
Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, North Dakota, South 
Dakota, and Wyoming.
(4 ) one member from each interstate agency created by an interstate 
compact to which the consent of the Congress has been given and whose 
jurisdiction extends to the waters of the area specified in Section 2.
S e c. 4. Functions, Powers, and Duties.  The Commission and its officers, 
members, and employees shall perform and exercise, with respect to the

research_rationale:
EO 11658 (Establishment of the Missouri River Basin Commission), signed 1972-03-22. The order establishes the Missouri River Basin Commission (Section 1), fixes its jurisdiction (Section 2) and membership (Section 3: a Chairman, Federal agency members, State members and interstate agency members), its functions (Section 4) and international coordination (Section 5) and reporting (Section 6) sections. Its held text has no sunset or termination provision.  First end: Section 5(a)(5) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11658, as amended, among the orders revoked effective October 1, 1981, so the revocation took effect on 1981-10-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on September 30, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end.  Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, 4 hits for this order), the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 (4 hits) and the Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition-note search (5 hits). They are leads only; the end, the later events and the savings were decided from the held Federal Register texts named in this claim. Search of the held order texts for this order's number (the packet records a bounded number-citation search over its lookup corpus, excluding clause-draft copies): apart from the order's own copies, the matching files are EO 11882, EO 12038, EO 12148, EO 12319.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(b) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11659, as amended, among the orders revoked effective January 1, 1982, so the revocation took effect on 1982-01-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on December 31, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2 of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(b) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11659, as amended, among the orders revoked effective January 1, 1982, so the revocation took effect on 1982-01-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on December 31, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause. EO 11737 rewrote this section; recorded as a later event.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3 of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(b) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11659, as amended, among the orders revoked effective January 1, 1982, so the revocation took effect on 1982-01-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on December 31, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3(2) of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(b) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11659, as amended, among the orders revoked effective January 1, 1982, so the revocation took effect on 1982-01-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on December 31, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause. The Federal agency member list in this clause was amended by EO 11882 (Atomic Energy Commission replaced by the Energy Research and Development Administration), by EO 12038 (that Administration replaced by the Department of Energy, effective as of October 1, 1977) and by EO 12148 (Federal Emergency Management Agency added, effective July 15, 1979); each is a later event and none ended the clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3(3) of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(b) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11659, as amended, among the orders revoked effective January 1, 1982, so the revocation took effect on 1982-01-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on December 31, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause. EO 11737 rewrote the State list in this item; recorded as a later event.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3(4) of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(b) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11659, as amended, among the orders revoked effective January 1, 1982, so the revocation took effect on 1982-01-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on December 31, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 4 of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(b) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11659, as amended, among the orders revoked effective January 1, 1982, so the revocation took effect on 1982-01-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on December 31, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 5 of the held order text is a separate command of this order. First end: Section 5(b) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11659, as amended, among the orders revoked effective January 1, 1982, so the revocation took effect on 1982-01-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on December 31, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause. EO 11737 rewrote this section; recorded as a later event.

THE PRESIDENT 6047
E X E C U T I V E  O R D E R  11659
Establishment of the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission
The Water Resources Planning Act (79 Stat. 244; 42 U.S.C. 1962 
et seq.)  provides for the establishment of river basin water and related 
land resources commissions. In conformity with the requirements of that 
act the Governors of the States of the Upper Mississippi River drainage 
basin, as defined in Section 2 of this order, and the Water Resources 
Council have requested, or concurred in, the establishment of such a 
Commission.
N O W , TH E RE FO R E, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 201 of the Water Resources Planning Act (42 U.S.C. 1962b), 
and as President of the United States, it is ordered as follows :
Section  1. Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission.  It is hereby 
declared that the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission is estab­
lished under the provisions of Title I I  of the Water Resources Planning 
Act (42 U.S.C. 1962b et seq.).
•  Se c. 2. Jurisdiction of the Commission.  It is hereby determined that the 
jurisdiction of the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission referred 
to in Section 1  of this order shall extend to those portions of the States 
of Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, and Wisconsin that are located 
within the Upper Mississippi River drainage basin, defined as the drain­
age basin of the Mississippi River above the mouth of the Ohio River, 
excluding the drainage basin of the Missouri River above a point 
immediately below the mouth of the Gasconade River.
S e c. 3. Membership of the Commission.  It is hereby determined that, 
in accordance with Section 202 of the Act (42 U.S.C. 1962b-l), the 
Commission shall consist of the following members :
( 1  ) a Chairman to be appointed by the President,
(2 ) one member from each of the following Federal departments and 
agencies: Department of Agriculture; Department of the Army; Depart­
ment of Commerce; Department of Health, Education, and Welfare; 
Department of Housing and Urban Development; Department of the 
Interior; Department of Transportation; Federal Power Commission; 
Atomic Energy Commission; and the Environmental Protection Agency; 
such member to be appointed by the head of the department or inde­
pendent agency he represents,
(3 ) one member from each of the following States: Illinois, Iowa, 
Minnesota, Missouri, and Wisconsin,
(4 ) one member from each interstate agency created by an interstate 
compact to which the consent of Congress has been given and whose 
jurisdiction extends to the waters of the area specified in Section 2.
S e c. 4. Functions, Powers, and Duties.  The Commission and its officers, 
members, and employees shall perform and exercise, with respect to the
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 37, NO. 58— FRIDAY, MARCH 24, 1972

6048 THE PRESIDENT
area specified in Section 2 of this order, their respective functions, powers,
and duties as set out in Title I I  of the Water Resources Planning Act.
S e c. 5. Consultation with Adjoining States.  The Commission is ex­
pected to provide for procedures for consultation with the States of 
Indiana, Michigan, and South Dakota on any matter which might affect 
the water and related land resources of the headwater drainages of the 
Mississippi River Basin in those States and to give notice to those States 
of meetings of the Commission.
S e c. 6. Reporting to the President.  The Chairman of the Commission 
shall report to the President through the Water Resources Council.

research_rationale:
EO 11659 (Establishment of the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission), signed 1972-03-22. The order establishes the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission (Section 1), fixes its jurisdiction (Section 2) and membership (Section 3), functions (Section 4), consultation with adjoining States (Section 5) and reporting (Section 6). Its held text has no sunset or termination provision. EO 11737 (1973) rewrote Sections 2 and 5, changed the State list in Section 3(3) and inserted a new international-coordination section, redesignating Section 6 as Section 7. First end: Section 5(b) of EO 12319 (River Basin Commissions, signed 1981-09-09 and published at 46 FR 45591) names Executive Order No. 11659, as amended, among the orders revoked effective January 1, 1982, so the revocation took effect on 1982-01-01. The Federal Register issue text also carries a 3 CFR index entry for this order recording the revocation by EO 12319 with the same effective date (the text layer is OCR with broken letter spacing, so I describe it without quotation). Section 1 of EO 12319 lists the commission established by this order as terminated on December 31, 1981, but it names commissions and not their establishing orders; under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments that is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end.  Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, 7 hits for this order), the eCFR search as of 2026-10-14 (7 hits) and the Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition-note search (6 hits). They are leads only; the end, the later events and the savings were decided from the held Federal Register texts named in this claim. Search of the held order texts for this order's number (the packet records a bounded number-citation search over its lookup corpus, excluding clause-draft copies): apart from the order's own copies, the matching files are EO 11737, EO 11882, EO 12038, EO 12148, EO 12319.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11663 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". This order (37 FR 6647, Federal Register of April 1, 1972, signed March 31, 1972) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference (designated in attached lists) and certain of their employees represented by the Sheet Metal Workers' International Association, a labor organization (disputes); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by April 30, 1972); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of the board created by this order (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated April 30, 1972. Thirty days after April 30, 1972 is May 30, 1972. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on April 30, 1972, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on May 30, 1972.

=== PDF page 7 of 88 ===
Presidential Documents
Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate Disputes Between the
Carriers Represented by the National Railway Labor Conference
and Certain of Their Employees
WHEREAS, disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference designated in lists attached hereto 
and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees represented by 
the Sheet Metal Workers’  International Association, a labor organization; 
and
WHEREAS, these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
WHEREAS, these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to 
a degree such as to deprive sections of the country of essential transporta­
tion service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I hereby create a board, of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any 
carrier.
The Board shall report its finding to the President with respect to 
these disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to 
the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or by 
their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.
Title 3—The President
E X E C U T IV E  O R D E R  11663

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (37 FR 6647, the issue of April 1, 1972) is the order itself: its number, Executive Order 11663, is printed in a displaced heading after the text, and it creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated March 31, 1972. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by April 30, 1972), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. A held lead copy of the report of the board created by this order (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated April 30, 1972. Thirty days after April 30, 1972 is May 30, 1972. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on April 30, 1972, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on May 30, 1972. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

retag.note: Filed under the 2026-10-21 reading; the 2026-10-28 ruling point 3 governs (R3). The recorded end instrument is the formal disposition; the first end is unresolved and bounded no later than it. Not re-researched.

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11694 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order (38 FR 729, Federal Register of January 4, 1973, signed January 2, 1973) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood Railway Carmen of the United States and Canada, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by February 1, 1973); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of the board created by this order (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated February 1, 1973. Thirty days after February 1, 1973 is March 3, 1973. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on February 1, 1973, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on March 3, 1973.

Presidential Docum ents
Creating an Emergency Board to Investigate a Dispute Between the
Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and Certain of Its
Employees
W H EREAS, a dispute exists between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson 
Corporation and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood 
Railway Carmen of the United States and Canada, a labor organization; 
and
W H EREAS, this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the 
provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W H EREAS, this dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation 
Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a de­
gree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential transportation 
service:
N O W , T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to in­
vestigate this dispute. N o member of the board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any 
carrier.
The board shall report its finding to the President with respect to the 
dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, from 
this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the 
President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the Port 
Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation, or by its employees, in the con­
ditions out of which the dispute arose.
Title 3—The President

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (38 FR 729, the issue of January 4, 1973) is the order itself: its number, Executive Order 11694, is printed in a displaced heading after the text, and it creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated January 2, 1973. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.

The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11706 (signed 1973-03-08, 38 FR 6663) orders, under section 6103(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, that returns for stated taxes 'shall be open to inspection' by U.S. attorneys and attorneys of the Department of Justice and for use in grand jury proceedings and in litigation in accordance with Treasury Decision 6543 and its amendments. The order is a single continuing authorization. The operative words include "hereby ordered that returns made in respect of the taxes imposed by". First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25): "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the entry at offset 26100 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11706 Providing for inspection of tax returns by U.S. Attorneys and justice Department attorneys for grand", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986". Held U.S. Code editorial note (release point 119-121): "Executive Orders 10738, 10906, 10954, 10962, 11102, 11206, 11213, 11650, and 11706, listed above, were revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12553, Feb. 25, 1986, 51 F.R. 7237." (26 note to 26 U.S.C. 6103)
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 6103(a) of the In­
ternal Revenue Code of 1954, as amended (26 U.S.C. 6103(a)),  it is 
hereby ordered that returns made in respect of the taxes imposed by 
chapters 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 11, 12, and 32, subchapters B and C of chapter 33, 
and chapter 41 of such Code shall be open to inspection by U.S. attorneys 
and attorneys of the Department of Justice and for use in grand jury 
proceedings and in litigation in accordance and upon compliance with 
the rules and regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury in 
Treasury Decision 6543, relating to inspection and use of returns by 
certain classes of persons and State and Federal Government establish­
ments, approved by the President on January 17, 1961, the amendments 
thereto approved by the President on April 4, 1963, March 18, 1965, 
and February 16, 1972, and the amendment thereto approved by me 
this date.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11745 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order (38 FR 30429, Federal Register of November 5, 1973, signed November 1, 1973) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen, AFL-CIO, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by December 1, 1973); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by the Long Island Rail Road or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by December 1, 1973) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date.

THE PRESIDENT 30429
E X E C U T I V E  O R D E R  11745
Creating an Em ergency Board T o  Investigate a  Dispute Between the 
L ong Island R ail R oad and Certain o f Its Employees
W HEREAS, a dispute exists between the Long Island Rail Road and 
certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad 
Signalmen, A F L -C IO , a labor organization; and
W HEREAS, this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the 
provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS, this dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation 
Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a 
degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential transpor­
tation service:
N O W , TH E R EF O R E, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute. N o member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its finding to the President with respect to the 
dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
Long Island Rail Road, or by its employees, in the conditions out of 
which the dispute arose.

End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11771 (signed 1974-03-18, 39 FR 10415) extends to the Liaison Office of the People's Republic of China in Washington, D.C. and its duly notified members the privileges and immunities of diplomatic missions, under the act of April 20, 1973 (Public Law 93-22), with the sentence "T his Executive Order shall be effective as of" followed on the next line by the date April 20, 1973. The order has no sunset or condition of its own. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25): "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the entry at offset 26383 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11771 Extending diplomatic privileges and immunities to the Liaison Office of the People’s Republic of China", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986". Held U.S. Code editorial note (release point 119-121): "Ex. Ord. No. 11771, Mar. 18, 1974, 39 F.R. 10415, which extended diplomatic privileges and immunities to the Liaison Office of the People’s Republic of China in Washington, D.C., was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12553, Feb. 25, 1986, 51 F.R. 7237." (22 note to 22 U.S.C. 288i)

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11852 in the number column of the table (the text layer separates the number column from the subject column for this part of the table, so its subject text is not quoted). This order (40 FR 17239, Federal Register of April 18, 1975, signed April 16, 1975) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference (designated in attached lists) and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railway, Airline, and Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and Station Employees, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within 30 days from the date of the order (due by May 16, 1975); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by May 16, 1975) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 11852
Creating an Emergency Board T o  Investigate a Dispute Between the
Carriers Represented by the National Railway Labor Conference
and Certain o f Their Employees
A  dispute exists between the carriers represented by the National 
Railway Labor Conference designated in lists attached hereto and made 
a part hereof, and certain o f its employees represented by the Brother­
hood o f Railway, Airline, and Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, 
Express and Station Employees, a labor organization; '
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions 
o f the Railway Labor A ct, as am ended; and
This dispute, in the judgm ent o f the National M ediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt interstate com m erce to a degree such 
as to deprive a section o f the country o f essential transportation service:
N O W , T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in m e by 
Section 10 o f the Railway Labor A ct, as amended (45 U .S.C . 1 6 0 ), 
I hereby create a board o f three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute. N o m em ber o f the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization o f railroad employees or 
any carrier.
T he board shall report its finding to the President with respect to the 
dispute within 30 days from  the date o f this order.
As provided by Section 10 o f the Railway Labor A ct, as amended, 
from  this date and for 30 days after the board has made its report to 
the President, n o change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or by 
their employees, in the conditions out o f which the dispute arose. ^

I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
