Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within 30 days from the date of the order (due by May 16, 1975), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by May 16, 1975) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 11876 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The sole paragraph creates a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), directs it to report within 30 days from the date of the order, and restates the section 10 status-quo period from the date of the order until 30 days after the report. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; when it ran out depends on the unrecorded report date. No earlier express end was found.

It creates a board to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Railway Employes’ Department, AFL-CIO and four named brotherhoods. Inventory: the order is a board order whose operative commands are 1 clause(s) as recorded in the dossier (whole). The list of parties attached to the order identifies the dispute and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 11876 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C): the report date and the end of any statutory standstill are spent facts that do not end the order; they are not recorded as later events because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence, so the claim states the functional spending without a date. The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings. Title 3—The President
Executive Order 12085 • September 28,1978
Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Betw een the Norfolk and  
W estern Railw ay Company and Certain of its Employees
A dispute exists between the Norfolk and Western Railway Company and  
certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railway, Airline  
and Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and Station Employes, a  
labor organization;
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
This dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens  
substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a  
section of the country of essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 10 of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1-101. Establishment of Board. There is established a board of three mem­
bers to be appointed by the President to investigate this dispute. No member  
of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of  
railroad employees or any carrier.
1-102. Report. The board shall report its finding to the President with  
respect to the dispute within 30 days from the date of this Order.
1-103. Maintaining Conditions. As provided by Section 10 of the Railway  
Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for 30 days after the board has  
made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Norfolk and Western Railway Company, or by its employees, in  
the conditions out of which the dispute arose.

Title 3—The President
Executive Order 12095 November 2,1978
Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between Wien A ir A laska, Inc.
and Certain Individuals
A  dispute exists between Wien Air Alaska, Inc., and certain individuals  
represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, a labor organization.
Section 44 o f the Airline Deregulation Act o f 1978 (Public Law 95-504)  
directed that the provisions of Section 10 o f the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended, be invoked despite the fact that the National Mediation Board has  
failed to find that the dispute in its judgment substantially threatens to inter­
rupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a section o f the  
country o f essential transportation service.
N O W , THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 44 of the  
Airline Deregulation Act o f 1978 (Public Law 95-504) it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1-101. Establishment o f  Board. There is established a board o f three mem­
bers to be appointed by the President to investigate this dispute. No member  
of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of  
airline employees or any carrier.
1-102. Report. The board shall report its findings to the President with  
respect to the dispute within 30 days from the date o f this Order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 12121 (signed 1979-02-26, 44 FR 11195) amends section 1-102 of EO 12083 by adding two members to the Energy Coordinating Committee, "The Director of the Community Services Administration." and "The Chairman of the Council on Wage and Price Stability."; its only command is that addition and it has no own-terms end. EO 12083 (signed 1978-09-27; held Federal Register text, 43 FR 44813, issue of September 29, 1978) has no sunset or other own-terms end. First end: EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17, 47 FR 36099), whose section 20 reads "Sec. 20. Executive O rder No. 12083, as amended, establishing the Energy" (continuing on the next line: Coordinating Committee, is revoked). EO 12379 does not name EO 12121; it revokes EO 12083 as amended, and because EO 12121's whole operative content is a textual addition to section 1-102 of EO 12083, the revocation of EO 12083 as amended removes the section it amends and ends the clause. EO 12379 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1982-08-17. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note on this order reads "Revoked by: EO 12379, August 17, 1982". Later event: EO 12156 (signed 1979-09-10, 44 FR 53073) adds member (z), the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, to section 1-102 as amended by EO 12121 and leaves the two members added by EO 12121 in place, so it is a later amendment event, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21, strike-and-insert). Disclosed earlier candidates under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; neither names EO 12121, so neither is the end): (1) the Community Services Administration. An Office of the Federal Register editorial note in the held 1989 codification text (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_12344.txt, sha256 747052eb81a27f8e0040ae9c8bd5f478841e46df4e9ba7c683587599624bdbf8; the same note is in EO_12160.txt) states that "The Community Services Administration was abolished through" the repeal of the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964 "by Pub . L. 97-35 (95 Stat . 519, 42 U.S.C. 2941)". The note gives no effective date and the statute is not held, so the date the Director's office ceased is not fixed by a held source beyond falling in or after 1981 and before EO 12379. (2) The Council on Wage and Price Stability. An editorial note in the held 1989 codification text (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_12154.txt, sha256 bff5d25514c124e6fc4decb93eeae7ae824204d396dcb03bca755207208da54a) states that "The Council on Wage and Price Stability was abolished by Execu-" tive Order 12288 of Jan. 29, 1981. The held Federal Register text of EO 12288 (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12288.txt, sha256 995315c4dc9f143a80b008ebfff389f119a3d67afbba6f82fc37508a35da5e6d) does not abolish the Council: it revokes EO 12092 and authorizes the heads of agencies, "including" the Council on Wage and Price Stability, to take steps to terminate actions adopted under EO 12092, which treats the Council as still existing. No held source fixes when the Council ceased, so it is not established that both offices had ceased before 1982-08-17. Even if both had ceased, the Energy Coordinating Committee continued under EO 12083 with its other members, the added entries remained text of section 1-102, and under the ruling the end is the instrument that revokes the amended order, EO 12379. Disclosed alternative reading: if a reviewer holds that an order not named by number is not ended by the revocation of its amended parent, no first end is shown in the held sources.

Before: section 1-102 includes members (x) and (y) added by EO 12121. After: the same members plus (z). Neither EO 12148 nor EO 12156 removes or alters the two entries added by EO 12121. The clause continues, amended, until EO 12083 is revoked.

research_rationale:
EO 12132 (Creating an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of its employees), signed 1979-05-08. The order creates an emergency board under Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for a dispute between the National Railway Labor Conference and certain employees represented by the American Train Dispatchers Association; Section 1-101 establishes a board of three members. First end: Section 4 of EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17, Termination of Boards, Committees, and Commissions) names this order by number, "Executive Order No. 12132," and provides that it is revoked. EO 12379 has no effective-date clause, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1982-08-17. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 12162 (signed 1979-09-28, 44 FR 56665) amends EO 12140 (delegation to Governors of motor gasoline end-user allocation authority) by deleting the first sentence of its Sec. 1-105; EO 12140's Sec. 1-105 began with the words "This O rder shall term inate, unless extended, at midnight on" (September 30, 1979), so the amendment removed that sunset. The amending words are "hereby amended by deleting the first sentence in Sec. 1-105." (preceded in the held text by 'Executive Order No. 12140 is'). First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25): "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the entry at offset 26770 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "12162", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986". The held EO 12553 text prints this part of the table (PDF page 14) as a number-only column followed by a separate subject column: the number 12162 is the 21st entry of the column and pairs by position with the 21st subject, "Continuing the delegation of authorities relating to motor gasoline end-user allocation" (offset 28535), consistent with this order's subject; the parent order EO 12140 is also listed in the table (its subject precedes at the 18th position).

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 12182 of December 14, 1979
Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute  
Between the Long Island Rail Road and Certain of its Em­
ployees
A dispute exists between The Long Island Rail Road and certain of its 
employees represented by Participating Labor Organizations designated in list 
attached hereto and made a part hereof.
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the 
Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
This dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens 
substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a 
section of the country of essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 10 of the 
Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it is hereby ordered as 
follows:
1-101. Establishm ent o f Board. There is established a board of three members 
to be appointed by the President to investigate this dispute. No member of the 
board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of 
railroad employees or any carrier.
1-102. Report. The board shall report its finding to the President with respect 
to the dispute within 30 days from the date of this Order.
1-103. M aintaining Conditions. As provided by Section 10 of the Railway 
Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for 30 days after the board has 
made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by The Long Island Rail Road, or by its employees, in the conditions out 
of which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12187, whose subject line describes providing for the base production control level for marginal properties. Sections 1-101 to 1-103 set, for pricing regulations under the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 and for months commencing after December 31, 1979, the base production control level for marginal properties at 20 percent of the old crude oil produced and sold from the property in 1978 (divided by 365 and multiplied by the days in the month), define marginal properties by the crude oil pricing regulations, and let the Secretary of Energy adopt conforming regulations. Executive Order 12209 of April 16, 1980 restated the order to read as follows (before: the 20 percent level applied to months commencing after December 31, 1979; after: it applies only to the months of January, February and March 1980); under owner ruling 2026-10-21 that is a strike-and-insert rewrite, the clause continues, amended, and the substance changed. Fixed period of the restated section 1-101: Executive Order 12209, signed April 16, 1980, makes section 1-101 apply only with respect to the months of January, February and March 1980, and says it was issued to permit the conversion to new oil status of all old oil production from marginal oil wells effective April 1, 1980. That fixed period ended on March 31, 1980 (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins), before the restatement was signed, so the pricing rule has no application to any later month and the order was functionally spent as to that rule on March 31, 1980. The restatement itself took effect on signing, April 16, 1980 (no effective date is stated). This own-terms period is a disclosed earlier candidate end and is not adopted as the first end: the restatement leaves section 1-102 (the definition of marginal properties) and section 1-103 (the Secretary of Energy's power to adopt conforming regulations) in force without any date, the restated section 1-101 still fixes the base production control level for the covered months, and under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert rewrites the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends, which here is the express revocation by Executive Order 12553. Whether the authority of the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 lapsed before 1986 is not established from held sources (the statute text is not held), and such a lapse would be an unnamed instrument and a disclosed candidate only. Executive Order 12287 of January 28, 1981 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12287.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) exempted all crude oil and refined petroleum products from the price and allocation controls adopted under that Act without naming this order; it is likewise a disclosed candidate earlier end and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. No earlier express end was found.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12187 (45 FR 3, Federal Register of January 2, 1980; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Base Production Control Level for Marginal Properties and signed December 29, 1979. It sets the base production control level for marginal oil properties. Inventory: three numbered sections (1-101 to 1-103), recorded as one whole clause; the dossier inventory matches the full held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12187, whose subject line describes providing for the base production control level for marginal properties. Executive Order 12209 (1980-04-16) restated the order and is a later event, not an end. Fixed period of the restated section 1-101: Executive Order 12209, signed April 16, 1980, makes section 1-101 apply only with respect to the months of January, February and March 1980, and says it was issued to permit the conversion to new oil status of all old oil production from marginal oil wells effective April 1, 1980. That fixed period ended on March 31, 1980 (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins), before the restatement was signed, so the pricing rule has no application to any later month and the order was functionally spent as to that rule on March 31, 1980. The restatement itself took effect on signing, April 16, 1980 (no effective date is stated). This own-terms period is a disclosed earlier candidate end and is not adopted as the first end: the restatement leaves section 1-102 (the definition of marginal properties) and section 1-103 (the Secretary of Energy's power to adopt conforming regulations) in force without any date, the restated section 1-101 still fixes the base production control level for the covered months, and under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert rewrites the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends, which here is the express revocation by Executive Order 12553.  The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found citations of this number outside its own printings only in the printings of EO 12209. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 12189 (signed 1980-01-16, 45 FR 3559) amends EO 12153, as amended by EO 12186, to read as a restated section 1-101 to 1-104 exempting first sales of heavy crude oil from price controls under the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973, with two definitions of 'heavy crude oil' (one for August 17 through December 20, 1979 and one from December 21, 1979 'and thereafter') and an authority for the Secretary of Energy to adopt regulations. The restated text includes the words "1-103. Effective D ecem ber 21,1 9 7 9  and thereafter," so the clause has no own-terms end; the dated window in the earlier definition ended on December 20, 1979, before the order was signed, and does not end the exemption. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25): "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the entry at offset 26794 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "12189", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986". The held EO 12553 text prints this part of the table (PDF page 14) as a number-only column followed by a separate subject column: the number 12189 is the 25th entry and pairs with the 25th subject, "Relating to the definition of heavy oil" (offset 28862), consistent with this order's subject. An independent AI-reviewed ACT record for the same pair is carried in the dossier and agrees.

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of 
the United States of A m erica, including the Em ergency Petroleum A llocation 
A ct of 1973, as am ended (15 U.S.C. 751 e t  s e q.), and in order to provide that 
certain oil is exem pt from price controls on and after August 17,1979, and that 
other oil is exem pt on and after D ecem ber 21, 1979, it is hereby ordered that 
Executive O rder No. 12153 of August 17,1979, as am ended by Executive O rder 
No. 12186 of D ecem ber 21,1979, is am ended to read as follow s:
“1-101. Prices charged in the first sale o f heavy crude oil are exem pted from 
price controls adopted pursuant to the Em érgency Petroleum A llocation A ct o f 
1973, as amended. This exem ption shall only apply to heavy crude oil as it is 
defined, and for the time period to w hich the definition is applicable, as set 
forth in this O rder.”.
“1-102. Effective August 1 7 ,1 9 7 9  through D ecem ber 20,1979, ‘heavy crude oil’ 
m eans all crude oil produced from a property, but only if, during the last 
month prior to July 1979 in w hich crude oil w as produced and sold from that 
property, such crude oil had a w eighted average gravity o f 16.0° API or less, 
corrected to 60° Fahrenheit.”.
"1-103. Effective D ecem ber 21,1 9 7 9  and thereafter, ‘heavy crude oil’ m eans all 
crude oil produced from a property, but only if, during the last month prior to 
July 1979 in w hich crude oil w as produced and sold from that property, such 
crude oil had a w eighted average gravity of 20.0° API or less, corrected to 60° 
Fahrenheit.”.
"1-104. The Secretary  of Energy may, pursuant to Executive O rder No. 11790, 
as am ended by Executive O rder No. 12038, adopt such regulations as he 
deem s necessary  to im plement this O rder.”.

Executive Order 12207 of April 12, 1980
Creating an Emergency Board to Investigate a Dispute  
Between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and  
Certain of its Employees
A  dispute ex ists betw een the Port Authority Trans-H udson Corporation and 
certain o f its em ployees represented by the Brotherhood of R ailw ay Carm en of 
the United States and C anada.
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the 
R ailw ay Labor Act, as amended; and
The dispute, in the judgment o f the N ational M ediation Board, threatens 
substantially to interrupt interstate com m erce to a degree such as to deprive a 
section of the country o f essen tial transportation service:
NOW , TH EREFO RE, by the authority vested in me by Section 10 o f the 
R ailw ay Labor A ct, a s am ended (45 U.S.C. 160), it is hereby ordered as 
follow s:
1-101. E s ta b lis h m e n t o f  B o a rd . There is established a board o f three m em bers 
to be appointed by the President to investigate this dispute. No m em ber o f the 
board shall be pecuniarily or otherw ise interested in any organization o f 
railroad em ployees or any carrier.
1-102. R ep o rt. The board shall report its finding to the President with respect 
to the dispute within 30 days from the date of this Order.
1-103. M a in ta in in g  C o n d itio n s. A s provided by Section 10 o f the R ailw ay 
Labor A ct, as amended, from this date and for 30 days after the board has 
m ade its report to the President, no change, except by agreem ent, shall be 
made by the Port Authority Trans-H udson Corporation, or by its em ployees, in 
the conditions out of w hich the dispute arose.

EO 12207 (Creating an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and certain of its employees), signed 1980-04-12. The order creates an emergency board under Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for a dispute between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and certain employees; Section 1-101 establishes a board of three members. First end: Section 8 of EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17, Termination of Boards, Committees, and Commissions) names this order by number, "Executive Order No. 12207," and provides that it is revoked. EO 12379 has no effective-date clause, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1982-08-17. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole operative paragraph amends Executive Order 12187 so that section 1-101 sets the base production control level for marginal properties for the months January to March 1980, section 1-102 defines marginal properties by reference to the crude oil pricing regulations, and section 1-103 lets the Secretary of Energy conform those regulations; the order has no sunset or effective-date wording of its own. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 orders that the listed Executive Orders, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and lists the number 12209 in the No. column of its revocation table (offset 26806 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt). This is an express revocation that names this order. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the first-end date is its signing date, 1986-02-25; that is a reading of the text, not express wording, and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and filing date 1986-02-26 are not effective dates. Earlier candidates that do not name EO 12209 (the period of section 1-101 ending 1980-03-31, EO 12287 of 1981-01-28, the believed 1981-09-30 lapse of the statutory authority) are disclosed but not adopted, because none names this order or is shown to have extinguished its sections.

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of 
the United States o f Am erica, including the Em ergency Petroleum A llocation 
A ct of 1973, as am ended (15 U.S.C. 751 e t  s e q .) , and notw ithstanding the 
delegations to the Secretary of Energy in Executive O rder No. 11790, as 
am ended by Executive Order No. 12038, and in order to permit the conversion 
to new  oil status o f all old oil production from m arginal oil w ells effective 
April 1,1980, it is hereby ordered that Executive O rder No. 12187 of D ecem ber 
29,1979, is am ended to read as follow s:
“1-101. For purposes o f the pricing regulations adopted pursuant to the 
Em ergency Petroleum A llocation A ct of 1973, w ith respect to the m onths of 
January, February and M arch 1980, the b ase production control level for 
marginal properties shall equal 20 percent of the total num ber of barrels of old 
crude oil produced and sold from the property concerned during calendar year 
1978, divided by 365, multiplied by the num ber of days during the month in 
1978 w hich corresponds to the months concerned.”
“1-102. For purposes of this Order, the term “m arginal properties” has the 
sam e meaning as that term under the crude oil pricing regulations adopted 
pursuant to the Em ergency Petroleum A llocation A ct of 1973, as am ended.”
“1-103. The Secretary of Energy may, pursuant to Executive Order No. 11790, 
as am ended by Executive Order No. 12038, adopt such regulations as he 
deems n ecessary  or appropriate to conform the crude oil pricing regulations to 
this Order.”.

research_rationale:
EO 12209 (signed 1980-04-16; 45 FR 26311) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12209.txt. It is a single amending paragraph that restates sections 1-101 to 1-103 of Executive Order 12187. The dossier evidence ACT:EO:12209>EO:12553 (an agent-located, independently reviewed provision) was re-read against the held EO 12553 text, whose revocation table lists the number 12209. The LOOKUPS number-citation search of the held order texts finds no order other than EO 12553 that names EO 12209. The machine searches (U.S. Code 0 hits, eCFR 0 hits, Federal Register catalog 2 hits that are EO 12553 and EO 12919) were read: EO 12919 only amends EO 11790 and does not name EO 12209. EO 12287 (1981-01-28), read in the held Federal Register text, decontrols crude oil and petroleum products without naming EO 12187 or EO 12209. Under the owner rulings of 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments) and 2026-10-28 (an endpoint needs a reason), the end is the instrument that names this order, EO 12553, and the unnamed candidates are disclosed. Original not yet confirmed as an authenticated official copy; the held text is the machine text layer of the official Federal Register PDF.

(2) Executive Order 12287 exempts all crude oil and refined petroleum products from the price and allocation controls but names neither EO 12187 nor EO 12209 and its section 3 authorizes entitlements actions for periods prior to it, so it does not extinguish this order. (3) The Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act authority is believed to have lapsed on 1981-09-30, but the statute is not held and the lapse is not express. (4) EO 12919 of 1994 amends EO 11790 only. No instrument naming EO 12209 is held other than EO 12553.","independent_command_check":"Sections 1-101, 1-102 and 1-103 are components of one amendment to EO 12187 and all end together on revocation. The recital of purpose (conversion to new oil status effective April 1, 1980) is not a separate command.","savings_check":"Read for savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause in its enacting sentence. The effects on pricing for January to March 1980 and the conversion of old oil to new oil status are accrued; nothing continues as a command.","scope_check":"The whole order is one amending paragraph with three restated sections (1-101 base production control level for January to March 1980, 1-102 definition of marginal properties, 1-103 regulation-conforming authority). No partial revocation, suspension or amendment of any of them is held; EO 12553 revokes the whole order."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order converted old oil from marginal oil wells to new oil status effective April 1, 1980 and fixed the base production control level for January to March 1980; those pricing consequences for past periods are accrued effects. EO 12287 section 3 itself contemplates actions for periods prior to its date. The order creates no continuing duty after revocation, and no held source shows an independent command that survives.

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of 
the United States, including Section 203 of the International Emergency Eco­
nomic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1702), Section 301 of Title 3 of the United States 
Code, Section 1732 of Title 22 of the United States Code, and Section 301 of the 
National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1631), in view  of thé continuing unusual 
and extraordinary threat to the national security, foreign policy and economy 
of the United States upon which w ere based the declarations of national 
emergency in Executive O rder No. 12170, issued November 14, 1979, and in 
Executive O rder No. 12211, issued April 17,1980, in light of the agreem ent w ith 
the Government of Iran, as reflected in the Declarations of the Government of 
the Democratic and Popular Republic of Algeria dated January 19, 1981, 
relating to the release of United States diplom ats and nationals being held as 
hostages and to the resolution of claims of United States nationals against 
Iran, in order to implement Article II of the D eclaration of Algeria concerning 
the settlem ent of claims and to begin the process of norm alization of relations 
betw een the United States and Iran, it is hereby ordered that as of the 
effective date of this Order:
Section 1. All claims which m ay be presented to the Iran-United States Claims 
Tribunal under the term s of Article II of the D eclaration of the Government of 
the Democratic and Popular Republic of Algeria Concerning the Settlem ent of 
Claims by the Government of the U nited States of Am erica and the Govern­
m ent of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and all claims for equitable or other 
judicial relief in connection w ith such claims, are hereby suspended, except as 
they m ay be presented to the Tribunal. During the period of this suspension, 
all such 1 'claims shall have no legal effect in any action now  pending in any 
court of the United States, including the courts of any state or any locality 
thereof, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, or in any action commenced 
in any such court after the effective date of this Order. Nothing in this action 
precludes the commencement of an action after the effective date of this O rder 
for the purpose of tolling the period of limitations for commencement of such 
action.
Section 2. Nothing in this O rder shall require dism issal of any action for w ant 
of prosecution.
Section 3. Suspension under this O rder of a claim or a portion thereof 
subm itted to the Iran-United States Claims Tribunal for adjudication shall 
term inate upon a determ ination by the Tribunal that it does not have jurisdic­
tion over such claim or such portion thereof.
Section 4. A determ ination by the Iran-United States Claims Tribunal on the 
merits that a claim ant is not entitled to recover on a claim shall operate as a 
final resolution and discharge of the claim for all purposes. A determ ination 
by the Tribunal that a claim ant shall have recovery on a claim in a specified 
am ount shall operate as a final resolution and discharge of the claim for all 
purposes upon paym ent to the claim ant of the full am ount of the aw ard, 
including any interest aw arded by the Tribunal.
Section 5. Nothing in this O rder shall apply to any claim concerning the 
validity or paym ent of a standby letter of credit, perform ance or paym ent 
bond or other sim ilar instrum ent.

1-102. The President shall designate a Chairman from among the members.  
1-2. F u n c tio n s .
1-201. The Commission shall study and analyze, and make recommendations  
to the President on, the question whether the United States should provide  
financial compensation to United States nationals who have been held in  
captivity outside the United States, either (1) by or with the approval of a  
foreign government, or (2) by reason of their status as employees of the United  
States Government or as dependents of such employees.
1— 202. The Commission shall submit a report to the President ninety days after  
the date of this Order. The report shall contain the Commission’s recommen­
dations as to whether legislation to deal with the foregoing com pensation  
issue is appropriate and, if so, as to w hat such legislation should provide. The  
report shall specifically contain the Commission’s recommendations concern­
ing the compensation of United States nationals held hostage in Iran on and  
after November 4,1979.
1-203. In analyzing the foregoing issues the Commission shall consider all  
factors which it m ay consider relevant, including the prior practice with  
respect to governmental compensation, both by the United States Government  
and by foreign governments, of persons held in captivity abroad.
1-204. In the performance of its functions the Commission shall specifically  
address the following issues:
(a) whether any legislation authorizing compensation should set forth specific  
legislative standards, or whether the standards by which to aw ard com pensa­
tion should be administratively developed;
(b) whether any standards developed either legislatively or administratively  
should be applied uniformly to civilian and military government employees,  
dependents of such employees, and private citizens, or whether separate  
criteria should be developed for these or other categories;
(c) whether an existing administrative body should determine amounts of  
compensation, or whether a new body should be established for this purpose;  
and
(d) whether compensation should be paid for injuries suffered by members of  
families of persons who have been held in captivity.
1-3. A d m in is t r a t iv e  P r o v is io n s .

reviews, and inquiries as m ay be necessary. In addition to conducting open  
meetings in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act, the Com-

such information that m ay be deemed necessary to carry out its functions

research_rationale:
EO 12285 (President's Commission on Hostage Compensation), signed 1981-01-19. The order establishes the President's Commission on Hostage Compensation (Section 1-101), sets its study and report functions (1-201 to 1-204), its procedures and support (1-301 to 1-304) and general provisions (1-401, 1-402). Section 1-402 provides that the Commission shall terminate thirty days after submitting its report, which is report-relative and not a dated end. EO 12307 and EO 12317 later moved the report date, and EO 12294 Section 8 ratified this order. First end: Section 21 of EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17, Termination of Boards, Committees, and Commissions) names this order by number, "Executive Order No. 12285," and provides that it is revoked. EO 12379 has no effective-date clause, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1982-08-17. The files filed under EO 11022, EO 11256 and EO 11829 matched only because they carry the same Federal Register pages as the EO 12379 revocation list; they are not separate instruments naming this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 1 establishes, effective July 10, 1982, a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 2 directs the board to report within 30 days from the date of its creation. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The board's report is dated August 19, 1982 (held report of Emergency Board No. 194; the time was extended from August 9 to August 19, 1982 with the President's approval on July 26, 1982), so the command was functionally spent on August 19, 1982; that date is stated here and not entered as a later event because no dossier evidence record covers the transmittal letter or the extension passage. No earlier express end was found.

The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 3 restates the section 10 status-quo period, from the date of creation of the board until 30 days after its report. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; it ran until thirty days after the report dated August 19, 1982, that is to about September 18, 1982 (a computed date, not shown in a source). No earlier express end was found.

section of the country of essential transportation service.

this dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise  
interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.

to the dispute within 30 days from the date of its creation.

and for 30 days after the board has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be made by the carriers or by their  
employees, in the conditions out of which the dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12370 (47 FR 30047, Federal Register of July 12, 1982; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Certain Railroads Represented by the National Carriers’ Conference Committee of the National Railway Labor Conference and signed July 8, 1982. It creates a board to investigate the dispute between the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and certain railroads represented by the National Carriers’ Conference Committee of the National Railway Labor Conference. Inventory: the order is a board order whose operative commands are 3 clause(s) as recorded in the dossier (sec1; sec2; sec3). The list of parties attached to the order identifies the dispute and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C): the report date and the end of any statutory standstill are spent facts that do not end the order; the held report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_12370_Report_of_Presidential_Emergency_Board_No._194_created_by_EO_12370_effective_July_10__6dbdcaaa92.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) shows that the board's report and recommendations were submitted to the President by a letter of transmittal dated August 19, 1982 (the cover is also dated August 19, 1982), after the President approved on July 26, 1982 an extension of the time for the report from August 9, 1982 to August 19, 1982. The board therefore made its report on August 19, 1982, the report command was functionally spent on that date, and the thirty-day period after the report ran to about September 18, 1982 (a computed date, thirty days after the transmittal date, not a date shown in the source). These dates are stated here and not entered as later events because no dossier evidence record covers the transmittal letter or the extension passage (the dossier's records from that file quote other passages of the report). The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found citations of this number outside its own printings only in an emergency-board report held under jobs/source-ladder. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12373 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The three numbered paragraphs (1-101 to 1-103) establish a three-member board effective immediately under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, direct it to report within 30 days from the date of its establishment, and restate the section 10 status-quo period from creation until 30 days after the report. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; when it ran out depends on the unrecorded report date. No earlier express end was found.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 12373 of July 21, 1982
Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute  
Between The United Transportation Union and Certain Rail­
roads Represented by the National Carriers' Conference Com­
m ittee of the National Railway Labor Conference
A dispute exists between the United Transportation Union and certain rail­
roads represented by the National Carriers’  Conference Committee of the  
National Railway Labor Conference designated on the list attached hereto and  
made a part hereof.
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
This dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens  
substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a  
section of the country of essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 10 of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C.§160), it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1-101. E stablish m en t o f Board. There is established, effective immediately, a  
board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this  
dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested  
in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
1-102. R eport. The board' shall report its finding to the President with respect  
to the dispute within 30 days from the date of its establishment.
1-103. M aintaining Conditions.  As provided by Section 10 of the Railway  
Labor Act, as amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board  
and for 30 days after the board has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be made by the carriers or by their  
employees, in the conditions out of which the dispute arose.

dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested  
in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
1-102. R eport. The board' shall report its finding to the President with respect  
to the dispute within 30 days from the date of its establishment.
1-103. M aintaining Conditions.  As provided by Section 10 of the Railway  
Labor Act, as amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board  
and for 30 days after the board has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be made by the carriers or by their  
employees, in the conditions out of which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12376, whose subject line describes increasing membership on the Presidential Commission on Drunk Driving. The single sentence amends the second sentence of section 1 of Executive Order 12358 of April 14, 1982 so that the Commission is composed of no more than 28 members appointed by the President (an increase of two). The amendment became part of the text of the parent order; the table of Executive Order 12553 lists this order by number and subject, so the revocation reaches it expressly, and no source shows the amendment being undone earlier. Executive Order 12415 of April 5, 1983 amended only section 4(b) of the parent order (the Commission’s termination date), not the membership sentence; it is a source note and not an end. The parent Commission's own termination date is a disclosed earlier candidate and not the first end: Executive Order 12415 of April 5, 1983 (48 FR 15117) amended section 4(b) of Executive Order No. 12358, as amended, to provide that the Commission shall terminate on December 31, 1983, and no held instrument extends it, so the Commission, and with it the membership ceiling this order set, had no operation after December 31, 1983 (functionally spent on that date on the inclusive reading). That instrument does not name Executive Order 12376, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments it is not an end; this order remained on the books until Executive Order 12553 revoked it by number. No earlier express end was found.

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution of the United  
States of America, and in order to increase the membership of the Presidential  
Commission on Drunk Driving by two, it is hereby ordered that the second  
sentence of Section 1 of Executive Order No. 12358 of April 14, 1982, is  
amended to read as follows: “The Commission shall be composed of no more  
than 28 members appointed by the President.”.

DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE
Agricultural Marketing Service
7 CFR Part 907
[Navel Orange Reg. 573]
Navel Oranges Grown in Arizona and  
Designated Part of California;  
Limitation of Handling
AGENCY: Agricultural Marketing Service, 
USDA.
ACTION: Final rule.
SUMMARY: This regulation establishes 
the quantity of fresh Califomia-Arizona 
navel oranges that may be shipped to 
market during the period April 8-ApriI
14,1983. Such action is needed to 
provide for orderly marketing of fresh 
navel oranges for this period due to the 
marketing situation confronting the 
orange industry.
EFFECTIVE DATE: April 8,1983.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: 
William J. Doyle^ 202-447-5975.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Findings
This rule has been reviewed under 
USDA procedures and Executive Order 
12291 and has been designated a “non- 
major” rule. William T. Manley, Deputy 
Administrator, Agricultural Marketing 
Service, has certified that this action 
will not have a significant economic 
impact on a substantial number of small 
entities. This action is designed to 
promote orderly marketing of the 
Califomia-Arizona navel orange crop for 
the benefit of producers and will not 
substantially affect costs for the directly 
regulated handlers.
This regulation is issued under the 
marketing agreement, as amended, and 
Order No. 907, as amended (7 CFR Part 
907), regulating the handling of navel
oranges grown in Arizona and 
designated part of California. The 
agreement and order are effective under 
the Agricultural Marketing Agreement 
Act of 1937, as amended (7 U.S.C. 601- 
674). The action is based upon the 
recommendation and information 
submitted by the Navel Orange 
Administrative Committee and upon 
other available information. It is hereby 
iound that this action will tend to 
effectuate the declared policy of the Act.
This action is consistent with the 
marketing policy for 1982-83. The 
marketing policy was recommended by 
the committee following discussion at a 
public meeting on September 21,1982. 
The committee met again publicly on 
April 4,1983 at Bakersfield, California, 
to consider the current and prospective 
conditions of supply and demand and 
recommended a quantity of navel 
oranges deemed advisable to be 
handled during the specified week. The 
committee reports the demand for navel 
oranges is slower.
It is further found that it is 
impracticable and contrary to the public 
interest to give preliminary notice, 
engage in public rulemaking, and 
postpone the effective date until 30 days 
after publication in the Federal Register 
(5 U.S.C. 553), because of insufficient 
time between the date when information 
became available upon which this 
regulation is based and the effective 
date necessary to effectuate the 
declared policy of the Act. Interested 
persons were given an opportunity to 
submit information and views on the 
regulation at an open meeting. It is 
necessary to effectuate the declared 
policy of the Act to make this regulatory 
provision effective as specified, and 
handlers have been apprised of such 
provisions and the effective time.
List of subjects in 7 CFR 907: 
Agricultural Marketing Service, 
Marketing Agreements and Orders, 
California, Arizona, Oranges (Navel).
1. Section 907.873 is added as follows:
§ 907.873 Navel orange regulation 573.
The quantities of navel oranges grown 
in California and Arizona which may be 
handled dining the period April 8,1983 
through April 14,1983, are established 
as follows:
(1) District 1:1,700,000 cartons;
(2) District 2: Unlimited cartons;
(3) District 3: Unlimited cartons;
(4) District 4: Unlimited cartons.
(Secs. 1-19, 48 Stat. 31, as amended; 7 U.S.C.  
601-674)

Grown in California; Nomination of  
Pear Commodity Committee Members
a g e n c y: Agricultural Marketing Service, 
USDA.
‘ACTION: Final rule.
s u m m a r y: This action reallocates the 
membership on the Pear Commodity 
Committee and re-groups districts (for 
purposes of representation) within the 
production area. The changes reflect the 
relative quantity of pears shipped from 
the respective representation areas.
d a t e : This rule becomes effective April
7,1983.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: 
William J. Doyle, Chief, Fruit Branch, 
F&V, AMS, USDA, Washington, D.C. 
20250, telephone 202-447-5975.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: This 
final rule has been reviewed under 
Secretary’s Memorandum 1512-1 and 
Executive Order 12291 and has been 
designated a “non-major” rule. William
T. Manley, Deputy Administrator, 
Agricultural Marketing Service, has 
certified that this action will not have a 
significant economic impact on a 
substantial number of small entities. 
This action is designed to promote 
orderly marketing of fresh California 
pears for the benefit of producers, and 
will not substantially affect costs for the 
directly regulated handlers.
This final rule is issued under 
Marketing Order No. 917, regulating the 
handling of fresh pears, plums, and 
peaches grown in California. The order 
is effective under the Agricultural 
Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, as 
amended (7 U.S.C. 601-674). The action 
is based upon the recommendation and 
information submitted by the Pear 
Commodity Committee, and upon other 
available information. It is hereby found 
that this action will tend to effectuate 
the declared policy of the Act.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12384 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The five numbered paragraphs (1-101 to 1-105) establish, effective October 1, 1982, a three-member board under section 510 of the Rail Passenger Service Act (45 U.S.C. 590), subject to the availability of funds, and direct a public hearing, an initial report within 30 days after creation, the submission of final offers if the dispute is not settled within ten days after the report, and a final report within 15 days after the final offers. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. No earlier express end was found.

Title 3— Executive Order 12384 of October 1, 1982
The President Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute  
Between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Au­
thority and the Delaware Transportation. Authority, and  
Certain Labor Organizations
A dispute exists between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Au­
thority (SEPTA) and the Delaware Transportation Authority (DTA), and  
certain labor organizations, designated on the list attached hereto and made a  
part hereof, representing those employees of the Consolidated Rail Corpora­
tion (Conrail) who are to be transferred to the SEPTA and DTA as part of the  
transfer of commuter fail service responsibility from Conrail to the SEPTA and  
DTA, pursuant to Section 1145 of the Northeast Rail Service Act of 1981.
The dispute concerns the terms and conditions of new collective bargaining  
agreements, which were required to be negotiated by September 1, 1982, by  
Section 510(a) of the Rail Passenger Service Act, as amended (“the Act”). As  
of this date, the parties have not entered into new collective bargaining  
agreements, and the SEPTA, the Northeast Commuter Services Corporation,  
and the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers have requested the President to  
establish an emergency board pursuant to Section 510(b) of the Act.
Section 510(c) of the Act provides for the President, upon request of a party, to  
appoint an emergency board to investigate such dispute and to make a report  
and recommendation for settlement.
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 510 of the Rail  
Passenger Service Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. § 590), it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1-101. E sta b lish m en t o f  B oard. There is established, effective October 1,1982,  
a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this  
dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any commuter authority providing  
commuter rail service. The Board shall perform its functions subject to the  
availability of funds.
1-102. P u b lic H ea rin g. The board shall conduct a public hearing on the dispute  
at which each party shall appear and provide testimony.
1-103. In itia l R eport. The board shall report on the dispute within 30 days 
after the date of its creation.
1-104. F in a l O ffers. If the parties have not settled the dispute within ten days  
after the board’s report, the board shall require the parties to submit, within  
five days, their final offers for settlement of the dispute.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12385 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The five numbered paragraphs (1-101 to 1-105) establish, effective October 1, 1982, a three-member board under section 510 of the Rail Passenger Service Act (45 U.S.C. 590), subject to the availability of funds, and direct a public hearing, an initial report within 30 days after creation, the submission of final offers if the dispute is not settled within ten days after the report, and a final report within 15 days after the final offers. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. No earlier express end was found.

pursuant to Section 1145 o f the N ortheast R ail Service A ct of 1981.
The dispute concerns the terms and conditions of new collective bargaining  
agreements, which were required to be negotiated by September 1, 1982, by  
Section 510(a) of the Rail Passenger Service Act, as amended (“the Act”). As  
of this date, the parties have not entered into new collective bargaining  
agreements, and the N JTRO and the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers  
have requested the President to establish an emergency board pursuant to  
Section 510(b) of the Act.
Section 510(c) of the Act provides for the President, upon request of a party, to  
appoint an emergency board to investigate such dispute and to make a report  
and recommendation for settlement.
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 510 of the Rail  
Passenger Service Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. § 590), it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1-101. E sta b lish m en t o f  B oard. There is established, effective October 1, 1982,  
a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this  
dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any 
organization of railroad employees or any commuter authority, providing  
commuter rail service. The Board shall perform its functions subject to the  
availability of funds.
1-102. P u b lic H ea rin g. The board shall conduct a public hearing on the dispute 
at w hich each party shall appear and provide testim ony.
1-103. In itia l R eport. The board shall report on the dispute within 30 days  
after the date of its creation.
1-104. F in a l O ffers. If the parties have not settled the dispute within ten days  
after the board’s report, the board shall require the parties to submit, within  
five days, their final offers for settlement of the dispute.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12386 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The five numbered paragraphs (1-101 to 1-105) establish, effective October 1, 1982, a three-member board under section 510 of the Rail Passenger Service Act (45 U.S.C. 590), subject to the availability of funds, and direct a public hearing, an initial report within 30 days after creation, the submission of final offers if the dispute is not settled within ten days after the report, and a final report within 15 days after the final offers. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. No earlier express end was found.

Executive Order 12386 of October 1, 1982
Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute  
Between the New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority  
and the Connecticut Department of Transportation, and Certain  
Labor Organizations
A dispute exists between the New York Metropolitan Transportation Authori­
ty (MTA) and the Connecticut Department of Transportation (CDOT), and  
certain labor organizations, designated on the list attached hereto and made a  
part hereof, representing those employees of the Consolidated Rail Corpora­
tion (Conrail) who are to be transferred to the MTA and CDOT as part of the  
transfer of commuter rail service responsibility from Conrail to the MTA and  
CDOT, pursuant to Section 1145 of the Northeast Rail Service Act of 1981.
The dispute concerns the terms and conditions of new collective bargaining  
agreements, which were required to be negotiated by September 1, 1982, b jy  
Section 510(a) of the Rail Passenger Service Act, as amended (“the Act”). As  
of this date, the parties have not entered into new collective bargaining  
agreements, and the MTA and the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers have  
requested the President to establish an emergency board pursuant to Section  
510(b) of the Act.
Section 510(c) of the Act provides for the President, upon request of a party, to  
appoint an emergency board to investigate such dispute and to make a report  
and recommendation for settlement.
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 510 of the Rail  
Passenger Service Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. § 590), it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1-101. Establishm ent o f Board. There is established, effective October 1,1982,  
a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate this  
dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any commuter authority providing  
commuter rail service. The Board shall perform its functions subject to the  
availability of funds.
1-102. Public H earing. The board shall conduct a public hearing on the dispute  
at which each party shall appear and provide testimony.
1-103. Initial Report.  The board shall report on the dispute within 30 days  
after the date of its creation.
1-104. Final O ffers. If the parties have not settled the dispute within ten days  
after the board’s report, the board shall require, the parties to submit, within  
five days, their final offers for settlement of the dispute.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12393 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The four numbered paragraphs (1-101 to 1-104) establish, effective November 16, 1982, a three-member board under section 9A of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 159a), direct a report within 30 days after creation, restate the section 9A(c) status-quo period of 120 days after creation, and provide that the board terminates ninety days after the report. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; paragraph 1-103 measures it from the creation of the board, effective November 16, 1982, for 120 days thereafter, so by the order's own terms it ran out on March 16, 1983 (a computed date, 120 days after November 16, 1982), whatever the report date was. This clause provides that the board terminates on or after the submission of its report. The report date is not held in this packet’s citable evidence, and the clause is read as a report-relative sunset that is functionally spent on the report date and not as the end, by analogy to owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C), which that ruling applies to report-relative sunsets of other boards; this analogy is a reading disclosed for the reviewer. No earlier express end was found.

Title 3— Executive Order 12393 of November 16, 1982
The Presid en t Establishing an  E m erg en cy  B o ard  T o In vestigate a  D ispute  
B etw een  T he Long Island R ail R o ad  an d  C ertain  L ab or O rga­
nizations
A dispute exists between The Long Island Rail Road and certain labor  
organizations, designated on the list attached hereto and made a part hereof,  
representing employees of The Long Island Rail Road.
The dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (“the Act”).
The New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the parent body of The  
Long Island Rail Road, has requested that the President establish an emergen­
cy board pursuant to Section 9A of the Act.
Section 9A(c) of the Act provides that the President, upon request of a party,  
shall appoint an emergency board to investigate and report on the dispute.
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 9A of the Act,  
as amended (45 U.S.C. § 159a), it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-101. Establishm ent o f Board.  There is established, effective November 16,  
1982, a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate  
this dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any carrier. The board shall perform its  
functions subject to the availability of funds.
1-102. Report. The board shall report its findings to the President with respect  
to the dispute within 30 days after the date of its creation.
1-103. M aintaining Conditions.  As provided by Section 9A(c) of the Act, as  
amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board, and for 120  
days thereafter, no change, except by agreement of the parties, shall be made  
by the carrier or the employees, in the conditions out of which the dispute  
arose.
1-104. Expiration.  The Emergency Board shall terminate ninety (90) days after  
the submission of the report provided for in paragraph 1-102 of this Order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The lead clause recites the authority, including the Federal Advisory Committee Act, states the purpose to increase the membership and extend the life of the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government, and directs that Executive Order 12369 be amended as follows; it is the instruction that carries subsections (a) and (b). Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 orders that the listed Executive Orders, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and lists the number 12398 in the No. column of its revocation table (offset 26972 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt). This is an express revocation that names this order. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the first-end date is its signing date, 1986-02-25; that is a reading of the text, not express wording, and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and filing date 1986-02-26 are not effective dates. EO 12534 (signed 1985-09-30; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt, sha256 2f7a5c13126573ec9fb7f10631df9e25cac3065f405355c469a0222363ab443c) revokes, in section 3(b), Executive Order No. 12369 establishing the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government, among orders that established committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed; its section 5 reads "Sec. 5 This Order shall be effective September 30,1985." It names the parent order (without the words as amended) but not this amending order, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments it is a disclosed earlier candidate end (1985-09-30), not the end.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Subsection (b) restates section 4(b) of EO 12369 so that, in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended, "the Committee shall terminate on June 30, 1983, unless" sooner extended. Later amendments of the same sentence are recorded as later events that change the date and do not end the clause: EO 12429 (signed 1983-06-28) restates it with October 30, 1983, EO 12447 (signed 1983-10-27) with December 31, 1983 and EO 12455 (signed 1983-12-29) with January 31, 1984, each as a rewrite of the whole sentence that changes its substance (the date) while the clause continues, amended, until the order ends. The last held sunset is 1984-01-31 ("unless sooner extended", EO 12455); no held source shows whether the Committee was extended again or the date on which it in fact ceased, although EO 12534 lists its establishing order among committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 orders that the listed Executive Orders, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and lists the number 12398 in the No. column of its revocation table (offset 26972 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt). This is an express revocation that names this order. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the first-end date is its signing date, 1986-02-25; that is a reading of the text, not express wording, and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and filing date 1986-02-26 are not effective dates.

later_events.mechanism: restatement of section 4(b) of EO 12369 by EO 12429 (signed 1983-06-28; 48 FR 30087, Federal Register of June 30, 1983; no effective-date wording, read as effective on signing), recorded as a later event and not an end under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments: section 4(b) of EO 12369, as amended, is further amended to read that the Committee shall terminate on October 30, 1983, unless sooner extended. Before: the sentence installed by EO 12398 reads that, in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended, the Committee shall terminate on June 30, 1983, unless sooner extended. After: the sentence reads that the Committee shall terminate on October 30, 1983, unless sooner extended. The rewrite replaces the whole sentence and changes its substance (the termination date); it also drops the words in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended.
